1.3 Reservoir Information

The primary target reservoir layer for the six wells in this Contract is Fahliyan, with a gross thickness of about 300 m. The Description of Reservoir is as below table.

Reservoir (Fahliyan)GOR 1500 SCF/STBH2S Content (ppm) 2000CO2 Content (ppm) 25,800Salinity (ppm as NaCl) 156,000Calcium Content (mg/lit) 5,600Temperature Gradient 1.3°F/100ft

Note: the relationship between temperature and depth is: Temperature (°F) = 0.013 * Depth (ftss) + 85.25

1.4 Program Outline

Well SPH-03 will be spudded as a producer well in the vicinity of the well SPH-01 (about 1000 meters away from the Well SPH-01). This Well will be penetrated finally into the Lower Khami Group including Gadvan sands and Lower Fahliyan carbonates with estimated depth of 4535 m (TD).

36" Hole section:

This hole would be drilled from surface to the depth of 104 m, inside the near top of Aghajari clastic/marly formation with mud weight of 67 to 68 pcf and this hole size is protected by 30" casing. The relevant casing shoe will be set at the depth of 104 m and then cemented up.

Well Drilling Program – SPH-03

Doc. No: SJD1-DDRGDP-DRDR-PLDR-3001-D03 Page 17 of 222

24" Hole section:

This hole would be penetrated into the Aghajari clastic/Marly formation with mud weight of 68 to 89 pcf. The hole would also penetrate into the Mishan Marly/Carbonate formation at the depth of 1402 m, and then will continue to the top of Gachsaran formation at the depth of 1439.74 m. In addition, during the drilling operation, the top most of Gachsaran formation will be also drilled to the depth of 1495 m (section TD). At the end of hole penetration, the required logs including CDR, GR for open hole will be run, after logging operation, the 18 5/8" casing will be run and cemented at 1495 m, 55m TVD below top of Gachsaran (Member 7) formation.

17" Hole Section:

Drilling this hole would be started from the upper part of Gachsaran formation with 110 to 137 pcf (Max mud weight based on SPH02 and SPH03 : 120pcf) mud weight and will continue into the entire members of Gachsaran formation (members 1 to 6). The related mud weight will be increased gradually to 137 pcf at the depth of 1928.5 m. At the end of hole penetration, the required wire line logs including CDR/GR,4 Arm CALI Logs will be run, after logging operation, the 13 3/8" x 13-5/8” casing would be run and set at the depth of 1928.5 m and then cemented up then CCL,GR,CBL, VDL for cased hole will be run as program.

The mentioned hole size encompasses the big interval of Gachsaran formation, including of gray marl, anhydrite, red marl, salt, limestone, argillaceous limestone and claystone.

12 1/4” Hole Section:

This hole would be drilled inside the Asmari formation with 75 to 86 pcf mud weight. The drilling operation will continue from Lower Asmari to basal part of Sarvak formation to the depth of 3727 m (TD), Mud weight would be adjusted and increased to 82 pcf based on hole condition. At the end of this hole drilling, the required logs including CDR and Full Set logs will be run, after logging operation, the 9 5/8" casing would be run and set at the depth of 3726 m (Casing Shoe) and then cemented up then CBL,VDL,CCL,GR,CAST or USIT for cased hole would be run.

The drilled lithology consists of mainly limestone, sandstone, gray marl, argillaceous limestone, red claystone, anhydrite, salt and dolostone, belong to the base of

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and

Production Operations Project

Well Drilling Program – SPH-03

Doc. No: SJD1-DDRGDP-DRDR-PLDR-3001-D03 Page 18 of 222

Gachsaran, Asmari, Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan and Sarvak formations.

8-1/2’’ Hole Section:

This hole would be started from the basal Sarvak formation (about 3726 m) and then penetrate into the Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan and Fahliyan formations respectively to target depth of 4535 m (TD). At the end of drilling operation, the required logs including CDR, Full Set Logs will be run. The 7” liner would be run and set at the depth of 4535 m (Liner Shoe) and then cemented up then CBL,VDL,CCL,GR,CAST or USIT for cased hole would be run and MTT Log will be run after perform perforation.

The mud weight would be started with 113 pcf and then gradually increases to 135 pcf, particularly within the Gadvan and Upper Fahliyan pressurized (clay rich) intervals.

The drilled lithology observed during operation consist of mainly limestone, sandstone, shale, chertified limestone, claystone, argillaceous limestone, belong to the Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan and Fahliyan.

Well Hole Section Problems

12-1/4" Gain and Calcium ion increase observed at 1792m, increase MW to 95 PCF

8-3/8" Jar fished in the hole at 2466m, fishing operation failed. Several stuck obs at 3202m.

6" / 5-7/8" Pipe stuck at 4230m, stuck free.

4-1/8"

twist off at 4533m, retrieved the fish. 5" B.P failed to pass 4527m. Perforatio tools stuck at 4466m. Slickline

cable left in hole

17-1/2" Tight spot obs at several points.

12"

20 TO 200 BPH loss observed from 1785 to 1814m. Pump LCM pill and decrease MW to 67 pcf, loss cured. Pipe stuck

observed at 2204m, stuck free with 120 KIPS overpool and 130 KIPS WOB. Pipe stuck observed at 2242m while POOH.

Stuck free with 400 klb downward and 120 klb upward and jarring. several pipe stuck occured while wash and ream.

reverse circulation observed.

8-3/8"

Flow in well observed, kill the well with 120 pcf mud through chocke manifold. Due to gain while pump is off,

increased MW to 145 pcf. Afterwards, decreased MW to 140 pcf due to loss. Stuck pipe observed, stuck free using

pipe lax.

5-7/8" Stuck pipe occurred, free same with pipe lax.

26" Gain observed around Conductor pipe, cemented same and drilled to TD.

17-12" Changed mud at 1652.5m due to inrease in viscusity and mud properties.

12" PDC bit and centeralizer did not pass 1755.5m, drilled section with Rock Bit and without centeralizer.

8-3/8" Changed mud form WBM to OBM at 4401 m due to pipe stuck and observation of shales on shakers.

5-7/8"

Increased MW to 126 pcf at 5022m due to flow. Flow obs at 5131m, killed well with 133 pcf mud. Pipe stuck at 5361m.

Backed off string and retrieved fish. Several stuck obs while hole condition. Dps stuck due to early hardening of

cement. Three back off jobs performed. Top of fish was at 4310m. Milling and cleaning the hole performed around

the fish. Fishing stopped due to observation of formation samples at 4456.7m.

2. Geological Information

2.1 Formation Description

A brief description of the predicted stratigraphical column in the Well SPH-03 has been taken as follows:

2.1.1 Aghajari Formation (from surface to 1402.12 m)

This huge clastic/marly formation (about 1385 m thickness) is Pliocene-Pleistocene in age and mostly composed of red claystones/siltstones, interbedded sandstone and red claystone beds. It is expected that the red claystone intervals increase to the bottom of the formation. The sandstone and siltstone layers are variably consolidated and generally can be described with light brown and light gray colors, fine to medium sand grains, well sorted and sometimes are dominated by sub-angular to sub-rounded quartz grains. The above-mentioned sandstones are loose (un-consolidated sands), friable to moderately hard form.

The marls are red, reddish brown to pale reddish brown, generally sticky and slightly silty, soft to firm, grading to claystone. The claystones are red color, sometimes show dark brown, generally soft, sticky and amorphous, locally some calcareous, grading to gray marl, generally non-silty and occasionally mottled. 36” and 24” Hole sizes will be penetrated into the Aghajari formation and then 30” casing shoe will be set at the near top of this formation, approximately will be located in the depth of 104 m (MD).

2.1.2 Mishan Formation (from 1402.12 to 1439.74 m)

The Mishan formation (about 37.6 m thickness) with Middle Miocene in age, is mainly comprised of alternated marls and limestone beds in this well, overlying the topmost Gachsaran anhydrite layer. 24” Hole size will be penetrated within this small marly/ carbonate formation.

2.1.3 Gachsaran Formation (from 1439.74 to 1942.41 m)

The Gachsaran (about 502.6 m thickness) formation with Early to Middle Pliocene in age, is predominantly made up of evaporates (anhydrite) beds, which are interbedded with gray to red marls. In terms of drilling hazards, the Gachsaran formation can be subdivided into two (2) main intervals, called Upper and Lower Gachsaran.

The Upper Gachsaran, which corresponds to members 2 to 7, is predominantly

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and

Production Operations Project

Well Drilling Program – SPH-03

Doc. No: SJD1-DDRGDP-DRDR-PLDR-3001-D03 Page 32 of 222

comprised of an alternation between anhydrite and grey marly beds. The marly succession is gray to light gray color and soft, which is observed as interbedded with some anhydrite beds. The relevant anhydrite is white, milky, soft, partly crystalline and medium hard to hard. The red marls are present and show variety of colors, ranged from red brown to brown, characterized by soft and sticky lithology. 18 5/8” casing shoe will be set at the near top of Gachsaran formation, in depth of 1495 m (MD). Otherwise, 17” hole size will be penetrated into the Gachsaran formation.

The Lower Gachsaran unit, usually corresponds to the member 1 or named Cap Rock unit, including alternated salt and anhydrite beds (in form of hard and crystalline rocks). It is noteworthy that the basal part of Gachsaran formation is characterized by dark grey to grey marls, accompanied with probable thin salt beds and interbedded anhydrite layers. The 13 3/8” casing shoe will be set at the basal part of Gachsaran formation in the depth of 1928.5 m (MD).

2.1.4 Asmari Formation (from 1942.41 to 2340.48 m)

The Asmari formation (about 398 m thickness) with Oligocene-Miocene age, is expected to be subdivided into several distinct lithological units in this well. The top of Asmari formation is characterized by bioclastic limestone and some dolomitized beds. Nevertheless, the main body of Upper Asmari unit is mostly comprised of clastic beds or fine sandstones/ siltstones (corresponds to Ghar Member).

The Upper Asmari sandy layers are interbedded with gray marls, few dolomite and claystone beds. The main body of sandstones are made up of medium grained sorted, gray to light gray, medium to coarse sands and partly pyritized. The claystone shows reddish to light brown color, soft and sticky form. The lower part of Asmari formation is made up of white, cream, light gray to gray dolomitic limestone/limestone beds. The 12 1/4” hole will be penetrated into this clastic/ carbonate formation.

2.1.5 Pabdeh Formation (from 2340.48 to 2667.23 m)

The Pabdeh formation (Paleocene-Eocene age) with about 326.75 m thickness, is expected to be subdivided into two (2) stratigraphic units in this Well. The upper part consists of grey to dark-brown argillaceous limestones, accompanied with some interbedded marls, representing pelagic facies.

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and

Production Operations Project

Well Drilling Program – SPH-03

Doc. No: SJD1-DDRGDP-DRDR-PLDR-3001-D03 Page 33 of 222

In terms of microfossil contents, index planktonic microfauna is common throughout these argillaceous intervals. There are some dark-brown and slightly argillaceous limestone interlayers. The 12 1/4” hole will be penetrated into this marly/ carbonate formation.

2.1.6 Gurpi Formation (from 2667.23 to 2919.91 m)

The Gurpi formation (Campanian to Maastrichtian age) with about 252.6 m thickness, can be subdivided into three (3) stratigraphic units, which are named the Upper Gurpi, Tarbur Tongue and Lower Gurpi from top to the bottom respectively. The Upper Gurpi unit is mainly characterized by grey to dark-brownish argillaceous limestone beds, which are marked by abundant pelagic facies and variable clay contents. Glauconitic argillaceous limestone to marl is one of the best markers to identify this unit.

The middle part of Gurpi formation corresponds to a shallow marine carbonate stack, which is named Tarbur Tongue. This particular carbonate interval is developed in the Sepehr-Jufair area, characterized by bioclastic limestone lithology and a huge accumulation of large bioclastic fragments. The Tarbur Tongue is creamy to light gray limestone stack, indicating moderate to fair reservoir quality (based on nearby wells) and probable economic hydrocarbon volume.

The Lower Gurpi unit is overlain directly by Tarbur limestone showing some similarities to the Upper Gurpi unit in terms of lithology and facies types. The Lower Gurpi is mainly characterized by grey argillaceous limestone layers (planktonic facies also dominant), which are interbedded by some grey marly intervals. The 12 1/4” hole size will penetrate this marly/ carbonate formation.

2.1.7 Ilam Formation (from 2919.91 to 3030.41 m)

The Ilam formation with Santonian in age, expected thickness of 110.5 m, known as one of the main hydrocarbons producing reservoir layers in the Sepehr-Jufair area. The Ilam formation is made up of grey to brown color limestone intervals, accompanied with few interbedded marly to claystone beds (rarely pyritic), which will increase significantly to the top of this formation.

Therefore, the Upper Ilam stack is considered to be an alternation between dolomitic

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and

Production Operations Project

Well Drilling Program – SPH-03

Doc. No: SJD1-DDRGDP-DRDR-PLDR-3001-D03 Page 34 of 222

limestone and marly to claystone beds. The above-mentioned dolomitic limestone interval may have significant reservoir quality and probable hydrocarbon contents. Although, the main body of Ilam formation, which is named Ilam-Main unit, is the main reservoir column and essentially comprised of limestone facies. This reservoir unit is characterized by planktonic facies such as Oligosteginid forms, associated with negligible clay contents. It is expected to be a big hydrocarbon bearing (more than 30 m) interval in this well.

The Lower Ilam unit, which is informally named Ilam-Poor (in terms of low reservoir quality), corresponds to a muddy limestone interval, overlying the Laffan unit directly and usually is marked by negligible hydrocarbon contents (most probably) and fully saturated by formation water. The 12 1/4” hole will penetrate this marly/ carbonate formation.

2.1.8 Laffan Unit (from 3030.41 to 3038.41 m)

Stratigraphically, the Laffan unit (about 8 to 10 m thickness) corresponds to the basal part of Ilam formation indicating Coniacian age and marked by a greenish-grey shale layers, expected to be seen in this well, overlying the top Sarvak carbonate interval. It is explained that this key formation was developed in Abadan Plain and offshore Persian Gulf areas, distinguished by fresh water to coastal Ostracod bearing interval.

This argillaceous formation significantly exhibits a sealing rock potential in the Operational Area, capped the Upper Sarvak reservoir. In terms of drilling hazards and abnormal pressure, this formation does not show any particular problem. The 12 1/4” will penetrate this argillaceous/ marly formation.

2.1.9 Sarvak Formation (from 3038.41 to 3755.78 m)

The Sarvak formation (about 717.3 m thickness) with Albian/Cenomanian-Turonian in age is mainly characterized by bioclastic carbonate successions. The Upper Sarvak interval is the main oil-bearing stack and generally described as a set of light brown to creamy bioclastic limestone, accompanied with negligible thin marls. On the whole, Upper Sarvak represents a moderate to fair reservoir quality, which is limited to the reservoir zones 3 and 4 particularly in the nearby wells. This reservoir unit is correlable with all nearby wells and significantly marked by Rudist fragments and generally is

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and

Production Operations Project

Well Drilling Program – SPH-03

Doc. No: SJD1-DDRGDP-DRDR-PLDR-3001-D03 Page 35 of 222

distinguished by clean Gamma radiation interval.

The middle to lower part of Sarvak formation is mainly dominated by bioclastic limestone beds, negligible clay contents, is mostly saturated by formation water. Ahmadi Shale unit is marked as a continuous argillaceous interval (about 10 to 15 m thickness), separates the upper and lower parts of Sarvak formation.

The lower to basal part of Sarvak formation (corresponds to the Mauddud unit) is composed of grain-supported bioclastic limestone beds, which are characterized by negligible clay contents and some chertified limestone beds. The clay volume shows a gradual increase in the vicinity of the Sarvak/Kazhdumi boundary.

In terms of drilling hazards and abnormal pressure, there is high risk and high-pressure interval just can be expected in the basal part of Sarvak formation (near to Top Kazhdumi boundary), where the clay volume and chertified limestone beds gradually appeared. It is planned that the hole size 12 1/4” will be mostly penetrated into this huge carbonate formation. The related 9 5/8” casing shoe will be set at the basal part of Sarvak formation in the approximate depth of 3726 m (MD) and also the 7” liner hanger will be set in the same interval (about 3626 m).

2.1.10 Kazhdumi Formation (from 3755.78 to 3953.9 m)

The Kazhdumi formation with Albian in age (198.1 m thickness), starts with (from base to the top) a thick bedded clastic (sandy) bed (named Azadegan Sand unit), developed in the nearby wells. The Lower Kazhdumi unit is expected to be a composition of consolidated sandstone and marly beds (about 45 m thickness). The middle to upper part of Kazhdumi formation is predominantly characterized by shallow marine (Orbitolinid facies) limestone/marly intervals, accompanied with some interbedded claystones.

The basal clastic unit exhibits fair reservoir quality that expected to be a fully saturated by formation water. The topmost interval of Kazhdumi formation (about 40 m thickness) is again dominated by clay/argillaceous muddy facies, marked by planktonic microfauna and some organic materials. The 8 1/2” hole size will penetrate this marly/ clastic formation.

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and

Production Operations Project

Well Drilling Program – SPH-03

Doc. No: SJD1-DDRGDP-DRDR-PLDR-3001-D03 Page 36 of 222

2.1.11 Dariyan Formation (from 3953.9 to 4125.45 m)

The Dariyan formation with Aptian in age (171.5 m thickness), is predominantly comprised of clean (ignorable clay contents) carbonate intervals, which are characterized by Orbitolinid facies domination. Stratigraphically, the Dariyan grey to brown color bioclastic limestone is situated between two (2) clastic bearing/ argillaceous formations including Gadvan (lower) and Kazhdumi (upper) formations and unlike this carbonate formation does not show any economic hydrocarbon saturation (based on nearby wells).

It is expected that the clay contents be increased particularly at the basal part of Dariyan formation, accompanied with some marly beds. In terms of drilling hazards and abnormal pressure, no particular problem has been reported in this pure carbonate formation. The 8 1/2” hole will penetrate into this carbonate formation.

2.1.12 Gadvan Formation (from 4125.45 to 4293.88 m)

The Gadvan formation with Barremian to Aptian in age (168.4 m thickness), is expected to be subdivided into two (2) stratigraphical units in this well, including Lower (interbedded sandstones and shales) and Upper (dominantly argillaceous/marly) units. The Gadvan formation can be started with a basal clastic sand/silt package (about 40 m thick.), which is interbedded with some marls/claystone beds and overlying the top of Fahliyan carbonates. Generally, the Lower Gadvan unit is characterized by alternated fine grain sandstone and argillaceous interlayers that are developed in the nearby wells and overlain by Khalij carbonate interval (about 20 m thick.). It is expected to be encountered with outstanding oil-bearing sand layers, based on what has been observed in Well SPH-01 and some Jufair wells. The Khalij member usually known as a muddy limestone interval, characterized by moderate to low reservoir quality and negligible hydrocarbon volume (based on log interpretation). This interval is expected to be subdivided into three (3) intervals including two (2) carbonate (Khalij A and Khalij B) and a claystone package, reported in the nearby wells. The Upper Gadvan unit is dominantly is characterized by alternated bioclastic limestone (Orbitolinid facies) and marly/claystone layers, which is comfortably overlain by Dariyan limy formation. In terms of drilling hazards and abnormal pressure, no particular problem has been occurred in this clay-rich/clastic bearing formation. Although the formation pressure in this interval is much more significant than the higher layers, we are faced with a

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and

Production Operations Project

Well Drilling Program – SPH-03

Doc. No: SJD1-DDRGDP-DRDR-PLDR-3001-D03 Page 37 of 222

significant increasing pressure trend. Therefore, the drilling mud weight should increase with respect to the recorded pressure. The 8 1/2” hole will penetrate this marly/clastic formation.

2.1.13 Fahliyan Formation (from 4293.88 to 4535 m)

The Early Cretaceous (Neocomian stage) Fahliyan formation (241 m thickness) is known as the most important reservoir layer in the Sepehr-Jufair area. In terms of stratigraphy and subsurface geology, the Fahliyan formation can be subdivided into two (2) units including Lower and Upper Fahliyan layers.

The Upper Fahliyan (about 100 m thick.) is characterized by the domination of argillaceous limestone and interbedded marly intervals, indicating low to non-reservoir quality. Stratigraphically, this limestone to marly unit can be correlated with Iraqi Ratawi formation representing the same age and facies.

The Lower Fahliyan (about 140 m thick.) is expected to be a bioclastic limestone stack with noticeable reservoir quality and economic hydrocarbon saturation. Stratigraphically, the Lower Fahliyan unit can be equivalent with the Iraqi Yamama formation, developed in the Iraqi/ Arabian areas. The Lower Fahliyan carbonates correspond to a grey to brown color bioclastic limestone stack in the form of muddy to grain-supported facies. The 8 1/2” hole will penetrate into this marly/carbonate formation. 7” liner shoe will be set at the TD (4535 m) and due to increase pressure, the drilling mud weight should be increased with respect to the well condition.

As previously mentioned, this forecasted stratigraphic column has been provided based on the reference (SPH-01) and nearby wells (new seismic data is also used). Therefore, there is still a possibility of slight changes in the depths of the formation tops and the lithology of some formations.

2.2 Cutting Sample Program

Wellsite geologist is fully responsible to determine the frequency of cutting sampling. The sampling crew shall take cutting samples based on wellsite geologist’s instruction. It is noted that the acquired sand samples from Asmari, Kazhdumi and Gadvan formations must be preserved unwashed. Note that to identify Rock Type standard classification systems (Dunham classification for carbonates and Petti john classification for sandstones) must be used.

3.3 Potential Drilling Hazards and mitigation plan

For each section a general list of most probable drilling risk has been summarized in below tables.

Potential drilling hazards/Risks for drilling 17” holePotential Hazard How to mitigateSalt water flowGachsaran formation consisting mainly of Anhydrate and Marls with inter beds of salt.Gachsaran formation also consists of marly limestone. This is a potential salt water flow zone.Maintain MW as plan MW.Check Calcium ions while drilling, in case of showing increasing trend, drilling to be stopped.Flow check if fast break experience.Loss of circulationMaintain MW as plan MW.Control running speed to prevent surge effect.Control mud rheology.Stuck drill stringClosely monitor losses while drilling.Maintain MW as plan MW.Minimize the overbalance (by decreasing mud weight)Minimize stationary time.Increase drill collar and drill string stabilization.Optimize fluid properties in attempts to minimize the risk of sticking.Stuck casing due to hole cleaning, hole geometry, loss/flow or tight holeAvoid creating ledges by easing bit in harder formation and reaming transition between [[formations.Watch](http://formations.Watch)]([http://formations.Watch](http://formations.Watch)) casing string weight, understand and monitor casing drag up and down.Avoid thick mud cake by controlling fluid loss and solids.Circulate hole clean prior to POOH for casing Survey check.Bit BallingEntire bit and/or stabilizers, teeth balling and bottom balling can be reduced by having a sufficiently inhibitive mud.Entire bit Balling risk will be reduced by consistently high flow rates, and good hole cleaning.Ensure of pumping at high flow rates, and sufficient HSI (&amp;gt;2).With tri-cone bits, center jet and oriented nuzzling will also aid preventing balling (oriented nuzzling directs part of the flow onto the cutting structure).Avoid excessive WOB while drilling through Gachsaran formation.Actions once balling has been detected:• Bits can be cleared if balling is detected early enough and actions taken.• Reduce WOB when ROP drops, pick up bit off bottom as quickly as possible andincrease flow rate.• Spin bit off bottom with high RPM and high flow rate for a period of time• Resume drilling with low weight• Prepare to pump pills (KCL solution pill), leave to soak and try to dissolve/loosenballed material

Drilling hazards/risks while drilling in 12-1/4” holePotential Hazard How to mitigateLoss circulationAsmari consists of porous limestone and dolomites providing very fast drilling. Asmari is a potential loss zone due to its high [[porosity.As](http://porosity.As)]([http://porosity.As](http://porosity.As)) losses have appeared, drilling with minimum parameter and sweep hole with High filter-loss LCM pill.Prepare to spot conventional LCM plugs.Shale instabilityPabdeh and Laffan Shales could be unstable at varying hole angles, although there are no apparent problems drilling it vertically.Raise mud density immediately if long slender pieces of Pabdeh or Laffan shale started coming over the shakers.Pabdeh, Laffan and Sarvak formations must be drilled with inhibited mud (mud weight must ensure stability even if severe losses encountered).Differential stickingThe mud weight must minimize the risk of differentially stuck pipe when crossing the zones within the reservoir objective.There are several specialized “bridging “products that reduce seepage thereby reducing the likelihood of differential sticking in low permeability zones.Install string stabilizers within the drill string to ensure ‘stand-off from the wellbore.Ensure preventative drilling practices are strictly adhered to (i.e. moving and rotating drill-string as much as possible, minimizing length of unstabilised BHA, use of spiral Drill Collars and HWDP).Control water loss, minimize mud cake building tendency.Monitor filter cake quality.Use of Rotary Steerable Systems will minimize overall contact with the wellbore and will reduce the tendency for differential sticking.Solids removal equipment should be used with full performance and efficiencyTight holeMaintain Mud weight as plan Mud weight.Monitor mud rheology.Ensure sufficient inhibitor exist in mud system.Consider wiper trip if hole condition [[dictates.To](http://dictates.To)]([http://dictates.To](http://dictates.To)) minimize chances of stuck pipe, avoid pulling above 25 Klbs.Drill string corrosionInspect drill string regularly.Use corrosion inhibitor into mud system.Ledging and hole spiralingLedging can be an issue when drilling alternate hard and soft formations particularly at an angle. This can occur when drilling through the reservoir zones. Ledging occurs generally at the top of the harder formations at the interface when whirl or other lateral instability is induced due to the reduced depth of cut. This can be reduced or eliminated by following negative drill break practices and easing the bit into the harder formation.Poor weight transfer to the bit can also produce ledging and hole enlargement by reducing the depth of cut at the bit, thus initiating lateral instability and whirl.The higher the bend angle the more likely hole spiraling will occur. To overcome this problem a long gauge bit or turbo-back stabilizer can be used. Another method of reducing hole spiraling is to reduce the distance from bit face to bent [[housing.Review](http://housing.Review)]([http://housing.Review](http://housing.Review)) the offset wells for problems encountered.

Poor hole cleaningHole angles between 45° and 65° present the most problems with drilled cuttings having a tendency to slide down the annulus and ‘pack off’. Hole angles greater than 65° do not present additional problems in this regard since the drilled cuttings are supported by sliding friction against the wellbore and become more stable as discrete cuttings beds. Use good hole cleaning practices to prevent formulation of cutting beds (Rotation, High GPM, Thin Sweeps. . .)Cement quality and cross flowUtilizing DV collar.QC cement and cement additives.Ensure applications and recording of Cement Quality Parameters (CQPs) evaluation.Follow up PEP’s cementing operation procedure.

Drilling hazards/risks while drilling in 8.5” holePotential Hazard How to mitigateStuck PipeThe mud weight must ensure stability within the Kazhdumi and Gadvan Shale and minimize the risk of differentially sticking when crossing the zones within the reservoir objective (Fahliyan).Installing string stabilizers within the drill string to ensure stand-off from the wellbore in permeable reservoir formations will compromise directional (build) capability.Use of Rotary Steerable Systems will minimize overall contact with the wellbore and will reduce the tendency for differential sticking, particularly in longer extended reach wells.Ensure preventative drilling practices are strictly adhered to i.e. moving and rotating drill-string as much as possible, minimizing length of unestablished BHA, use of spiral Drill Collars and HWDP. These measures however may not be practical in wells where the build to horizontal is a critical objective.Well ControlMost of well control problems occur while tripping out due to swabbing (tripping speed) or failure to fill the hole with proper fluid volume; trip sheet has to be filled accurately and control tripping out speed to avoid well control problems.Cement quality and cross flowUtilizing rotating liner hanger and centralizers.QC cement and cement additives.Ensure applications and recording of Cement Quality Parameters (CQPs) evaluation.Follow up PEP’s cementing operation procedure.

Loss Circulation Mitigation:

24” hole section loss control:

Downhole Losses

Concentration of LCM will vary according to the size of losses. In the event of seepage losses, no specific action will be taken but close monitoring of the loss rate over the time and drilled depth shall be made.

In the event of moderate to high rate of well bore loss, prepare pills at different grades and concentrations, and spot it over thief zone. The concentration may vary between 20 to 100 ppb.

Below procedure is supposed to be followed in case that various rates of losses are encountered in the course of drilling, though the most effective plan is the one which is customized based on actual situation on site:

Losses less than 10 bbl/hr:

➢ No action to be taken, but close monitoring of the loss shall be made

Losses 10 - 30 bbl/hr:

➢ Load Kwik-Seal F in system up to 10 ppb

If no success, then:

➢ Pump 50 bbl LCM pill containing:

▪ 3-6 ppb Mica Medium

▪ 7-12 ppb Walnut Shells Fine

▪ 7-12 ppb Kwik-Seal Fine &amp;amp; Medium

▪ 3-6 ppb CaCO3-M

Note: System is loaded gradually from low concentration to maximum mentioned ranges.

Losses 30 – 100 bbl/hr:

➢ Load CaCO3 Medium &amp;amp; Coarse in active system up to 5 ppb of each

➢ Load Kwik-Seal F in system up to 10 ppb

 If needed / required; shaker-man should be ready for managing a part of the return

flow toward the mud pits by-pass the shakers to avoid screens get blinded and LCM

get wasted. However, this is a matter of operation-dictated decision.

If no success, then:

➢ Stop Drilling

➢ Pull out string above the loss zone

➢ Spot 60-90 bbl pill containing:

▪ Pre-Hydrated Bentonite 5-10 ppb

▪ 6-10 lb/bbl Kwik-Seal F

▪ 6-10 lb/bbl Kwik-Seal M

▪ 6-10 lb/bbl Walnut-Shells F

▪ 6-10 lb/bbl Mica M

▪ 20-30 lb/bbl CaCO3-F, M

▪ Repeat this pill for two times

➢ If LCM pill at above concentration cannot pass through the string (bit nuzzles, etc.), we need

to pump the pill through a Mule-Shoe while following the procedure of the next state.

Losses more than 100 bbl/hr to Total Losses:

In the event of severe losses, Squeeze Pills, Barite or CaCO3 or Cement Plugs, Silicate Pill or Cross-Linking Pills should be pumped to minimize losses.

17” Hole section loss control:

Downhole Losses

The concentration of LCM will vary according to the size of losses. In the event of seepage losses, treat system with a finer grade of LCM at 10-15 lb/bbl.

In the event of moderate to high rate of well bore loss, prepare pills at different graded concentrations and spot over thief zone. The concentration may vary between 25-95 lb/bbl. In order to avoid LCM plugging MWD tools a circulation sub should be installed in the drill string. The MWD engineer is to advise on the size and concentration of LCM that can be pumped through MWD Tools. Ensure that the drilling displace the LCM pill out of the string prior to shutting down the mud pumps.

In the event of severe losses, cross linking pills should be pumped to minimize losses.

The following plan is to be followed prior to intersecting the loss zone while drilling in case losses are encountered:

The following plan is to be followed in case losses are encountered:

Losses less than 10 bbl/hr:

➢ Load CaCO3-M in active system up to 5ppb.

➢ Load synthetic fibre in system up to 0.1 ppb

➢ Load KWIK SEAL-F in system up to 10 ppb

Losses 10 - 30 bbl/hr:

➢ Load CaCO3-M in active system up to 5ppb.

➢ Load Synthetic Fibre in system up to 0.1ppb

8.5” Hole section loss control:

Downhole Losses

Losses/Differential sticking will be minimized/avoided by the planned use of properly sized bridging/weight material (and Polymer) in conjunction with appropriate drilling practices. If seepage losses are noted on the well no specific action will be taken but close monitoring of the loss rate is to be made. For moderate loss rates addition of CaCO3 50 micron and 150mic. is recommended to ensure that there is adequate correctly sized material to act as bridging agents.

CaCO3 will minimize filtrate/whole mud invasion of the reservoir and reduce potential problems of losses and differential sticking. The fluid loss and cake quality are two of the most important mud properties to prevent or alleviate potential stuck pipe. Note that, the maintenance of the correct amount and size of bridging material cannot be over-stressed.

Seepage losses Less than 10 bbl/hr.

Load the mud system with 5 ppb of CaCO3 M LCM. Some of the CaCO3-300 will be separated on the shale shaker. Add 4 sacks per 5 meters drilled to compensate the separated amount on the shakers.

Losses from 10-30 bbl/hr.

➢ Load CaCO3 M in system up to 5ppb.

➢ Pump 45-60bbl of the following pill:

▪ 5ppb CaCO3 75mic

▪ 10-15 ppb CaCO3 200-300mic or Oyster shell F

▪ 10-15 ppb CaCO3 600mic or Oyster shell M

Losses from 30-50 bbl/hr.

➢ Load CaCO3 M in system up to 5ppb.

➢ Pump 45-60bbl of the following pill:

▪ 10-15ppb CaCO3 75mic

▪ 20-30 ppb CaCO3 200-300mic or Oyster shell F

▪ 20-30 ppb CaCO3 600mic or Oyster shell M

This will cause severe mud losses while entering Cap-Rock formation due to high mud weight used to drill the basal Gachsaran.Tight Hole Having tight intervals are expected while drilling in most of the formations of this hole. 4.1.2 Sequence of Operation

1. Check Pre-Spud Check List. Make up 36” BHA (24'' Bit &amp;amp; 36'' Hole Opener as tandem) as per BHA

design. Tag formation at ±10.5m.

Note:

▪ Ensure that all drilling tools and equipment are on well site and are in serviceable condition.

▪ Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this section of hole are available.

▪ Enough Mud Material, LCM and Cement Should be Available before spud the rig to use in

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and

Doc. No: SJD1-DDRGDP-DRDR-PLDR-3001-D03 Page 60 of 222

case of needing.

▪ 1 Set cement pump truck should be available on well site before start drilling.

▪ Mud Logging unit should be available from rig spud.

2. Drill ahead formation down to 104 m (30” casing point in Aghajari formation) using hi-vis

bentonite pill. Pay enough attention to drill straight hole. Control flow rate and take care of wash

outs below rig sub base.

Note:

▪ TD should be adjusted to have 2 m of rat hole below casing shoe.

▪ The exact TD will be determined based on casing tally.

▪ Run Survey to Check inclination @ 50 &amp;amp; 100 mt (to ensure the deviation is below 1 degree)

3. At TD, Circulate and clean the hole. Observe the well. Perform Wiper Trip Prior to running casing.

Spot viscous mud @ Well Bottom. POOH to surface. Check Bit.

4. Perform Pre-Job Safety meeting (PJSM).

5. R/Up CSG/ Running Equipment.

6. Run 30" Casing 234# to 104 Mt with stinger shoe to bottom as per casing program. Casing shoe

should be adjusted to have 2 m of rat hole and enough stick up (1.5 m on rig floor). Fill casing by

non-LCM fresh mud.

➢ Do not exert much load and compressing stress on the shoe if encountered tight hole and

ledges.

➢ Make sure that 2 No. of 2” nipple had been welded on conductor and it is plugged w/ a quick

union low pressure plug.

7. Run stinger on 5" DP’s using the “C” Plate and 5” x 30” centralizer. Sting in. M/U &amp;amp; test cementing

lines. Circulate for 1.2 or till shaker clean volume (Maximum allowable pressure: 150 psi). While

circulating, check the DPs annulus for any return. Use all DPs weight on the string if observing

any minor leakage through DPs annulus.

8. Cement casing as per program. Any minor adjustment regarding the corrected depth will be

done in due time. Displace with mud (1-2 bbl. Short Displace). Monitor the pressures. Record

and report the final pressure, Sting out. Check the float. POOH one stand, Circulate to flush/clean

drill pipe. POOH to surface. L/D Stinger While W.O.C to Get Hard, perform top Job If Needed.

Note:

▪ Based on the results obtained from cementing, decision will be made to perform top-up jobs

While W.O.C to Get Hard.

9. After cement returns to cellar floor, open the 2" nipple on conductor &amp;amp; flush it.

10. If there is no cement return to surface, a top-up job should be performed to fill the annulus. Use

same slurry weight as the primary cement slurry. The cement should be accelerated with max.

(2%) Calcium Chloride BWOC and no other additives. Wait for the top job cement to get hard.

11. Slack Off Weight. Check Cement by slack off weight and check for any movement.

12. Rough Cut Conductor Pipe and 30" Casing, Dress &amp;amp; Bevel Casing Neck. Prepare and Install 29-

1/2'' Flange (Locking flange). Check Cement by slack off weight. Check for any movement.

13. N/U BOP (29-1/2" Diverter- 500 psi) Bell Nipple &amp;amp; flow line and Related Lines &amp;amp; Valves.

14. Perform diverter function Test.

15. P/U Next BHA and Stand Back 5" DP's as needed.

16. RIH W/ New BHA and 24" Bit #1 (1-3-5) to Tag Shoe, Drill Out Shoe &amp;amp; cement below shoe.

• BOP’s Schematics with all related dimensions

• BOP’s test Report

21. RIH with 5-7/8” bit drill out Pack off bushing to LDC

22. CIRC Btm`s UP. POOH To Surf.

23. Test BOP Stack and all Related Lines as NIOC POLICY when at Surf.

24. P/U Dry Test Equip &amp;amp; run to 50 m above L-lap. Perform Dry test.

DRY TEST PROCEDURE:

➢ Remove wear bushing

➢ RIH W/DST tools (Fill up string with water cushion each 5 stands &amp;amp; observe cushion level to make

2000 psi as Driving Force. Max. RIH speed must be 8 stands per hour)

➢ After reaching packer depth (±50 m above liner lap) make up head &amp;amp; surface equipment &amp;amp;

pressure test (packer should not set on casing connection), Set packer

➢ Open the tools for 3 hours or reach water cushion to surface.

➢ Close the tools for 6 hours &amp;amp; drop shearing bar &amp;amp; reverse circulation @ the sixth hour, Unset

packer, Circulate bottom up (CBU)

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and

Production Operations Project

Well Drilling Program – SPH-03

Doc. No: SJD1-DDRGDP-DRDR-PLDR-3001-D03 Page 71 of 222

➢ Observe the well, POOH

25. Secure the Well, POOH to Surf, L/D Test Equipment.

26. P/U 7" Suitable Scrapper, RIH to liner Shoe, Scrap. CIRC Btm`s Up, POOH to Surf, L/D Scrapper.

27. R/Up Logging Tools, Run USIT/CAST Log inside 7" liner, L/D Logging Tools.

28. P/U 7" Suitable Scrapper, RIH to TD, Scrap. CIRC Btm`s Up, Displace 30 bbl suitable perforation

fluid (CaCl2).

29. Test BOP Stack and all Related Lines as NIOC POLICY.

30. R/U TCP equipment, RIH TCP (for Shoot and Pull), perform TCP correlation, Perforate selected

intervals of Fahliyan formation, POOH.

31. RIH MTT/MFC to confirm perforation interval, POOH.

32. RIH w/ 5 7/8'' Bit To top of perforation interval, Displace Hole with completion fluid (CaBr2).

POOH and L/d DPS.

33. R/U and prepare all equipment for Running Completion String, Running Completion String as

program.

34. N/D BOP, Install X-Mass tree and test

35. Open SSD, reverse circulation and displace annulus and tubing fluid (CaBr2) with packer fluid.

Close SSD and pressure test, Retrieve plug and prong.

36. Rig up and pressure test surface line and equipment.

37. Flow the well by Coiled Tubing, perform acid wash, POOH CT and flow the well to cleanup and

perform PLT

38. Close choke manifold.

39. Inflow Test TRSCSSSV (Well pressure below TRSCSSSV &amp;amp; 500 psi above TRSCSSSV), If injectivity

is good, Bullhead solvent &amp;amp; diesel to the well &amp;amp; if injectivity is not good, displace the well with

diesel by CT.

40. Rig up slick-line &amp;amp; perform pressure test, set plug &amp;amp; prong in No-Go landing nipple, perform

plug &amp;amp; completion string test (4500/7500psi for 15min), Retrieve protection sleeve.

41. Rig up BPV running/retrieval equipment, Pressure test the same &amp;amp; install one-way check valve.

42. Close 3SV and X-Mas tree valves except BMV

43. Rig Released.

Production Operations Project

Well Drilling Program – SPH-03

6.1.4.1 Stress Components

Note:

• The optimum range for RPM, based on the stress components plot, is 85 to 95, 110 to 120 and

130 to 140.

• At RPM 85, 95 to 105 and 125 the string stress concentration is high, specially shear and bending

stress.

• The maximum axial stress is likely to occur at HWDP according to the position plot at 90 rpm,

the position plot displays the position of the relative stress vs. distance from the bit at specific

RPM.

• Based on Displacement plot, the abnormal displacement happens at 95 to 105 rpm.

• Final optimum RPM and other drilling parameters shall be revised during the operation based

on drilling condition.

10.2.1 Casing 30"

Suggested depth for surface 30” casing shoe is about 104 m (Aghajari formation) in order to seal off the shallow strata, and will be cemented up to the surface.

10.2.2 Casing 18 5/8"

Aghajari Clastic / Marly and Mishan Marly formations will be covered by this casing. The 18 5/8” casing shoe will be set in the most upper part of Gachsaran formation at the approximate depth of 1495 m MD.

10.2.3 Casing 13 3/8" &amp;amp; 13 5/8”

The penetrated hole in the Gachsaran formation will be covered by tapered 13 3/8" and 13 5/8” casing and the relevant casing shoe will be set inside Cap rock unit of Gachsaran formation right above top of Asmari formation. The approximate depth of this casing shoe is about 1928.5 m MD.

10.2.4 Casing 9 5/8"

The penetrated hole in the Asmari, Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan and Sarvak formations will be covered by this casing. The 9 5/8” casing shoe will be set at the basal Sarvak or near top of Kazhdumi formations in approximate depth of 3726 m MD.

10.2.5 Liner 7"

The penetrated hole in the Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan and Fahliyan formations will be covered by 7" liner and the liner shoe will be set at well TD (4535 m). In fact, the main Khami reservoir layers including Lower Gadvan and Lower Fahliyan will be covered by the 7” liner.

14. Waste Management Program

Detailed Waste management Program will be prepared by drilling fluid service company and will be delivered separately before rig spud.

1. While the drilling/completion operation is ongoing, perform all related services

such as design, supply, execute, supervise and control of waste water, mud and

drilling cuttings treatment plan complied with Iranian Petroleum Standards (IPS) as

well as good engineering practices,

2. Solidification treatment units and/or other proposed methods/units to dispose the

drilling waste materials (liquids and solids including used drilling and completion

fluids, drilling cuttings materials, residual acid and sometimes small amounts of oil),

equipment, Personnel and necessary chemicals for the waste treatment will be

available

3. Transport the treated waste materials from the location to the designated area

specified by Company.

4. Discharge water after dewatering shall meet below standards:

▪ pH=7~9

▪ Total hardness&amp;lt; 800 mg/L

▪ Turbidity (NTU) &amp;lt; 50

▪ T.S.S (Total Suspended Solid) &amp;lt; 80 mg/L

▪ Nitrate ion (NO3-) &amp;lt; 50 mg/L

▪ Aluminum &amp;lt; 3 mg/L

▪ Sulphate &amp;lt; 3200 mg/L

▪ Ca2+ &amp;lt; 600 mg/L

5. Ensure that dried and fixed cuttings can pass the CAN test. For fixing the cuttings,

100-150 kg cement and 3 - 4-liter sodium silicate shall be used for each cubic meters

of cuttings.

Prevent environmental pollution, conserve resources and minimize waste materials. Minimize the impact of Work on the environment.

Appropriate treatment of waste materials shall be undertaken and monitored to minimize the impact of discharges and disposals on the environment.

The waste treatment and disposal shall be performed during the drilling period.

The system should consist of separation, containment, handling, treatment and

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and

Production Operations Project

Well Drilling Program – SPH-03

Doc. No: SJD1-DDRGDP-DRDR-PLDR-3001-D03 Page 185 of 222

disposal equipment.

Equipment which should be used to carry out the process are as follow:

1. Separation: high efficiency solid and liquid separation system

2. Containment and handling

• Conveyer: for collection and discharge of all cuttings

• Drying shale shaker: giving dryer cuttings and reduced mud

consumption

• Contingency tanks: arrangement for the occasional collection,

separation and isolation of cutting wastes

• Fluid sump: for the collection of site drains and excess drilling fluid

• Tanks: for the storage of excess fluid prior to treatment

• Pumps: transfer equipment

• Backhoe, dump truck and etc. for the transportation of disposals

3. Treatment and disposal:

• Fixation: using cement or similar to stabilize the salt or chemicals

• Dewatering of excess fluids, site water, and water-based drilling fluid

• At least 50 percent of liquid phase should be used in mud making

system.

4. Equipment requirement:

• Dewatering unit including: dosing pump, PAC and polymer’s tanks

• Connectors and hoses for pumps and tanks

• Filter press/centrifuge unit

• 3 buffer tanks including: mixers and transfer pumps

• 2 air pumps

• 1 wash down gun

• 1 submersible pump

• Testing equipment such as pH meter, jar test, Hach test, retort kit and

titration accessories

15. Health, Safety and Environment

15.1 General Quality, Health, Safety and Environmental Requirements

COMPANY is committed to conducting operations in a manner which minimizes the risks to the health and safety of those involved in, and affected by, such operations. COMPANY is also committed to conducting its operations in a manner which minimizes the impact on natural and ‘built’ environments in the area of operations.

1. This section sets out minimum Quality, Health, Safety and Environmental

(QHSE) requirements for the WORK that CONTRACTOR and subcontractors will

be required to comply with whilst conducting operations for COMPANY.

2. COMPANY may perform audits and assessments of CONTRACTOR’s and its

subcontractors’ performance under the CONTRACT. COMPANY reserves the

right without prior notice to conduct quality, health, safety, security and

environmental audits of the Operations.

3. CONTRACTOR shall at all times be responsible for performing the WORK in a

manner so as to protect against loss of life, injury to people, damage to property

and the environment. The detailed manner means and methods of performing

the WORK shall be under the control and direction of CONTRACTOR.

4. Prior to the start of Operations, certain QHSE processes must be completed.

15.8 Well Control

(1) Recording Reference

All BOP tests, drills, function tests, any malfunctions, repair or maintenance to the mud system and well control equipment shall be recorded in the IADC daily reports and shall be signed by both the Drilling Contractor's Tool Pusher and Drilling Supervisor on the well site. They shall also be recorded in the Daily Drilling Report.

(2) Flow Check Procedure

To avoid a kick situation, it is recommended that a flow check be conducted at specific times during the drilling operation.

• While drilling (any warning sign)

• Prior to tripping the drill string

• While tripping (any warning sign)

• While out of hole(continuously)

• Trip out:

➢ After pulling 5% of the drill pipe

➢ At the midpoint depth of the wellbore

➢ Prior to pulling the first stand of drill collars

➢ After all the drill string is out of hole.

• Trip in:

➢ Upon reaching surface casing shoe

➢ At midpoint of the wellbore

(3) Primary Control Reference

It is the responsibility of the Drilling Contractor to keep the hole full at all times by using all the available equipment. The Drilling Supervisor shall monitor that the correct preventive practices are being implemented and/or conducted at all times.

Extreme care shall be taken to monitor mud volume, drilling breaks and gas cut mud.

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and

Production Operations Project

Well Drilling Program – SPH-03

Doc. No: SJD1-DDRGDP-DRDR-PLDR-3001-D03 Page 205 of 222

The MACP (Maximum allowable casing pressure) shall be confirmed by the Drilling Supervisor, either after setting each new casing string or, whenever the density of the drilling mud changes.

The MACP shall be clearly written on a kick control sheet that will be posted near the choke control panel.

The predetermined distance at which the Tool Joint is to be pulled above the rotary should be posted on rig floor near the BOP control panel.

The Driller is responsible for carefully measuring and recording the slow pump pressure. Awareness of these values is an important element in killing operations, in order to avoid formation breakdown.

Take a measure and record the slow pump pressure at three different flow rates with all pumps at the following times:

1) Once per tour.

2) Whenever changes occur in the mud density/rheology.

3) Whenever changes occur in the dimension and characteristics of the

string, BHA, jet size, jet plugged or jet lost, etc.

4) Secondary Control Reference

Any time a drilling break is noticed, drilling shall stop and a static monitoring of the well shall be carried out. Space-out for all Pipe Rams and Annular Preventer must be known to the Driller at all times to keep tool joints clear of annular preventer and rams.

5) Kick Detection Procedure While Drilling

If there is an indication of a possible kick occurring, the Driller shall follow the kick detection procedures outlined below:

Stop drilling with the pump on→Pick up top drive to a predetermined space-out position→Shut off the pumps and check for well flow by visual examination on the bell nipple or flow line.

If the well is not flowing:

• Immediately notify the rig manager, Drilling Supervisor and Tool pusher.

• The Drilling Supervisor will decide whether to circulate bottoms up or

resume drilling. The penetration rate will be limited as long as the cause of

the abnormal situation is undetermined. Always be aware that some

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and

Production Operations Project

Well Drilling Program – SPH-03

Doc. No: SJD1-DDRGDP-DRDR-PLDR-3001-D03 Page 206 of 222

hydrocarbons (gas or oil cut mud) may rise to the surface. Ensure that the proper monitoring and safety systems all in place.

If the well is flowing:

• Close the well as per the Shut-in Procedure.

• Immediately notify the Wellsite Drilling Supervisor, rig manager and Tool

pusher.

(4) Soft Shut-in Procedure and Line Up

During operations the circuit has to be lined up as follows:

• Manuel valve on choke line is opened

• Hydraulic valve on choke line has to be closed

• The choke on choke manifold has to be opened

• All the valves leading to the separator passing by the choke (downstream

valves) have to be in open positions.

• Beside these valves, all the valves have to be in closed position.

▪ Soft Shut in procedure while drilling

The procedure is performed as follows:

- if there is any kick indication, stop rotation, pick up off bottom and space

out (Tool joint one meter above rotary table to avoid getting the next

tool joint on the pipe rams)

- Stop pumps, perform flow check. If the well is flowing then:

- Open choke line valve at the BOP stack (Called HCR)

- Close annular BOP

- Close Choke

- Read and Record pressures and times. Check pit volume gain in order to

prepare the kill sheet

- If the gas is migrating, control the wellbore pressures during the shut in.

▪ Soft Shut in procedure while tripping

If there is any kick indication, stop tripping immediately. Here, two different

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and

Production Operations Project

Well Drilling Program – SPH-03

Doc. No: SJD1-DDRGDP-DRDR-PLDR-3001-D03 Page 207 of 222

situations can be identified:

a) The well is flowing, then the shut in is proceeded as follows:

- Set the string on the slips

- Install a fully opening safety valve in open position. Close the valve

once is installed

- Open choke line valve at BOP stack (HCR valve)

- Close annular BOP

- Close choke.

- Read and record pressures and times, check pit volumes

It depends on the situation to weather to start killing procedures or to strip back to the bottom.

- If the stripping is faced, then, Stab IBOP (Grey valve)

- Open the fully opening safety valve

- Reduce the annular pressure and start stripping the string to the

bottom

b) The well is not flowing:

- Set the string on the slips

- Install IBOP (grey valve or non-return valve)

- Run back in the hole with controlling the volumes, if any anomalies are

noticed then proceed to the stripping. Once on bottom, circulate

annular volume and evaluate the situation.

15.9 H2S Monitoring and Prevention Measure

Monitoring H2S

1) Somewhere on the well site is apt to accumulate H2S, such as mud pit, shale shaker,

and drilling platform, should be installed one set of. Make sure H2S monitor and

alarm system can be used.

2) Alarm threshold setting for H2S warning indicator: the first warning level is

10mg/m3, unable warning sound, just show present value of H2S content to

operators. The second warning level is 20mg/m3, when the H2S content in air

exceed 20mg/m3, H2S warning indicator can give an alarm automatically, and

warning sound should be heard by everyone work in well site. The audible alarm

should be installed on Kelly board.

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and

Production Operations Project

Well Drilling Program – SPH-03

Doc. No: SJD1-DDRGDP-DRDR-PLDR-3001-D03 Page 208 of 222

3) Equip enough gas masks on drilling platform, shaker screen (total amount should

large than 24), and equip 12 sets of 30min positive pressure Air Aspirators， 2 sets

of portable H2S monitor and appropriative H2S warning indicator. Arrange a person

specially assigned for taking charge all the protective apparatus. This man must do

periodical check to keep this equipment in a good condition.

4) H2S monitor should be done weekly check and compulsory examination.

5) After drilling into the pay zone, strengthen the detection of H2S content in mud.

6) Contractor shall implement H2S service system by himself or 3rd party for

controlling the risk of H2S leakage.

7) All equipment and devices shall be on location before Tarbur formation

penetration, service Personnel shall be on location before Spud in the hole section

which contains H2S or other poisonous gases.

Measures for H2S prevention

1) Windsocks shall be set on the drill floor and in the monsoon direction or/and

prevailing wind direction of Sepehr-Jufair oil field, off well site. In emergency,

employees must follow the evacuation procedure.

2) Explosion-proof blowers shall be installed around the rig, shale shaker, and drilling

fluid tanks to blow away toxic and flammable gas at the well site.

3) The rig crew in the H2S area shall be furnished with H2S monitors and adequate

protective apparatus in accordance with IPS. Everybody shall be able to use,

maintain, and check the apparatus.

4) The technicians of rig crew are responsible for H2S proof training and the tool

pusher is in charge of the supervision and examination.

5) The pH value of drilling fluid in the H2S area shall be kept over 9.5. Pay attention to

measurement of H2S concentration in drilling fluid. The H2S concentration shall be

kept at less than 50mg/cm3 by using sulphur removal agents and degassers.

6) Personnel safety and protection shall be carried out according to IPS during

operations in polluted areas where H2S content exceeds the critical concentration.

7) When the rig crew makes decision to bleed and fire because well control cannot be

performed due to well site conditions, operations shall be performed according to

procedures in IPS.

8) Once blowout occurs, the incident shall be reported to the higher-level department

as soon as possible and firefighting trucks, ambulances, medical care personnel and

technicians shall be on duty at the well site.

9) After the blowout is controlled, H2S concentration should be measured in the

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and

Production Operations Project

Well Drilling Program – SPH-03

Doc. No: SJD1-DDRGDP-DRDR-PLDR-3001-D03 Page 209 of 222

places where H2S is possible to gather.

10) The personnel are not allowed to access until the H2S concentration is below the

critical concentration.

15.10 H2S Monitoring &amp;amp; Control

The H2S system equipment provided shall be designed for the safety-zone-area classification where they are deployed. Equipment supplied by the service company for the purpose of the work shall at all times be maintained in good conditions of the performance of the services.

Doc. No: SJD4 DDRGED DRDR PLDR 9001 D01 Page 19 of 281

1. Introduction

The Sepehr-Jufair Field is located in the Abadan Plain, Southwest of Khuzestan Province, about 60 km West of Ahwaz and 30 km South of Susangerd. The Sepehr-Jufair field covers about 352 square kilometers area with approximately 23 kilometers long and 27 kilometers wide. Figure-1 illustrates the geographical situation of the Sepehr and Jufair gentle culminations that are located in the vicinity of South Azadegan and Yadavaran giant fields. Currently four wells are in production in the Jufair area. The penetrated formations from top to bottom will be Aghajari, Mishan, Gachsaran, Asmari, Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam respectively.

Figure 1-1: Geographical location of the Sepehr-Jufair field

The first well (JR-01) was Spudded in the crestal area of the Jufair Field by DEMINEX Co. in 1975. The first drilling operation was continued to the depth of 4276 meters (MD) in order to evaluate the Bangestan (Ilam and Sarvak) and Gadvan reservoir layers. After drilling the well, five wells have been drilled in the Jufair area. Based on the achieved data from these wells, it was planned to drill Well JR- 06 (as an appraisal/ producer well) to further investigate the Khami Group layers, especially the Lower Fahliyan reservoir layer. Well JR-06 was drilled as an appraisal/production well at December 2020 in vicinity of Ilam horizontal well. The evaluation of acquired data from this well proved having good potential of hydrocarbon in the Jufair area. In order to further investigation of Khami Group it was decided to drill new appraisal/production wells in Jufair area. The third production well which is named Ilam horizontal well will be drilled in central part of Sepehr-Jufair Field in vicinity of the Well JR-06 &amp;amp; JR-05. Geographically, the well JR-09 will be spudded in vicinity of the well JR-05 with a distance about 1616m. Therefore, the aforementioned well was used as reference well. In fact, the well JR-09 will be drilled in Western Area of Jufair Culmination, in the West of well JR-05. The Ilam horizontal well will be drilled into the Ilam Formation (2962 TVDSS/4126 mMD depth).

2.5. Well Objective:

• Zero safety incidents

Achieve all safety, environment and community related objectives.

• Deliver Ilam New Well JR-09 as Ilam Horizontal Production well that is effectively hydraulically

isolated by achieving zonal isolation requirements to secure the well for drilling horizontal section

and production through the reservoir in the 6 1/8" &amp;amp; 5 7/8" section.

• Hit all subsurface targets within allowable range.

• Obtain open hole wireline logs and cuttings sample to evaluate the reservoir quality of the Ilam

formation. Also provide appropriate information on non-target reservoir interval.

• Collect data for drilling performance optimization and future well planning.

• Adopt best drilling practices in order to have quality borehole across Ilam formation.

• Successful well handover as per plan.

The drilling program is a guideline to conduct drilling operation. The drilling team may adjust appropriate changes according to site condition, but any changes must be approved by Pasargad E&amp;amp;P Company.

approval process.

2.7. JR-09 Operation Summary:

JR-09 is horizontal production well with expected TD of 4126mMD. The target formation is Ilam formation.

▪ Drill 12 1/4" vertical hole to ±2400 m MD (KOP)

▪ Drill 12 ¼” directional hole to ±2639m MD

▪ Drill 8 ½” directional hole to ±3073m MD

▪ Drill 6 1/8” main horizontal open hole to ±4126m MD

▪ Drill 5 7/8" Lateral leg from previous 6 1/8" open hole (from 3500m) with 500m length to TD

▪ RIH Kick off string including suitable tubing hanger and temporary X-mass tree

▪ Perform selective acidizing by inflatable packer and perform flow test

▪ Run slotted liner as per wellbore stability condition of 6 1/8" main hole (as contingency)

▪ R/U Perforation equipment and perform perforation in Ilam 2A layer

▪ Displace the well by CaCl2 completion fluid

▪ Run ESP completion

▪ Flow the Well and Record Data

▪ Secure the Well and Release the Rig

3. Geological Information

Well JR-09 will be spudded as a producer well and adjacent to Wells JR‐03, JR‐04 and JR-05 in the North West part of Sepehr-Jufair Field. This Well will be penetrated finally into the Ilam reservoir layers with estimated depth of ±4126mMD (2980mTVD).

In terms of structural geology, the proposed well is located in the Western part of the Jufair culmination. It is noted that the new updating Ilam‐Main depth map has been used in order to determine the accurate position of the Ilam horizontal well. (Figure 3-1)

Figure 3-1: Sepehr-Jufair structural geometries based on Ilam depth maps

A brief description of the predicted stratigraphy column in the well JR-09 from top to TD are as follows:

3.1. Aghajari Formation (from surface to 1408 m MD)

This huge clastic/marly succession (1408 m thickness) is Pliocene-Pleistocene in age and mostly composed of red marls, interbedded sandstone, gypsum/anhydrite, and red claystone layers. It is expected that the claystone and anhydrite intervals increase from top to the bottom. The clastic intervals include of sandstone and siltstone layers are variably consolidated and generally described

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production

Operations Project

Well Drilling Program - JR-09

Doc. No: SJD4 DDRGED DRDR PLDR 9001 D01 Page 27 of 281

as light brown and light gray colors, fine to medium sand grains. They are commonly well sorted representing sub‐angular to subrounded sand grains. The main body of sandstone packages are loose (un‐consolidated sands), friable to moderately hard. The mentioned interbedded marls are red to reddish brown color, generally sticky and slightly silty, soft to firm and grading to claystone. The claystone layers are reddish in color, showing generally soft, sticky, and amorphous. They are locally calcareous, grading to gray marl, generally non‐silty and occasionally mottled. There are negligible argillaceous limestone beds that can be observed in both middle and lower parts of the Aghajari formation (between depths of 600 to 800 m). Both 32” and 24” holes will be drilled into the Aghajari formation and 26” and 18 5/8” casings will be run within the formation. In addition, 26” casing shoe will be set at the near top of this clastic formation, about the depth of 100m (MD).

3.2. Mishan Formation (from 1408 to 1496m MD)

The Mishan formation (about 88 meters thick) with Middle Miocene in age, is mainly comprised of alternated marl, anhydrite and limestone beds in this well, overlying the topmost Gachsaran anhydrite layer. 24” Hole size will be penetrated within this small marly/ carbonate formation.

3.3. Gachsaran Formation (from 1496 to 2020m MD)

The Gachsaran formation is Early to Middle Pliocene in age, and expected to be about 524 m thick. It is predominantly comprised of evaporate successions (Anhydrite and salt beds), which are interbedded with some gray to red marls. In terms of drilling hazards, the Gachsaran formation is subdivided into two (2) major intervals, called Upper and Lower Gachsaran. The Upper Gachsaran corresponds to members 2 to 7, predominantly constituted by alternated anhydrite, marly and salt successions. The marl is gray to light gray in color and soft, which is seen commonly interbedded by white anhydrite layers. The relevant anhydrite is white to milky in color, soft, partly crystalline, medium hard to hard in terms of physical properties.

The Lower Gachsaran interval, usually corresponds to member 1 (Cap Rock unit) known as alternated salt and anhydrite beds (in form of hard and crystalline). The basal part of Gachsaran formation is characterized by dark grey to grey marls, thin salt beds and interbedded anhydrite layers.

The top of Gachsaran formation will be drilled by 24” hole and 18 5/8” casing shoe will be set around 10 to 30m inside this formation, the rest of Gachsaran formation will be drilled by 17 1/2” hole size to set 13 3/8” casing shoe inside Cap rock unit (8-10 m inside Cap Rock). The rest of Gachsaran interval will be drilled by 12 1/4” bit size.

3.4. Asmari Formation (from 2020 to 2401.5 m MD)

The Oligocene‐Miocene Asmari formation (About 381.5 m thickness) to be subdivided into several distinct stratigraphical units in this well. It is predicted that the top of Asmari formation is made by limestone and interbedded carbonate succession (Less than 25 m). Whilst, the upper part is mostly dominated by clastic packages including sandstones/siltstones beds (About 150 m thickness). The above‐mentioned sandy interval shows some interbedded gray marls, few dolomites and scattered brownish claystone layers. The relevant gray to light gray sandstones is essentially medium sorted, medium to coarse

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production

Operations Project

Well Drilling Program - JR-09

Doc. No: SJD4 DDRGED DRDR PLDR 9001 D01 Page 28 of 281

grain size and contain some ironic oxides such as pyrite. The interbedded claystone package is characterized by reddish to light brown color, soft and sticky form. The lower part of Asmari formation is again carbonated (About 75 m thickness) and essentially composed of light gray/gray dolomitic limestone to dolomite beds. The base of this formation is also characterized by thin layer sandstones that are directly located on the marly facies of the Pabdeh formation. Asmari formation will be drilled by 12 ¼” hole in Ilam new well.

3.5. Pabdeh Formation (from 2401.5 to 2651.5m MD)

Pabdeh formation (Paleocene‐Eocene age) is estimated to be about 245.5 m thick, in this well. This formation is expected to be subdivided into two (2) lithological units as well. The upper part consists of grey to dark‐brown argillaceous limestone and Limestone, accompanied with some interbedded marls and shale/ claystone. In terms of microfossil contents planktonic microfauna is dominant throughout the Pabdeh argillaceous intervals. This formation is mainly consisting of light grey, pale yellowish brown and rarely off-white moderate hard to hard argillaceous limestone with chert nodules (approximately 30% in 60-80 m interval). There are some interlayers of dark-brown argillaceous limestone beds. The 12 1/4” hole will be penetrated into this marly/ carbonate formation.

Note: In upper Pabdeh has water wet calaystone/Shale which can caved without sufficient mud material (KCl).

3.6. Gurpi Formation (from 2651.5 to 2974m MD)

The Gurpi formation (Campanian to Maastrichtian age) is estimated to be about 267 m thick and is also expected to be subdivided into three (3) stratigraphical units in this well, including Upper Gurpi, Tarbur Tongue and Lower Gurpi from top to the bottom of the formation respectively. The Upper Gurpi unit is mainly characterized by grey to dark‐brownish argillaceous limestone beds, which are assigned by abundant planktonic microfauna and noticeable clay contents. This interval is mostly composed of gray buff to gray, soft to medium hard, glauconitic to argillaceous limestone intervals with interbedded grey marls.

The middle part of Gurpi formation corresponds to a shallow marine carbonate stack that named as Tarbur Tongue. This particular carbonate interval was developed in the Sepehr‐Jufair area like other areas of Abadan Plain, which is commonly characterized by bioclastic limestone facies and shows huge accumulation of the large skeletal fragments such as bivalve debris. The Tarbur tongue is a cream to light gray in color, illustrating weak to moderate reservoir quality (Estimated based on nearby wells) and as with other parts of Abadan Plain, it also has economic oil-bearing intervals.

The Lower Gurpi unit is overlain directly by Tarbur limestone and shows so many similarities to the Upper Gurpi unit in terms of lithology and facies. The Lower Gurpi is mainly characterized by grey color argillaceous limestone facies (planktonic facies is dominant), which are interbedded by some grey color marly intervals.

In terms of drilling hazards, these units have not shown any particular hazards until now. The 12 1/4” and 8 ½” hole size will penetrate this marly/ carbonate formation.

3.7. Ilam Reservoir Formation (from 2974 to 4126m MD)

The Ilam formation (Santonian age), is expected to be drilled about 67 m thickness in this well, known as one of the main oil-bearing reservoir formations, extended predominantly in the Operation Area. Lithologically, the Ilam formation is essentially comprised of grey to brown limestone intervals, observed often with few interbedded marly to claystone beds (Rarely pyritic).

Therefore, the upper part of Ilam formation is characterized by an alternation between limestone/ dolomitic limestone beds and marly to claystone interlayers. The Upper Ilam carbonate interval shows fair reservoir quality in the Jufair area, accompanied with noticeable economic hydrocarbon volume (It is highly recommended to check this interval accurately).

The main reservoir body of Ilam formation, named Ilam-Main unit, producing economic oil in this area and essentially composed of mud-supported limestone facies with huge micro-porosity volumes. This carbonate stack is characterized by planktonic microfossils such as Oligosteginid and Globotruncanid families and accompanied with negligible clay contents.

The lower part, which named Ilam-Poor (In terms of low reservoir quality), corresponds to a small muddy limestone interval, overlying directly the Laffan unit and represents negligible hydrocarbon contents and mostly tightened or fully saturated by formation water. The main target of the Ilam wells is to produce from Ilam-Main unit (Il-IIIB: 3070.5m MD (-2937m TVDSS)) and II-AII, so the lower part of Ilam formation will not be penetrated. The 8 ½” hole sizes (As deviated well) and 6 1/8” (As horizontal leg- Ilam-Main) will penetrate this marly/ carbonate formation.

This hole was drilled from surface to the depth of 249 m, just penetrated into the near

top of Aghajari clastic/ marly formation. At the end of drilling of this hole, the 20”

casing was driven into the hole. The 20” casing shoe was set at the depth of 245 m

and then was cemented up. The used mud weight ranged from 65 to 68 pcf. No

specific problem has been reported in this hole.

This hole was drilled mostly inside the Aghajari clastic/marly formation. The drilling

mud weight was changed from 68 to 87 pcf. The hole was also penetrated into the

Mishan formation at the depth of 1366 m and continued down to the top of

Gachsaran formation with mud weight of 91 to 123 pcf. In addition, the topmost of

Gachsaran formation was also drilled at the depth of 1446 m. Drilling operation was

continued with gradual increasing of salt and this saturated mud weight increased up

to maximum 137 pcf. At the end of drilling operation, the required wireline logs

including BSC/CDR and GR were taken from the bottom hole to the depth of 245 m (by

CNLC Co.). The 13 3/8" casing shoe was set at the depth of 2001 m (Cap-Rock) and

then was cemented up (behind casing).

O peration Summary

This hole size was started from the upper part of Cap-Rock unit (salty-evaporate

interval) with 80 pcf mud weight, which was decreased abruptly from 137 to 80 pcf

(Figure 21). This hole was also penetrated into the Asmari clastic/carbonate formation

at the depth of 2010 m. The deeper formations including Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam and

Sarvak were drilled respectively by the same hole size. The used mud weight was

increased (ignorable) from 80 to 85 pcf, occurred at the bottom of the hole (3720 m).

The mud lost was recorded about 0 to 4 bbl/hr that was ignorable. At the end of

drilling operation, the required logs such as CDR, DSI, Image logs (FMI), CALI/GR

logs were acquired from 3251m to 2001m. In addition, the logs MDT/GR were run from

3232 m to 2900 m and totally forty-one (41) points from Ilam/Sarvak and three (3) oil

samples from Ilam formation were taken. At the end of this operation, the 9 5/8"

casing shoe was set at the depth of 3720 m and then was cemented up. The drilled

sequence consists of mainly limestone, argillaceous limestone, shale, dolomitic

limestone, sandstone, red to gray marls, cherty limestone, claystone, dolomite and

anhydrite beds, which are observed in the basal Gachsaran, Asmari, Pabdeh, Gurpi,

Ilam, Laffan, and Sarvak Formations respectively.

This hole was drilled from the basal Sarvak formation (about 3720 m) and then

continued into the Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan and Fahliyan formations respectively.

At the end of drilling operation, the required logs including CDR and full-set logs

were run. The used mud weight was started from 100 pcf (due to abnormal increasing

of pressure in the basal Sarvak/Top Kazhdumi formations) and then gradually

increased to 115 pcf, particularly within the pressurized Gadvan and Upper Fahliyan

intervals. The drilling operation was stopped due to coring plan that was taken from

the Lower Gadvan sandstones. In addition, the mud weight was increased up to 113

pcf. A complete core interval (from 4256 m to 4265.5 m) was taken from the sandstone

with 100% recovery. After coring operation, drilling was continued to the depth of

4402.5 m and then was stopped due to logging operation. The required logs including

HRI/SDL/CSNG/WSTT/GR and VSP were run by CNLC Co. In addition, MDT log was

run from depth of 4043 m to the bottom of the hole. After running the 7” liner, the

related liner shoe was set at the depth of 4616 m (Lower Fahliyan/Garau boundary)

and then was cemented up. The liner hanger was also set at the depth of 3606 m,

which is situated in the Lower Sarvak interval. 9 5/8" hole summary log in Well JR-04

is shown in Figure 22. The drilled lithology consists of mainly limestone, argillaceous

limestone, shale, dolomitic limestone, sandstone, gray marls and claystone in

Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan and Fahliyan Formations.

After the end of well test operation, it was decided to drill the deeper Jurassic layers.

Hence, drilling was continued in Garau formation with mud weight equal to 126 pcf

and 5 7/8” bit. Drilling of Garau and Gotnia formations was performed with 133-138 pcf

to 5361 m until the pipe stuck observed in this depth. After several attempts the pipes

got free and drilling was continued to 5385 m with 140 pcf. At the end of this hole

drilling, the 5" liner was run and related liner shoe was set at the depth of 5385 m and

cemented up.

After opening a window at 4435 m (KOP) directional drilling was performed to 4485 m.

The hole was completed as open hole condition and tested in terms of production

rate, representing economic oil and gas production. Drilling was continued to 4505 m.

Finally, after completing and securing, the drilling operation was finished in 2009.

The drilled lithologies consist of mainly limestone, argillaceous limestone, shale,

anhydrite, salt and sandstone in base of Fahliyan, Garau and Gotnia Formations.

3.10.4. Drilling Hazard in Nearby Wells

Over-Pressure

The formation pressure gradient in Gachsaran Formation reaches 152pcf based on the data of offset wells (JR-02). Precautions should be taken to prevent any well kick. Enough weighting material and kill mud must be stocked at rig site.
