Stuck casing due to hole cleaning, hole geometry, loss/flow or tight holeAvoid creating ledges by easing bit in harder formation and reaming transition between [[formations.Watch](http://formations.Watch)]([http://formations.Watch](http://formations.Watch)) casing string weight, understand and monitor casing drag up and down.Avoid thick mud cake by controlling fluid loss and solids.Circulate hole clean prior to POOH for casing Survey check.Bit BallingEntire bit and/or stabilizers, teeth balling and bottom balling can be reduced by having a sufficiently inhibitive mud.Entire bit Balling risk will be reduced by consistently high flow rates, and good hole cleaning.Ensure of pumping at high flow rates, and sufficient HSI (&amp;gt;2).With tri-cone bits, center jet and oriented nozzle will also aid preventing balling (oriented nozzle directs part of the flow onto the cutting structure).Avoid excessive WOB while drilling through Gachsaran formation.Actions once balling has been detected:• Bits can be cleared if balling is detected early enough and actions taken.• Reduce WOB when ROP drops, pick up bit off bottom as quickly as possible and increase flowrate.• Spin bit off bottom with high RPM and high flow rate for a period of time• Resume drilling with low weight• Prepare to pump pills (KCL solution pill), leave to soak and try to dissolve/loosen balled material

4.2. 17" Hole Section Potential Geological Hazard

Potential Hazard DescriptionChange in forecasted formation topsDue to seismic uncertainty and quality of interpretation, the forecasted formation tops may be changed which may cause several issues specially while entering Gachsaran formation.Tight Hole Tight intervals in Aghajari and Gachsaran increases risk of stuck pipe while running wireline tools, which may cause delay in wireline operation and event loss of tool.Abnormal PressureAbnormal pressure in Gachsaran.Possible encountering with the high-pressure packets in Gachsaran formation which cannot be detected by seismic data and nearby wells.Using high mud weight to mitigate risk of flow that can decrease the quality of logs.Fault and Natural FractureMay cause different issues such as mud loss, stuck pipe and unexpected high pressure.

4.3. 12 1/4" &amp;amp; 8 1/2" Hole Section Potential Drilling Hazard

Potential Hazard How to mitigateLoss circulationAsmari consists of porous limestone and dolomites providing very fast drilling. Asmari is a potential loss zone due to its high [[porosity.As](http://porosity.As)]([http://porosity.As](http://porosity.As)) losses have appeared, drilling with minimum parameter and sweep hole with High filter-loss LCM pill.Prepare to spot conventional LCM plugs.Shale instabilityPabdeh and Laffan Shales could be unstable at varying hole angles, although there are no apparent problems drilling it vertically.Raise mud density immediately if long slender pieces of Pabdeh or Laffan shale started coming over the shakers.Pabdeh and Laffan formations must be drilled with inhibited mud (mud weight must ensure stability even if severe losses encountered).The mud weight must minimize the risk of differentially stuck pipe when crossing the zones within the reservoir objective.

Differential stickingThere are several specialized “bridging “products that reduce seepage thereby reducing the likelihood of differential sticking in low permeability zones.Install string stabilizers within the drill string to ensure ‘stand-off from the wellbore.Ensure preventative drilling practices are strictly adhered to (i.e. moving and rotating drill-string as much as possible, minimizing length of unsterilized BHA, use of spiral Drill Collars and HWDP).Control water loss, minimize mud cake building tendency.Monitor filter cake quality.Use of Rotary Steerable Systems will minimize overall contact with the wellbore and will reduce the tendency for differential sticking.Solids removal equipment should be used with full performance and efficiencyTight holeMaintain Mud weight as plan Mud weight.Monitor mud rheology.Ensure sufficient inhibitor exist in mud system.Consider wiper trip if hole condition [[dictates.To](http://dictates.To)]([http://dictates.To](http://dictates.To)) minimize chances of stuck pipe, avoid pulling above 25 Klbs.Drill string corrosionInspect drill string regularly.Use corrosion inhibitor into mud system.Ledging and hole spiralingLedging can be an issue when drilling alternate hard and soft formations particularly at an angle. This can occur when drilling through the reservoir zones. Ledging occurs generally at the top of the harder formations at the interface when whirl or other lateral instability is induced due to the reduced depth of cut. This can be reduced or eliminated by following negative drill break practices and easing the bit into the harder formation.Poor weight transfer to the bit can also produce ledging and hole enlargement by reducing the depth of cut at the bit, thus initiating lateral instability and whirl.The higher the bend angle the more likely hole spiraling will occur. To overcome this problem a long gauge bit or turbo-back stabilizer can be used. Another method of reducing hole spiraling is to reduce the distance from bit face to bent [[housing.Review](http://housing.Review)]([http://housing.Review](http://housing.Review)) the offset wells for problems encountered.Poor hole cleaningHole angles between 45° and 65° present the most problems with drilled cuttings having a tendency to slide down the annulus and ‘pack off’. Hole angles greater than 65° do not present additional problems in this regard since the drilled cuttings are supported by sliding friction against the wellbore and become more stable as discrete cuttings beds. Use good hole cleaning practices to prevent formulation of cutting beds (Rotation, High GPM, Thin Sweeps. . .)Cement quality and cross flowUtilizing DV collar.QC cement and cement additives.Ensure applications and recording of Cement Quality Parameters (CQPs) evaluation.Follow up PEP’s cementing operation procedure.

5. Well Integrity Management Plan

Well Integrity is defined as the application of technical, operational and organizational solutions to reduce the risk of uncontrolled release of formation fluids to atmosphere or subsurface layers, throughout the life cycle of a well.

It will be responsibility of Senior Drilling &amp;amp; Completion Supervisor at wellsite and Drilling &amp;amp; Completion Superintendent in Tehran office to ensure the following certificates are prepared after each job carried out during the drilling and completion operations of the well and submitted to the respective drilling engineer for inclusion in the Integrity Management File for the well.

Moreover, a dedicated well integrity input report is generated in WELLVIEW which will pick up data entered in WELLVIEW during daily drilling and completion reports compilation. The senior drilling and completion supervisor shall ensure the proper filling of all the reports on daily basis. The following reports must be filled and sent to drilling engineer at the end of job

• Wellbore Sections

• Casing Strings (Casing Tally)

• Cementing Report

• Wellheads Information

• Formation Integrity Test Report (If applicable)

Note: For each test performed a well integrity certificate provided in below is to be filled.

10.Drilling Procedures

10.1.Rig Mobilization and Preparations to Spud

• Survey well location and access road in advance. Review site conditions with Company Witness.

• Apply moving rig by large modular as much as possible according to the conditions of access road

and well site, derrick, substructure, mud pump and other equipment shall be wholly moved.

• Move rig according to designed plan.

• Install equipment as required by the well site layout. The crown block, rotary table and wellhead

shall be aligned.

• The equipment, instrumentation and lighting system provided for the well site shall be explosion

proof.

• The total volumes of drilling fluid tanks shall not be less than 2400bbls.

• Before spud:

o Ensure all the drill string is inspected as per DS-1 Cat IV.

o Ensure all lifting gears are inspected appropriately pre-rig move.

o Prepare all the tools and materials as required, drift, measure and clean drill pipe before first

pick up.

o Record GL to RKB height on drilling report.

o Consult with E&amp;amp;P for wellhead valves orientation.

o Hold a pre-spud meeting. Ensure all parties are in attendance, all personnel are familiar with

their roles and responsibilities.

o Confirm Well control certificates and level for key personnel.

o All Well control equipment certified.

10.2. 36" Hole Section

10.2.1. General Information

The 36” interval will be drilled from surface to section TD at 100m, using Bentonite Mud for drilling and PHG as Hi-Vis Pill to assist in hole cleaning. At section TD the hole will be swept with 50bbl high viscosity pill followed by 150-200bbl viscous gel mud spotted on the bottom before the 26" casing is run.

Casing Point 26” Casing @ 100 mFormation Aghajari FormationRisks &amp;amp; Hole problems Rig Subbase Wash out / Erosion, Mud Loss, Almost Problem FreeDeviation Control TOTCOLogging N/ADrilling Fluid ParametersSpud MudMW (pcf) 67-68Vis. (sec/qt) &amp;gt;80PV (cp) -YP (lb./100ft²) &amp;gt;2510 Sec / 10 Min Gel (lb./100ft²) -API FL (ml/ 30min) NCPH 9.5 - 10.5Drilling ParametersGPM 300 - 900WOB (KLBs) 10 - 30RPM 80 - 100

10.2.2. Sequence of Operation

1. Check Pre-Spud Check List. Hold Pre – Job Safety Meeting.

2. Make up 26'' Bit as per BHA design. Tag formation at ±10.5 m.

Note:

▪ Ensure that all drilling tools and equipment are on well site and are in serviceable condition.

▪ Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this section of hole are available.

▪ Enough Mud Material, LCM and Cement Should be Available before spud the rig to use in case

of needing.

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production

Operations Project

Well Drilling Program - JR-09

Doc. No: SJD4 DDRGED DRDR PLDR 9001 D01 Page 67 of 281

▪ 1 Set cement pump truck should be available on well site before start drilling.

▪ Mud Logging unit should be available from rig spud.

3. Drill ahead formation down to 100 m (26” casing point in Aghajari formation) using hi-vis

bentonite pill. Pay enough attention to drill straight hole. Control flow rate and take care of wash

outs below rig sub base.

4. POOH to Surf, P/U 36" HO to enlarge the hole, RIH, Cont. enlarging hole to 100m.

Note:

▪ TD should be adjusted to have 2 m of rat hole below casing shoe.

▪ The exact TD will be determined based on casing tally.

▪ Run Survey to Check inclination @ 50 &amp;amp; 100 m (to ensure the deviation is below 1 degree)

5. At TD, Circulate and clean the hole. Observe the well. Perform Wiper Trip Prior to running casing.

Spot viscous mud @ TD. POOH to surface. Check Bit.

6. Perform Pre-Job Safety meeting (PJSM).

7. R/Up CSG/ Running Equipment.

8. Run 26" Casing 136.2# to 100 m with stinger shoe to bottom as per casing program. Casing shoe

should be adjusted to have 2 m of rat hole and enough stick up (1.5 m on rig floor). Fill casing by

non-LCM fresh mud.

Note:

▪ Do not exert much load and compressing stress on the shoe if encountered tight hole and

ledges.

▪ Make sure that 2 No. of 2” nipple had been welded on conductor and it is plugged w/ a quick

union low pressure plug.

▪ Don’t exceed 80% of collapse rating pressure of casing while pumping (200 psi).

9. Run stinger on 5" DP’s using the “C” Plate and 5” x 26” centralizer. Sting in. M/U &amp;amp; test

cementing lines. Circulate for 1.2 or till shaker clean volume. While circulating, check the DPs

annulus for any return. Use all DPs weight on the string if observing any minor leakage through

DPs annulus.

10. Cement casing as per program. Any minor adjustment regarding the corrected depth will be

done in due time. Displace with mud (1-2 bbl. Short Displace). Monitor the pressures. Record

and report the final pressure, Sting out. Check the float. POOH one stand, Circulate to

flush/clean drill pipe. POOH to surface. L/D Stinger While W.O.C to Get Hard, perform top Job If

Needed.

Note:

▪ Based on the results obtained from cementing, decision will be made to perform top-up jobs

While W.O.C to Get Hard.

11. After cement returns to cellar floor, open the 2" nipple on conductor &amp;amp; flush it.

12. If there is no cement return to surface, a top-up job should be performed to fill the annulus. Use

same slurry weight as the primary cement slurry. The cement should be accelerated with max.

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production

Operations Project

Well Drilling Program - JR-09

Doc. No: SJD4 DDRGED DRDR PLDR 9001 D01 Page 68 of 281

(2%) Calcium Chloride BWOC and no other additives. Wait for the top job cement to get hard.

13. Slack Off Weight. Check Cement by slack off weight and check for any movement.

14. Rough Cut 26" Casing, Dress &amp;amp; Bevel Casing Neck. Prepare and Install 29-1/2'' Flange (Locking

flange). Check Cement by slack off weight. Check for any movement.

15. N/U BOP (29-1/2" Diverter- 500 psi) Bell Nipple &amp;amp; flow line and Related Lines &amp;amp; Valves.

16. Perform diverter function Test.

17. P/U Next BHA and Stand Back 5" DP's as needed.

18. RIH W/ New BHA and 24" Bit #1 (1-1-5) to Tag Shoe, Drill Out Shoe &amp;amp; cement below shoe.

10.2.3. Potential Risks of the Section

Potential Risks How to MitigateWash out below the conductor• Controlled drilling parameters first 30m under the conductor shoe.• Control the mud properties as per the program.• Control flow rateLost Circulation• Continuous monitoring mud returns and volume on tanks.• Sufficient circulation to ensure good hole cleaning and avoid annulus overloading.• Sweep hole clean with hi-vis pill.Bit Balling• Sweep the cuttings regularly with Hi-vis pill.• Control drilling parameters, max FR and HSI on the bit to keep bottom holeclean of cuttings.• Pull the bit off bottom,rotating with high RPM

Table 10: Potential Risk of 36" Hole Section

▪ Hole caving, deviation and stuck pipe are commonly potential hazards in drilling this section.

Precaution for caving, deviation and stuck pipe:

• Viscous mud will be used.

• Pendulum BHA is utilized to prevent hole deviation.

• Ream and back ream each single/stand prior to making a connection.

10.3. 24" Hole Section

10.3.1. General Information

This section will be drilled from 100 m at 26” casing shoe to ±1500 m through AGHAJARI, MISHAN and 10 to 30m in GACHSARAN #7 formation as section TD. The section will be drilled with Bentonite mud receiving from previous section to ±700m then the well will be displaced with KCL / PHPA / Salt Polymer Mud and continued to section TD. The 18 5/8" casing is run to TD to provide a barrier for drilling through the Gachsaran formation.

10.3.2. Sequence of Operation

1. After D/O of 26'' Casing shoe and Cement Below Shoe, drilling 24" Hole to 103 m with 24" Bit #1

would be done.

2. Circulate &amp;amp; Clean the Hole. Adjust bentonite mud weight and circulate to have unified mud in

hole.

3. Cont. Drilling 24" Hole till stabilizer below the Casing Shoe, with reduced drilling parameter.

Note:

For the first run, only one stabilizer will be used till stabilizer below the casing shoe.

4. POOH to Surface to change BHA, P/U &amp;amp; M/U pack hole assembly (w/2 Stabilizer), RIH to BTM.

5. Drilling 24" Hole to 423 m or Bit Life.

6. CBU, Run TOTCO Survey. POOH, Change bit, RIH W/24'' Bit #2 (If required).

7. Cont. Drilling 24" Hole to 723 m.

8. CBU, Run TOTCO Survey. POOH, Change bit (to PDC Bit), RIH W/24'' Bit #3.

9. Circulate and Clean the Hole. Adjust new mud weight (Salt/KCl/PHPA/Polymer) and displace the

hole with new mud.

Note:

Due to limitation of surface volume, maybe it needed to displace to new mud at 400 m Depth. It will be decided at due time based on the situation.

10. Continue Drilling 24" Hole to 1500 m. (section TD) CBU, Drop TOTCO Survey.

11. Perform Condition Trip Prior to Logging. POOH and L/D Bit

▪ Note any tight spots or overpull on DDR, wipe out any tight spots. Circulate hole clean &amp;amp;

POOH, Conduct flow check while POOH and ensure well stable prior to performing wireline

logging.

12. Run Well Survey log (CDR or Gyro)/GR.

▪ Drilling fluid will be conditioned per the hole situation after logging. If some more fill was

detected after logging, then more anti-caving agent will be added into fluid system. If tight

hole encountered, then the MW should be increased a little more.

13. Perform PJSM.

14. Rig Up Casing Running Equipment. Run 18 5/8" Casing to 1500 m.

▪ Monitor hook loads during running of the casing to detect excessive drag.

▪ Tag bottom to confirm casing setting depth.

15. Perform cement job for 18 5/8” Casing using cement plug.

Note:

In case of no bumping during cement job, CIT should be done before drilling shoe track.

16. W.O.C to Get Hard, perform top Job If Needed.

17. Slack off Weight, Check for pipe movement. Rough Cut 26" Casing &amp;amp; Lay Down Landing Joint,

Remove Landing Flange.

18. Rough Cut 18 5/8" casing, Dress &amp;amp; Bevel Casing Neck, Install C.H.H 18 5/8'' Slip lock on casing *

20-3/4" 3K &amp;amp; DSA Locking Tie down Flange. Test the same.

19. N/U 20-3/4" 3K BOP's Stack. Meanwhile Perform Top job if Required, BOP Test as NIOC Policy.

20. P/U Next BHA as per plan and Stand DP's as needed.

21. RIH W/ New BHA and 17" R. Bit #1. Drill out Shoe track &amp;amp; CMT below shoe. Monitor closely and

Report Drill out Parameters.

10.3.3. Preventive Measures

▪ This section may experience formation cave-in and bit balling, which ultimately may affect

wellbore stability and cementing quality. Control 3-5% KCl and the concentration will be

increased as hole dictate to avoid bit balling and cave-in.

▪ If observe high Torque fluctuation or vibration at surface, the driller should do drill off test to

choose proper RPM to relax the BHA vibration.

▪ On the bottom of Aghajari and Mishan formation will encounter Red Marl and gradually

increased till reach to top of Gachsaran, which may lead to bit balling and tight hole, short trip

per 200m to eliminate the tight hole. Increase MW and control the mud properties as per the

Drilling Fluid program.

▪ Wiper trip to the casing shoe (if hard back reaming, POOH to surface to change Tri-Cone bit),

RIH, ream any tight spot, then RIH to TD, circulate and condition the mud for RIH casing, Pump

Hi-Vis at bottom if required.

▪ Before connection, back ream and ream down at least one time to check the hole is in good

shape and then make connection.

▪ To prevent overloading the annulus, keep a controlled ROP.

▪ Ream any tight spots until the section is clean prior to making connections. Note pick up and

slack off weight of drill string to identify any abnormal increase in drag and friction.

▪ Pump Hi-Vis mud, sweeps per three stands to clean the hole as soon as possible.

10.3.4. 18 5/8" Casing Running/Cementing Preparation

▪ 18 5/8" Casing Running &amp;amp; Cementing Program will be issued separately.

▪ Use API Drift to verify the drift of every joint of casing prior to running. The DS shall physically

check and confirm the OD of the casing drift. Any joints that cannot be drifted should be clearly

marked and set aside.

▪ Measure the casing at least 2 times to confirm the casing tally's accuracy. Clean and inspection

all the threads.

▪ Double check the float collar, float shoe, confirm the floats in good work condition.

▪ Install the casing centralizers as per the final Casing Running &amp;amp; Cementing Program.

▪ After Visual Thread Inspection (VTI) is completed and measured for pipe tally, apply API

modified thread compound and install the protectors hand tight.

▪ Ensure all casing running equipment has valid certificates and address the lessons learned

from the previous casing running in Sepehr-Jufair Oil Field.

▪ All BTC casing shall be made up to the base of the triangle.

▪ Circulate and wash down the last joint of casing and tag bottom lightly.

This section will be drilled from 1500 m at 18 5/8” casing shoe to ± 2000 m through GACHSARAN members until inside Cap Rock GACHSARAN member (8-10m inside cap rock) as section TD. The section will be drilled with a new build Salt Saturated Mud to section TD.

10.4.2. Sequence of Operation

1. After D/O of 18 5/8'' Casing shoe and Cement below Shoe, work bit through the shoe track

interval several times with or without rotation, pull the bit into shoe, Perform FIT w/137 pcf

equivalent MW, Resume Drilling Formation to 1505 m with 17" Bit #1.

2. Circulate, Clean the Hole, Condition Mud &amp;amp; work on Junk Sub, POOH to Surf.

3. P/U New Bit &amp;amp; Drilling BHA (17" PDC BIT #2 &amp;amp; New BHA), RIH to Bottom.

4. Drilling to 1520 m with reduced parameter till stabilizer below the Casing Shoe.

5. Cont. Drill 17" Hole to 2000 m (section TD), (While Increase MW. Stepwise as Program &amp;amp; based

on hole condition).

6. Run Survey Each 300 m Drilled.

7. Perform Condition TRIP Prior to Logging, C.B.U @ BTM, POOH and L/D Bit.

▪ Note any tight spots or overpull on DDR, wipe out any tight spots. Circulate hole clean &amp;amp;

POOH, Conduct flow check while POOH and ensure well stable prior to performing wireline

logging.

8. Test BOP Stack and all Related Lines as NIOC POLICY.

9. R/Up Logging Tools , Run (CDR or Gyro)/GR/FIR

10. Perform Condition TRIP Prior to Run Casing. perform wiper trip to shoe and observe well @

shoe. Spot 100 bbl. hi-vis pill @ bottom.

11. Perform PJSM.

12. Rig Up Casing Running Equipment. Run 13-3/8" &amp;amp; 13-5/8” Casing to 2000 m.

13. Circulate 1.2 casing volume &amp;amp; perform Cement job as Per Program.

Note: In case of no bumping during cement job, CIT should be done before drilling shoe track.

14. Set the 13-3/8" Casing hanger, Slack off Weight, Check for pipe movement. N/D BOP's, Rough

Cut and L/D Landing Joint. Dress &amp;amp; bevel casing neck.

15. Install C.H.S. 20-3/4" 3K BTM * 13-5/8" 5K TOP, &amp;amp; Adaptor Flange 13 5/8'' 5K BTM - 5K TOP. Test

P-Seal and cavity w/max 80% collapse pressure.

16. N/U 13-5/8" 5K BOP's Stack.

17. Test BOP Stack and all Related Lines as NIOC POLICY.

10.4.3. Preventive Measures

▪ If observe high Torque fluctuation or vibration at surface, the driller should do drill off test to

choose proper RPM to relax the BHA vibration.

▪ Wiper trip to the casing shoe (if hard back reaming, POOH to surface to change Tri-Cone bit), RIH,

ream any tight spot, then RIH to TD, circulate and condition the mud for RIH casing, Pump Hi-Vis

at bottom if required.

▪ The Gachsaran formation contains Anhydrite which interbedded with gray to red Marl and Salt,

which may lead to tight spots or tight hole, hard back reaming.

▪ Ream any tight spots until the section is clear prior to making connections. Note P/U and S/O

weight of string.

▪ It's necessary to flow check prior to POOH, reach the casing shoe and before BHA enter BOPs.

▪ Enough weighting material and kill mud must be stocked on rig site.

▪ BOP drill should be performed on location as policy.

▪ Carefully watch pit level and monito MW of flow line. Control tripping speed to avoid swabbing

and surging. Condition the mud as per drilling program and hole conditions.

10.4.4. 13 3/8" – 13 5/8" Casing Running/Cementing Preparation

▪ 13 3/8" x 13 5/8" Casing Running &amp;amp; Cementing Program will be issued separately.

▪ Use 12.25" Drift to verify the drift of every joint of casing prior to running. The DS shall physically

check and confirm the OD of the casing drift. Any joints that cannot be drifted should be clearly

marked and set aside

▪ Measure the casing at least 2 times to confirm the casing tally's accuracy. Clean and inspection all

the threads.

▪ Double check the float collar, float shoe, confirm the floats in good work condition.

▪ Install the casing centralizers as per the final Casing Running &amp;amp; Cementing Program.

▪ After Visual Thread Inspection (VTI) is completed and measured for pipe tally, apply API modified

thread compound and install the protectors hand tight.

▪ Ensure all casing running equipment has valid certificates and address the lessons learned from

the previous casing running in Sepehr-Jufair Oil Field.

▪ Circulate and wash down the last joint of casing and tag bottom lightly.

▪ Check casing tally against the casing shoe depth desired. The casing shoe should be set at 1-2m

off bottom.

▪ During all the running casing operation, the volume of the flow back and the volume of the casing

run into the hole shall be observed and record in the trip sheet.

▪ Circulate one bottom to up at least 2 bottoms up or until hole clean. Monitor returns for losses.

10.5.3. Preventive Measures

▪ If observe high Torque fluctuation or vibration at surface, the driller should do drill off test to

choose proper RPM to relax the BHA vibration.

▪ Wiper trip to the casing shoe (if hard back reaming, POOH to surface to change Tri-Cone bit), RIH,

ream any tight spot, then RIH to TD, circulate and condition the mud for RIH casing, Pump Hi-Vis

at bottom if required.

▪ Ream any tight spots until the section is clear prior to making connections. Note P/U and S/O

weight of string.

▪ It's necessary to flow check prior to POOH, reach the casing shoe and before BHA enter BOPs.

▪ Wiper trip according to wellbore condition and tight spot indication.

▪ During drilling this hole section tight hole or caving may occur, leading to pack off/pipe stuck.

▪ According to actual condition, if necessary, spot HVP to sweep the hole.

▪ Reduce time for connections stop, check for mud weight, jar should be in good condition, drillers

should vigilant, ream and back ream to confirm the string is free before making connection.

▪ Make any effort to clean hole for reducing ECD to avoid lost circulation.

▪ Avoid excessive circulation rates and pump surge.

▪ Employ thin mud. Maintaining a low yield point is particularly important to reduce the ECD in the

annulus. Use mud with minimal gel strength.

▪ Rotate and reciprocate pipe slowly before starting to circulate (breaking circulation). Then break

circulation by starting pump slowly as drill pipe is raised.

▪ Run in hole slowly to avoid any sudden movement. Do not exceed calculated surge pressure or

pipe running speed.

▪ 7" Liner Running &amp;amp; Cementing Program will be issued separately.

▪ Use 6.125" Drift to verify the drift of every joint of liner prior to running. The DS shall physically

check and confirm the OD of the drift. Any joints that cannot be drifted should be clearly marked

and set aside

▪ Measure the liner at least 2 times to confirm the liner tally's accuracy. Clean and inspection all the

threads.

▪ Double check the LDC, float collar, float shoe, confirm the floats in good work condition.

▪ Install the centralizers as per the final Liner Running &amp;amp; Cementing Program.

▪ After Visual Thread Inspection (VTI) is completed and measured for pipe tally, apply API modified

thread compound and install the protectors hand tight.

▪ Ensure all liner running equipment has valid certificates and address the lessons learned from the

previous liner running in Sepehr-Jufair Oil Field.

▪ Check tally against the shoe depth desired. The shoe should be set at 0.5 - 1m off bottom.

▪ During all the running liner operation, the volume of the flow back and the volume of the string

run into the hole shall be observed and record in the trip sheet.

▪ Circulate one bottom to up or until hole clean. Monitor returns for losses.

▪ Chloride and Calcium content in the water to be used for spacer and the slurry should be checked

ahead of job.

▪ Condition mud property while circulation before performing cement job.

▪ Make sure that the shale shaker is clean of cutting and MW in = MW out.

▪ Rig pump efficiency to be checked accurately by the DS together with the cementing engineer

before the job and reported in DDR.

10.7.3. Preventive Measure

▪ Ream any tight spots until the section is clear prior to making connections. Note P/U and S/O

weight of string.

▪ It's necessary to flow check prior to POOH, reach the casing shoe and before BHA enter BOPs.

▪ Wiper trip according to wellbore condition and tight spot indication.

▪ During drilling this hole section tight hole or caving may occur, leading to pack off/pipe stuck.

▪ According to actual condition, if necessary, spot HVP to sweep the hole.

▪ Reduce time for connections stop, check for mud weight, jar should be in good condition, drillers

should vigilant, ream and back ream to confirm the string is free before making connection.

▪ Make any effort to clean hole for reducing ECD to avoid lost circulation.

▪ Avoid excessive circulation rates and pump surge.

▪ Employ thin mud. Maintaining a low yield point is particularly important to reduce the ECD in the

annulus. Use mud with minimal gel strength.

▪ Rotate and reciprocate pipe slowly before starting to circulate (breaking circulation). Then break

circulation by starting pump slowly as drill pipe is raised.

▪ Run in hole slowly to avoid any sudden movement. Do not exceed calculated surge pressure or

pipe running speed.

▪ Drilling fluid will be conditioned per the hole situation after logging. If some more fill was detected

after logging, then more anti-caving agent will be added into fluid system. If tight hole

encountered, then the MW should be increased a little more. In addition, the lubricant and

torque-less should be added into fluid system to reduce friction.

This section will be drilled to ±100m through AGHAJARI formation, and it contains the red marl and clay with a thin bed of sandstone also occasionally trace of Gypsum.

PHG pill will be used to clean the hole and since Bentonite has the best cake around the wellbore, it will make a good cake for hole stability.

While drilling, the lime will be used to control pH and in order to disperse the formation clay.

If drilling water has the chloride concentration of more than 1000 mg/Lit, Bentonite will not be hydrated well and Xanthan Gum will be used to increase Rheology along with Bentonite.

Drilling fluid density will be controlled around 67-68pcf. Use available solids control equipment to reduce low gravity solids build-up, thus reducing any dilution requirements for density control. Mud weight to be adjusted as hole conditions dictate.

At the beginning of the drilling for the first 20 meters of the drilling, due to prevent the rig subbase washout, the mud viscosity must be around 60-70 sec/qt. Then viscosity must be decreased to 40 - 50 sec/qt. in order to prevent overflow from shakers.

Yield Point of the Bentonite Mud to be maintained more than 25-40 lb./100ft2 for the first 20m due to prevent the rig subbase washout. After drilling 20m, the Yield Point of Bentonite Mud between 18- 28 lb./100ft2 is enough for sufficient hole cleaning. The Yield Point of PHG between 30-40 lb./100ft2 is enough for sufficient hole cleaning. Plastic viscosity should be maintained as low as possible by extensive use of solids control equipment, coupled with whole new mud dilution.

During normal drilling operations, pH should be kept 10-11. This will maximize chemicals performance and minimize corrosion problems. The pH will be adjusted with caustic soda for fresh mud. While

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production

Operations Project

Well Drilling Program - JR-09

Doc. No: SJD4 DDRGED DRDR PLDR 9001 D01 Page 185 of 281

drilling the pH will be adjusted with the lime (1-2ppb) for controlling of the formation clay dispersion and prevent mud Rheology build up.

Total hardness should be maintained below 600 mg/L with the addition of Soda Ash and/or Caustic Soda.

Measuring the MBT is the direct indication of Clay formation reactivity. MBT doesn’t need to be controlled in this hole section when Bentonite mud designed as this section DF system.

All SCE should be function tested and repaired as necessary prior to spud the well. Dress Shakers with 60 - 80 and mud cleaner with 140 – 175 mesh size screens. Ensure shakers are running immediately prior to and during all periods of circulation. Use all the solids control equipment available on the rig site.

Drilling Issues

In case of stuck pipe, 50bbl of un‐weighted PIPE LAX pill at 3.5‐4.5 gal/bbl. of diesel can be pumped down to the string and every 10min 5bbl spotted around the stuck area while working on the string.

Cleaning cuttings from a vertical hole has been covered extensively by numerous investigators. Hole cleaning in a vertical hole is essentially a matter of overcoming the slip velocity of the cuttings with sufficient annular velocity and carrying capacity of the drilling fluid. Although any velocity greater than the settling velocity of the largest cutting will theoretically lift all the cuttings to surface eventually, too low an annular velocity will lead to an undesirable high concentration of cuttings in the annulus. Experience has shown that cuttings concentrations more than 5% by volume cause tight hole or stuck pipe when circulation is stopped.

The driving parameter that shows the hole cleaning is the 6 and 3 RPM readings. The 6 reading has to be over 8 all time to ensure good hole cleaning. 30bbl of Hi-Vis Bentonite pill must be pumped every drilled stand and circulated out of the hole prior to connecting the next stand.

In case of high torque &amp;amp; drag, LUBRICANT or diesel would be used at 1 ‐ 2% by volume.

It is recommended to prevent the bit balling phenomenon by pumping periodically anti-bit balling pills:

• LIGNOSULFONATE Brine as Low Vis Pill

1. Fill up a pit with required drill water.

2. Add NACL and adjust mud weight for 67 to 68pcf as per current mud in the hole.

3. Add 5 ppb of LIGNOSULFONATE.

4. Add 0.2 ppb of Xanthan Gum to raise the viscosity above 30 – 32 sec/qt.

5. Add 5 ppb of Walnut Shell (F) + 5 ppb of Walnut Shell (M).

• Hi Vis Pill

1. Fill up a pit with required volume of current mud in the hole.

2. Add 3 ppb of Xanthan Gum to raise the viscosity between 80 to 90 sec/qt.

• Hi Vis Pill

• Pumping Procedure

1. Pumped 50bbl of LIGNOSULFONATE Brine or Lime Brine as low viscous pill.

2. Pumped 50bbl of Xanthan Gum Hi Vis Pill.

3. Pumped down until LIGNOSULFONATE Brine or Lime Brine come out the bit.

4. While keep the bit 1m off bottom, jerking the string, increase the RPM to the maximum

possible.

As it is seen in geological forecast, soft &amp;amp; sticky marls referred as Gumbo, contained large amount of SMECTITE and/or ILLITE could be associated with problems such as bit balling, mud rings, plugged flow lines and hole washout &amp;amp; cause low process of drilling and unnecessary trips and some more difficulties to drill the section as fast as possible.

The formation fluid influx could affect the mud system without a sign of an increase in the mud volume which necessitates mud weight increase. The major sign of this influx is the increase in the hardness and decrease in the pH.

The PHPA will be added to the system after 2 mud cycles, when the mud is warm enough gradually from 0.25ppb to 1ppb in order to prevent shakers overflow. The concentration must be maintained while drilling because this chemical goes out of the system by the cuttings.

At this system uses Salt as the source of density, salinity and Clay inhibition in the system. When mud weight reaches 80pcf the solution must be built as a saturated solution then increase mud weight to the desired value. While drilling to section TD the mud weight will be increase gradually as per plan or hole dictation to 89pcf by Barite as weighting agent. Use available solids control equipment to reduce low gravity solids build-up, thus reducing any dilution requirements for density control. The provision of keeping on the reserve pits, sufficient quantity of heavy mud as kill mud should be considered. This will help to prompt increasing mud weight in the shortest time.

Yield Point of the Bentonite Mud to be maintained between 18-28 lb./100ft2 which is enough for sufficient hole cleaning. While drilling this section with Polymer Mud, XC Polymer will be used as base of rheology to extend hole cleaning and providing suitable YP and LSRV. Yield Point to be maintained at a range of 14-20 lb./100ft2. Plastic viscosity should be maintained as low as possible by extensive use of solids control equipment, coupled with new mud dilution.

Due to drilling long sections in Marl and Clay formations, full consideration must be taken on Rheology to be in the range in order to prevent shooting up Rheology. Increasing in the Rheology will made further problems such as shaker overflow, increasing in the MW, hole washout, and SPP.

While drilling to 700m with Bentonite Mud the fluid loss will not be controlled. After displacing, the hole with Salt Polymer Mud the fluid loss will be controlled gradually below 10 cc/30min and gradually will be decreased to below 5 cc/30min by section TD. Fluid loss will be kept under control by the addition of polymeric chemicals such as, Starch.

While drilling with Bentonite Mud the pH will be kept at 10-11 in order to have Rheology in the range and prevent of formation's Clay from flocculating. While drilling with Salt Polymer mud the pH will be maintained 9.5-10. to achieve the mentioned subject, the pH will be adjusted with caustic soda for fresh mud and while drilling the pH will be adjusted by Lime (1-2ppb) for controlling the formation's clay dispersion and prevent mud Rheology build up.

Total hardness should be maintained below 1,200 mg/L with the addition of Soda Ash and/or Caustic Soda. While drilling this section encounter with Ca2+ based Gypsum is inevitable. Gypsum is calcium sulfate with water of crystallization (CaSO4.2H2O), Calcium sulfate contamination is similar to cement contamination because both liberate calcium ions, which in turn cause flocculation. The sulfate ion

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production

Operations Project

Well Drilling Program - JR-09

Doc. No: SJD4 DDRGED DRDR PLDR 9001 D01 Page 191 of 281

contributes to the flocculation of clay solids, although its effect is small compared to calcium ions. The severity of flocculation depends to a great degree on clay content. When CaSO4 causes the calcium concentration to increase and viscosity may fluctuate drastically. As calcium ion concentrations further increase, a base exchange occurs in which sodium montmorillonite becomes calcium montmorillonite. There are several methods for handling CaSO4 contamination. The drilling fluid can be maintained as a low-calcium fluid by chemically precipitating by adding soda ash.

Measuring the MBT is the direct indication of Clay formation reactivity. MBT doesn’t need to be controlled in this hole section when Bentonite mud designed as this section DF system. After displacing the hole to Salt Polymer mud the MBT must be controlled below 15 ppb by utilizing all solids control equipment and mud dilution.

All SCE should be function tested and maintained as necessary prior to starts the section. Dress Shakers with 100-140 mesh size screen and mud cleaner with 170 - 200. Ensure shakers are running immediately prior to and during all periods of circulation. Use all the solids control equipment available on the rig site.

Centrifuges must be run immediately after starting drilling as the ROP is high in this section and there is no sufficient time to discard undesirable solids after the build-up. After adding the Barite to the mud system, the centrifuges must be run as the Barite recovery system in order to keep Barite in the system for saving cost and well control purposed.

Drilling Issues

In case of stuck pipe, 50bbl of un‐weighted PIPE LAX pill at 3.5‐4.5 gal/bbl. of diesel can be pumped down to the string and every 10min 5bbl spotted around the stuck area while working on the string.

Hole cleaning in a vertical hole is essentially a matter of overcoming the slip velocity of the cuttings with sufficient annular velocity and carrying capacity of the drilling fluid. Although any velocity greater than the settling velocity of the largest cutting will theoretically lift all the cuttings to surface eventually, too low an annular velocity will lead to an undesirable high concentration of cuttings in the annulus. Experience has shown that cuttings concentrations more than 5% by volume cause tight hole or stuck pipe when circulation is stopped.

The driving parameter that shows the hole cleaning is the 6 and 3 RPM readings. The 6 reading has to be over 6 all time to ensure good hole cleaning. 30bbl of Hi-Vis Bentonite pill must be pumped every drilled stand and circulated out of the hole prior to connecting the next stand while drilling with the Bentonite Mud and 30bbl of Hi-Vis of Salt Polymer Mud build with Xanthan Gum while drilling with the Salt Polymer Mud.

Prior to tripping, if any concern exists in regard to hole cleanliness, consideration should be given to pumping a high weight pill while on bottom. This is especially important if no pills have been pumped during the section drilled. Returns of all such pills at the shakers should be monitored to gauge their effectiveness. Care should be exercised to ensure that excessive amounts of high-density pills are not

pumped due to their effect on hydrostatic head. In the case of all pills do not stop or reduce the circulation rate before the pill(s) have been evacuated from hole. To do so will result in material dropping out of the pill. Circulation should continue if solids are still coming over the shakers.

Before POOH for casing running follow below procedure:

• Prepare 300 bbl. (it is not included dead volume) FL controlled pill (FL&amp;lt;3)

• Pill weight should 2pcf upper from system weight

• Spot 300 bbl. of this pill at bottom

In case of high torque &amp;amp; drag, LUBRICANT or diesel would be used at 1 ‐ 2% by volume.

It is recommended to prevent the bit balling phenomenon by pumping periodically anti-bit balling pills:

• LIGNOSULFONATE Brine as Low Vis Pill

1. Fill up a pit with required drill water.

2. Add NACL and adjust mud weight for 67 to 68pcf as per current mud in the hole.

3. Add 5 ppb of LIGNOSULFONATE.

4. Add 0.2 ppb of Xanthan Gum to raise the viscosity above 30 – 32 sec/qt.

5. Add 5 ppb of Walnut Shell (F) + 5 ppb of Walnut Shell (M).

• Hi Vis Pill

1. Fill up a pit with required volume of current mud in the hole.

2. Add 3 ppb of Xanthan Gum to raise the viscosity between 80 to 90 sec/qt.

OR

• Lime Brine as Low Vis Pill

1. Fill up a pit with required drill water.

2. Add NACL and adjust mud weight for 67 to 68pcf as per current mud in the hole.

3. Add 5 ppb of Lime.

• Hi Vis Pill

1. Fill up a pit with required volume of current mud in the hole.

2. Add 3 ppb of Xanthan Gum to raise the viscosity between 80 to 90 sec/qt.

• Pumping Procedure

1. Pumped 50bbl of LIGNOSULFONATE Brine or Lime Brine as low viscous pill.

2. Pumped 50bbl of Xanthan Gum Hi Vis Pill.

3. Pumped down until LIGNOSULFONATE Brine or Lime Brine come out the bit.

4. While keep the bit 1m off bottom, jerking the string, increase the RPM to the maximum

possible.

After drilling the cement inside the casing and before drill out the shoe track with carried mud from previous section the old Salt Polymer Mud will be displaced with new 120pcf fresh Salt Saturated Mud to drilling this hole section.

Saturated Salt Muds are primarily used to prevent excessive hole enlargement while drilling massive salt beds. They can also be used to reduce the dispersion and hydration of shales and clays.

The chloride content of saturated salt muds is 188,000 mg/l at saturation. As the temperature of the mud increases, more salt is able to go into the solution. This means that a fluid which is saturated under surface conditions may not be saturated in downhole temperatures and can cause substantial washout in a salt zone due to increased salt solubility.

At this system uses Salt as the source of density, salinity and Clay inhibition in the system. Salt saturated solution must be used to build the mud for this section. While drilling to section TD the mud weight will be increase gradually as per plan or hole dictation from 120pcf to 137pcf by Barite and FerO-Bar as a weighting agent. The Fer-O-Bar will be used from 125pcf to desired mud weight with a ratio of 3:1 Barite / Fer-O-Bar. Use available solids control equipment to reduce low gravity solids build-up, thus reducing any dilution requirements for density control. The provision of keeping on the reserve pits, a sufficient quantity of heavy mud as kill mud should be considered. This will help to prompt increasing mud weight in the shortest time.

While mixing heavy mud of this section, the XC Polymer will not be used at all or used only 0.2 ppb as the base of rheology to provide the suitable YP and LSRV for suspending weighting agent materials. Yield Point to be maintained at a range of 16-30 lb./100ft2 while drilling with Salt Saturated Mud to have sufficient hole cleaning. Plastic viscosity should be maintained as low as possible by extensive use of solids control equipment, coupled with new mud dilution.

Due to drilling Marl and Clay formations, full consideration must be taken on Rheology to be in the range in order to prevent shooting up Rheology. Increasing the Rheology will made further problems such as shaker overflow, increase in the MW, hole washout, and SPP.

While drilling the hole with Salt Saturated Mud the fluid loss will be controlled below 3 cc/30min to section TD. Fluid loss will be kept under control by the addition of Starch LV.

While drilling pH will be kept at 9-10 in order to have Rheology in the range and prevent of formation's Clay from flocculating. To achieve the mentioned subject, the pH will be adjusted with caustic soda for fresh mud and while drilling the pH will be adjusted by Lime (1-2ppb) for controlling the formation's clay dispersion and prevent mud Rheology build up.

Foaming is generally restricted to surface foam and is not troublesome unless aggravated by mechanical agitation. The degree of foaming may sometimes be decreased by increasing the alkalinity of the mud (Pm). A De-foaming agent may be necessary. Unless Mg++ sensitive additives are used, a Saturated Salt Mud is less prone to foam and air cut with a 9.5-10 pH.

Control of the pH of saturated salt muds varies widely. Saturated salt muds require larger additions of caustic soda to maintain a pH in Salt Saturate Muds. Maintaining an ± 9.5 pH offers several advantages:

• De flocculants are more effective

• Corrosion is reduced

• Lower concentrations of filtration control additives are required when Ca++ and Mg++ solubility

is reduced

• Foaming tendency is lessened

• Mud is generally more stable

Total hardness should be maintained below 1,300 mg/L with the addition of Soda Ash and/or Caustic Soda. while drilling this section encounter with Ca2+ based Anhydrite is inevitable. There are several methods for handling CaSO4 contamination. The drilling fluid can be maintained as a low-calcium fluid by chemically precipitating by adding soda ash.

Saturated salt muds will normally contain soluble calcium due to the formations penetrated and the type of makeup water used. In addition, the sodium ions from the salt will undergo a base exchange and release calcium ions from the clay platelets, thereby contributing to the free calcium. Generally, the presence of calcium does not produce detrimental effects on the mud; except when the pH is increased beyond 12.0 and then the fluid loss will be difficult to control.

Ca++ and Mg++ hardness less than 1500 mg/lt do not adversely affect filtration control in Saturated Salt Muds when using starch, however, the hardness of the system will be maintained below 1300 mg/lt by using Soda Ash, Caustic, and dilution.

The MBT must be controlled below 7.5 ppb by utilizing all solids control equipment and mud dilution in order to have stability in the mud.

The fluid for this section is one designed to give proper inhibition to the formations to be able to drill through the troublesome argillaceous limestone, shale and marls. This inhibition will be achieved with KCL at range of 5-7%wt, PHPA at range of 0.25-1ppb and Glycol at range of 1-3 %vol. (Contingency).

The PHPA will be added to the system after 2 mud cycles, when the mud is warm enough gradually from 0.25ppb to 1ppb in order to prevent shakers overflow. The concentration must be maintained while drilling because this chemical goes out of the system by the cuttings. The Glycol as contingency chemical will be added to the system, when the mud is homogenized. The started concentration is 1 percent by volume. Then after checking the mud properties and ensuring that the mud is stable, the concentration can increase to 3 percent by volume stepwise.

The clay and marl inhibitors in the system are potassium ion for cation exchange with the clays, to reduce hydration and swelling, and PHPA partially hydrolysed polyacrylamide to encapsulate drilled cutting for more effective solids removal efficiency on surface and avoid the clay and marl cuttings to be dispersed in mud system prior to be passed over the shakers.

In Addition, Glycol behaviour causes the polyglycol to become insoluble or precipitate out of solution at a certain temperature and salinity. Thus, resulting in glycol-coated clays that are somewhat waterrepellent.

The chloride content of KCL / PHPA / Salt Polymer Mud is 125,000 - 195,000 mg/l at saturation. As the temperature of the mud increases, more salt is able to go into the solution. This means that a fluid which is saturated under surface conditions may not be saturated in downhole temperatures and can cause substantial washout in a salt zone due to increased salt solubility.

At this system uses KCL / NACL salts as the source of density, salinity and clay inhibition in the system. Salt saturated solution must be used to build the mud when the mud weight reach to 78pcf for this section. For preparing the 73pcf KCL / PHPA / Salt Polymer Mud, the salt solution weight with 20ppb

KCL and addition of NACL must be 70pcf then adding the rest of the chemicals to get 73pcf mud weight. While drilling to section TD the mud weight will be increase gradually as per plan or hole dictation from 73pcf to 88pcf by calcium carbonate as a weighting and bridge agent. Controlling of MW could be done by running SCE (Centrifuges) and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens &amp;amp; dumping the sand trap and dilution. The provision of keeping on the reserve pits, a sufficient quantity of heavy mud as kill mud should be considered. This will help to prompt increasing mud weight in the shortest time.

Maintain the Yield point around 14 to 20 lb/100ft² to ensure adequate hole cleaning, making adjustment with fresh mud or water as required. XC. Polymer will be used to provide an optimized rheological profile with elevated low-shear-rate-viscosity and high shear-thinning characteristics, which result in fluid with inverted flow properties with yield point greater than plastic viscosity.

Care must be taken of shakers overflow while adding PHPA to the system because it will make an appearance Rheology.

Circulate viscous pill sweeps as required for additional hole cleaning. When TD is reached, a minimum of two circulations should be pumped prior to make a wiper trip to surface, followed by a circulation when back on bottom prior to pull out to run 9 5/8" casing.

While drilling the hole with KCL / PHPA / Salt Polymer Mud the API fluid loss will be controlled below 3 cc/30min to section TD. Fluid loss will be kept under control by the addition of Starch LV and PAC LV. The addition of calcium carbonate as a weighting agent will improve filter cake and help lower API Fluid loss. It is strictly forbidden to add Starch and PAC LV directly into the active system. All the treatments must be done as a pre-mix.

The pH should be maintained around 9. to 9.5 using Caustic Soda and Soda Ash. This will maximize chemicals performance and minimize corrosion problems. pH above 10 will cause to convert PHPA to be full hydrolysed and loss its effect of encapsulation. pH should not be increased to be above 10.

Total hardness of water should be maintained below 400 mg/L prior to start mixing the other chemicals for optimum polymer performance with the addition of Soda Ash. Total hardness should be maintained below 800 mg/L with the addition of Soda Ash and/or Caustic Soda while drilling this section. All The premix that uses to add to the system as dump and dilution must be treated for total hardness below 400 mg/lt.

Measuring of the MBT is the direct indication of formation reactivity. MBT below 7.5 lb/bbl. is acceptable. Above this range, API fluid loss will start to shoot up to uncontrollable levels. Using fine screens &amp;amp; high-speed centrifuges will help in maintaining lower values of MBT by discarding the fine solids and consequently minimize the dilution rate.

Shakers to be dressed initially with 100/120 mesh screens and after two or three cycles when the mud polymers are sheared enough dress with finer mesh sizes. Meanwhile drilling could be started with low concentration of PHPA (0.2-0.3 lb/bbl. is recommended) after mud became heated and fully sheared increase PHPA concentration to desired range. It has been experienced that the screen sizes with 175 - 200 API sizes can be applied while drilling this section. There may be a requirement to dress

Doc. No: SJD4 DDRGED DRDR PLDR 9001 D01 Page 204 of 281

the shakers with coarser screens for a number of circulations in order to minimize loss of mud on shakers. Ensure shakers are running immediately prior to and during all periods of circulation.

Use all the solids control equipment available on the rig site. The combination of linear motion shale shaker with centrifuge proved best results. Centrifuge should be run at all the time if available at high flow rate on LGS mode (High Speed) to remove low gravity solids and keep mud weight &amp;amp; properties in range. Constant monitoring of the underflow should determine the efficiency of this equipment. All efforts should be made to maintain the LGS below 6%.

Drilling Issues

Experience has shown that cuttings concentrations more than 5% by volume cause tight hole or stuck pipe when circulation is stopped. The driving parameter that shows the hole cleaning is the 6 and 3 RPM readings. The 6 reading has to be over 5 all time to ensure good hole cleaning. 30bbl of Hi-Vis pill must be pumped every drilled stand and circulated out of the hole prior to connecting the next stand while drilling.

Prior to tripping, if any concern exists about hole cleanliness, consideration should be given to pumping a high weight pill while on bottom. This is especially important if no pills have been pumped during the section drilled. Returns of all such pills at the shakers should be monitored to gauge their effectiveness. Care should be exercised to ensure that excessive amounts of high-density pills are not pumped due to their effect on hydrostatic head. In the case of all pills do not stop or reduce the circulation rate before the pill(s) have been evacuated from hole. To do so will result in material dropping out of the pill. Circulation should continue if solids are still coming over the shakers.

Before POOH for casing running follow below procedure:

• Prepare 300 bbl. (it is not included dead volume) FL controlled pill (FL&amp;lt;3), KCL: 7 %wt.

• Pill weight should 2pcf upper from system weight

• Spot 300 bbl. of this pill at bottom

After KOP the well is deviated and the hole cleaning concern is for cleaning the deviated section. It is noticeable, that cutting beds are created in the deviated part of the hole, and pumping tandem pills (15bbl Low viscous pill followed by 30bbl weighted viscous pill) is strictly required to remove curing beds.

In case of high torque &amp;amp; drag, LUBRICANT or diesel would be used at 1 ‐ 2% by volume.

13.6. 8 1/2" Holes Section Mud Program

Table 57: 8 1/2" Hole Section Mud Program

The fluid for this section is one designed to give proper inhibition to the formations to be able to drill through the troublesome argillaceous limestone, shale and marls. This inhibition will be achieved with KCL at range of 5-7%wt, PHPA at range of 0.25-1ppb and Glycol at range of 1-3 %vol. (Contingency).

The Glycol as contingency chemical will be added to the system, when the mud is homogenized. The started concentration is 1 percent by volume. Then after checking the mud properties and ensuring that the mud is stable, the concentration can increase to 3 percent by volume stepwise.

The clay and marl inhibitors in the system are potassium ion for cation exchange with the clays, to reduce hydration and swelling. In Addition, Glycol behavior causes the polyglycol to become insoluble or precipitate out of solution at a certain temperature and salinity. Thus, resulting in glycol-coated clays that are somewhat water-repellent.

The chloride content of KCL / Salt Polymer Mud is 150,000 - 195,000 mg/l at saturation. As the temperature of the mud increases, more salt is able to go into the solution. This means that a fluid which is saturated under surface conditions may not be saturated in downhole temperatures and can cause substantial washout in a salt zone due to increased salt solubility.

At this system uses KCL / NACL salts as the source of density, salinity and clay inhibition in the system. Salt saturated solution must be used to build the mud for this section. For preparing the 83pcf KCL / PHPA / Salt Polymer Mud, the salt solution weight with 22ppb KCL and addition of NACL must be 75pcf then adding the rest of the chemicals to get 83pcf mud weight. While drilling to section TD the mud weight will be increase gradually as per plan or hole dictation from 83pcf to 87pcf by calcium carbonate as a weighting and bridge agent. Controlling of MW could be done by running SCE (Centrifuges) and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens &amp;amp; dumping the sand trap and dilution. The provision of keeping on the reserve pits, a sufficient quantity of heavy mud as kill mud should be considered. This will help to prompt increasing mud weight in the shortest time.

This section is deviated and the hole cleaning concern is for cleaning the deviated section. It is noticeable, that cutting beds are created in the deviated part of the hole, and pumping tandem pills (15bbl Low viscous pill followed by 30bbl weighted viscous pill) is strictly required to remove curing beds.

Circulate and sweep the hole with tandem pill of low viscous and weighted viscous pill periodically after each drilled stand for hole cleaning because this section is deviated to horizontally.

In case of high torque &amp;amp; drag, LUBRICANT or diesel would be used at 1 ‐ 2% by volume.

13.8. 5 7/8" Hole Section Mud Program

Table 67: 5 7/8" Hole Section Mud Program

The carried mud from previous section must be use to drill the 5 7/8” lateral leg. The fluid for this section is one designed to give proper inhibition to the formations to be able to drill through the troublesome argillaceous limestone, shale and marls. This inhibition will be achieved with KCL at range of 5-7%wt, PHPA at range of 0.25-1ppb and Glycol at range of 1-3 %vol. (Contingency).

The chloride content of KCL / Salt Polymer Mud is 150,000 - 195,000 mg/l at saturation. As the temperature of the mud increases, more salt is able to go into the solution. This means that a fluid which is saturated under surface conditions may not be saturated in downhole temperatures and can cause substantial washout in a salt zone due to increased salt solubility.

At this system uses KCL / NACL salts as the source of density, salinity and clay inhibition in the system. Salt saturated solution must be used to build the mud for this section. For preparing the 85pcf KCL / PHPA / Salt Polymer Mud, the salt solution weight with 22ppb KCL and addition of NACL must be 75pcf then adding the rest of the chemicals to get 85pcf mud weight. While drilling to section TD the mud weight will be increase gradually as per plan or hole dictation from 85pcf to 87pcf by calcium carbonate as a weighting and bridge agent. Controlling of MW could be done by running SCE (Centrifuges) and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens &amp;amp; dumping the sand trap and dilution. The provision of keeping on the reserve pits, a sufficient quantity of heavy mud as kill mud should be considered. This will help to prompt increasing mud weight in the shortest time.

Maintain the Yield point around 14 to 20 lb/100ft² to ensure adequate hole cleaning, making adjustment with fresh mud or water as required. XC. Polymer will be used to provide an optimized rheological profile with elevated low-shear-rate-viscosity and high shear-thinning characteristics, which result in fluid with inverted flow properties with yield point greater than plastic viscosity.

While drilling the hole with KCL / Salt Polymer Mud the API fluid loss will be controlled below 3 cc/30min to section TD. Fluid loss will be kept under control by the addition of Starch LV and PAC LV.

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production

Operations Project

Well Drilling Program - JR-09

Doc. No: SJD4 DDRGED DRDR PLDR 9001 D01 Page 221 of 281

The addition of calcium carbonate as a weighting agent will improve filter cake and help lower API Fluid loss. It is strictly forbidden to add Starch and PAC LV directly into the active system. All the treatments must be done as a pre-mix.

The pH should be maintained around 9 to 10 using Caustic Soda and Soda Ash. This will maximize chemicals performance and minimize corrosion problems.

Total hardness of water should be maintained below 400 mg/L prior to start mixing the other chemicals for optimum polymer performance with the addition of Soda Ash. Total hardness should be maintained below 800 mg/L with the addition of Soda Ash and/or Caustic Soda while drilling this section. All The premix that uses to add to the system as dump and dilution must be treated for total hardness below 400 mg/lt.

Measuring of the MBT is the direct indication of formation reactivity. MBT below 7.5 lb/bbl. is acceptable. Above this range, API fluid loss will start to shoot up to uncontrollable levels. Using fine screens &amp;amp; high-speed centrifuges will help in maintaining lower values of MBT by discarding the fine solids and consequently minimize the dilution rate.

Shakers to be dressed initially with 100/120 mesh screens and after two or three cycles when the mud polymers are sheared enough dress with finer mesh sizes. It has been experienced that the screen sizes with 175 - 200 API sizes can be applied while drilling this section. There may be a requirement to dress the shakers with coarser screens for a number of circulations in order to minimize loss of mud on shakers. Ensure shakers are running immediately prior to and during all periods of circulation.

Use all the solids control equipment available on the rig site. The combination of linear motion shale shaker with centrifuge proved best results. Centrifuge should be run at all the time if available at high flow rate on LGS mode (High Speed) to remove low gravity solids and keep mud weight &amp;amp; properties in range. Constant monitoring of the underflow should determine the efficiency of this equipment. All efforts should be made to maintain the LGS below 6%.

Drilling Issues

In case of stuck pipe, 50bbl of un‐weighted PIPE LAX pill at 3.5‐4.5 gal/bbl. of diesel can be pumped down to the string and every 10min 5bbl spotted around the stuck area while working on the string.

Prior to tripping, if any concern exists about hole cleanliness, consideration should be given to pumping a high weight pill while on bottom. This is especially important if no pills have been pumped during the section drilled. Returns of all such pills at the shakers should be monitored to gauge their effectiveness. Care should be exercised to ensure that excessive amounts of high-density pills are not pumped due to their effect on hydrostatic head. In the case of all pills do not stop or reduce the circulation rate before the pill(s) have been evacuated from hole. To do so will result in material dropping out of the pill. Circulation should continue if solids are still coming over the shakers.

Before POOH for casing running follow below procedure:

All cleaning should be done well in advance wherever possible. To clean pits and lines, 100bbl of water containing 1 to 2 drums of Chemical Wash (Detergent Pill) should be mixed up and circulated through all lines, gun lines, mixing lines, etc. This can also be used to clean the tank system initially.

1. Flash &amp;amp; clean surface pits (All required pits).

2. Clean the mixing hoppers and related lines.

3. Clean the ditches line from shakers to suction pit after displacement is over.

4. Clean shakers while bypass sand traps after displacement.

5. Clean the trip tank after displacement.

Completion Fluid Mixing Procedure

1. Fill up clean reserve pits with required fresh water.

2. Added 183 ppb CACL2 to weight up at 85 PCF.

3. Added 0.5-1 ppb lime to adjust PH about 9-10.

4. Filtered 85 PCF completion fluid from reserve pits to suction pit.

5. Check NTU &amp;lt; 50 and recode NTU.

6. Check TSS &amp;lt; 50 and recode TSS.

7. Added 1 %v/v Corrosion Inhibitor in suction pit. (From top of pit)

8. Added 0.5 %v/v H2S Scavenger in suction pit. (From top of pit)

9. Added 0.5 %v/v Oxygen Scavenger in suction pit. (From top of pit)

10. Added 0.5 % v/v Biocide (Anti-Bacterial) in suction pit. (From top of pit)

Displacement Procedure

1. HPJSM and review pit management plan with all involved crew.

2. Circulate and condition mud.

3. Pump 60bbl of 85 PCF Hi-Vis brine pill as spacer.

4. Start to pumping 85 PCF filtered brine from suction pit to the hole while return mud to

dedicated pits as per pit management plan.

5. When 85 PCF filtered brine on shaker then stop circulation.

6. Clean the ditches line from shakers to suction pit.

7. Bypass sand traps and clean shakers.

8. Take return brine to suction pit.

16.Specific Recommendations for Drilling Optimization

1. Minimize time in the slips and keep pipe moving at all other times when not in the slips.

Reciprocation is preferable to rotation in this aspect; the reciprocation distance shall be more than

5m.

2. Applying Reciprocation with the Rotating Off-Bottom operation ensures that the wear resulting

from the tool joint and inner casing wall contact is distributed over the entire stroke length of

reciprocation, thereby reducing the effect of wear at any particular contact point.

However, if the drill string is not reciprocated with Rotating Off-Bottom, the wear resulting from tool joint contact with casing wall is concentrated at just one contact point only. As a result, for the same amount of operation time, Rotating Off-Bottom without any reciprocation will result in significantly higher wear on the casing as compared to a case when reciprocation is applied.

3. Perform a wiper trip every 200~400m according to the actual condition.

4. Place a ditch magnet at outlet to collect metal filings, report the weight in daily drilling report.

5. During drilling, it is necessary to drill smoothly, strictly avoid drilling string inappropriately braked

and percussion drilling and pay attention to the variation of rotary table torque. Prevent bit

accidents.

6. While drilling in Chert formation, sticky and slip formation, the surface torque may be abnormal

higher and drastic fluctuated, the driller should adjust the WOB and RPM, find out proper WOB

and RPM to reduce the torque fluctuation. Normally if 10% Cherts, control the WOB&amp;lt;15 klb., RPM

80~100, if 20% Chert, insert cone bit will be considered. The driller should understand long time

torque fluctuation with same WOB will lead to BHA fatigue damage soon.

7. Accurately judge the utilization state of bit and grasp the time of replacing the bit well. While

drilling in argillaceous limestone formation, shale formation, or claystone formation, the ROP may

be very low 0.5~1.5m, the torque may very low also, the surface parameters are similar like bit

dull or bit balling, more patients should be paid on this, POOH only after fully considered and

compared with offset wells drilling performance.

8. If SPP decrease sharply and hook load decrease at same time, circulate one bottoms up POOHto

check the BHA; If SPP decrease slowly and no change on hook load, then:

a. Check the surface equipment first, the surface circulate system, mud pumps one by one.

b. After confirmation of all the surface equipment are in work condition, POOH to check

the BHA, do not circulate long time.

c. The tool pusher check every stand on the pipe body and connections, if no wash out

was found, inspect all the BHA before RIH, or RIH joint by joint to check every joint

thoroughly until find the root cause of the SPP dropping.

9. When replacing the bit, measure the outer diameter of the bit, in case of serious wear, RIH and

reaming down slowly must be performed to prevent bit stuck.

10. Stabilize the drill string to minimize wall contact. Consider the use of under-gauge stabilizers

further up the string.

11. Utilize Hi-Vis sweep at section TD and prior to wiper trips, only if needed. Use with caution, since

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production

Operations Project

Well Drilling Program - JR-09

Doc. No: SJD4 DDRGED DRDR PLDR 9001 D01 Page 256 of 281

the overuse of such pills can quickly affect the viscosity of the active mud system. Once the pills

have been pumped, do not stop the pumps until they have returned at the shakers. Hi Vis sweeps

should be caught and segregated or if not able to do so efficiently, that sweep must be dumped

to reduce the chance of increasing Vis of active mud.

12. According to the hole condition, ream down and clean out that section several times and make

sure no debris and no drag are observed.

13. Hole Cleaning Guidelines:

Best drilling practices shall be adopted in order to void annulus overloading / cutting settling around BHA during connections / bridges around the DP.

The following guideline shall be followed:

• Ream each stand prior to connection

• Sweep hole with Hi-Vis pills periodically

• Monitor the mud carrying capacity after any change in the rheology

• Minimize the ECD by keeping low YPs

14. Tripping out guidelines

The following guideline apply for tripping out

• Record periodically P/U, S/O weight, on bottom &amp;amp; off bottom Torque and chart the related

trends.

• POOH without pumping &amp;amp; Rotating (on the elevator) and monitor the P/U weight trend by

comparing the results recorded while drilling.

17.5. Pressure Test Requirements

• All pressure tests shall be performed according to API RP53.

• Rig crew must be alerted when pressure test operations are underway. No one must

remain in the test area.

• All tests must be performed using clear water.

• Should any of the tests identify faulty equipment, drilling operations must be suspended

and well secured, if needed, until the faulty equipment is repaired or replaced.

• All valves located downstream of the valve being tested must be placed in the OPEN

position.

• All pressure tests must be held for a minimum duration of 5 minutes with no observable

pressure decline. (Low pressure test w/250-300 psi for 5 minutes and high pressure test

w/max 70% of WP for 10 minutes)

• Pressure should be released only through pressure release lines.

• Only authorized personnel go in the test area to inspect for leaks when the equipment is

under pressure.

• All lines and connections that are used in the test procedure should be adequately

secured.

• Tightening or repair work must be done only after pressure has been released and all

parties have ensured that there is no possibility of trapped pressure.

• All pressure tests must be conducted with a test pump. Avoid the use of rig pumps for

pressure testing. Cement units are acceptable.

• All test result must be documented in addition to the pressure chart.

• Top drive IBOP's should be inflow tested up to rated working pressure as initial.

• With all BOP equipment installed on the wellhead, any pressure test to be performed shall

not exceed 80% of the internal pressure strengthen on the casing in the well.

• Each part in choke lines be tested respectively to its rated working pressure.

• The relief lines be pressure tested to no less than 1450 psi.

17.6. Pressure Testing of Well Control Equipment

• BOP equipment must be pressure tested as per the following criteria:

o When installed.

o Before drilling out each string of casing.

o Following the disconnection or repair of any wellbore pressure seal in the

wellhead/BOP stack (limited to the affected components only).

o After a maximum of 14 days from last pressure test.

• All BOP pressure tests must be witnessed by DSV and Rig Manager.

• A pressure test is required after the installation of casing rams. This test is limited to the

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production

Operations Project

Well Drilling Program - JR-09

Doc. No: SJD4 DDRGED DRDR PLDR 9001 D01 Page 263 of 281

components affected by the disconnection of the pressure containment seal.

• All well control equipment except annular BOP’s is to be tested to the lowest of the

following criteria after the installation of any wellhead body component or prior to drilling

out cement inside each casing string.

o Maximum anticipated wellhead pressure to be encountered in the hole section being

drilled.

o 70% of casing burst pressure.

o Wellhead rated pressure.

o BOP rated pressure.

• Annular preventer will be tested to a minimum of 70% of the rated working pressure.

• Annular preventer should be tested with the smallest OD pipe to be used.

• All high pressure connections associated with the well control equipment are to be

pressure tested upon the installation or reinstallation of each connection.

• The volume of test fluid must be monitored and recorded. The opening and closing

volumes of all BOP functions must be monitored and recorded.

• All casing pack-offs are to be pressure tested.

• When testing wellhead components due consideration must be given to burst and

collapse rating of relevant casing and components.

• Well control equipment that has been subject to any modification or body repair is to be

pressure tested and, if applicable, re-certified before use.

• Wellheads and drilling spools must have full bore double valve isolation whilst the

wellhead is in communication with open formation. The non-active spool side outlet

should have a Valve Removable Plug (VRP) installed to enable the installation of valves if

necessary.

17.7. Casing Integrity Test

• All surface, intermediate and production casing/liners shall be pressure tested prior to

drilling out the shoe track or perforating.

• For surface and intermediate casings/liners the minimum pressure test must be the

highest of:

o Calculated surface pressure required to perform the planned leak off test plus a test

margin. The recommended test margin for development wells is 4 pcf.

o Calculated pressure for circulating out maximum kick as used in casing design

calculations.

• For production casing/liners, the minimum pressure test must be equivalent to the shut

in tubing pressure on top of the annulus completion fluid.

• Any additional loads that are to be placed on the casing string (e.g. operating annulus

Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production

Operations Project

Well Drilling Program - JR-09

pressure controlled test tools) must also be taken into account when planning pressure

tests).

• Test pressures must not exceed any of the following:

o 70% of burst pressure of the weakest casing.

o Wellhead rated pressure.

o BOP rated pressure.

• Due consideration must be given to the following factors:

o The burst rating of the weakest casing in the string.

o The density of the mud columns inside and outside the casing.

o The minimum design factors assumed in the casing design.

o The effect of pressure testing on casing tensile loads.

• Production casing strings that are to be used in a well for production or injection

operations must be designed and pressure tested to the maximum possible wellhead

pressure.

• Liner overlaps will be positively pressure tested to a minimum of 500 psi over formation

leak-off pressure of previous casing; meanwhile an inflow test must be carried out, with

a sufficient drawdown to test the liner top to the most negative differential pressure that

will exist during the life on the well. The type of fluid below the packer during negative

differential pressure calculation must be considered as existing drilling fluid in the hole.

• The test pressure and method for each well are determined on an individual basis.

• Casing wear and consequent reduction in casing strength must be considered during

planning of drilling and well testing operations.

18.Well Control Procedure

The PECO Well Control Manual brought into force earlier but not later than commence drilling through Gachsaran formation with the mutual agreement of the parties. Introducing the PECO Well Control Manual earlier may be prudent if the formation tops and pore pressures vary significantly from that forecast.

The PECO Well Control Manual applies to all well operations conducted in the transition zone, and reservoir sections of the JR-09 well. This includes all drilling and well Completion/Testing activities.

The procedures and practices in the PECO Well Control Manual provide guidance from which specific procedures are to be developed to take account of the prevailing rig and well conditions. All key members of PECO, Rig Contractor and appropriate service contractors must review these procedures.

However, for any other Well Control procedures and guidelines to take precedence over the ones shown in the “PECO Well Control Manual”, the following is a must and cannot be deviated:

1. At least two tested Safety Barriers shall be present in drilling and producing wells. If for some

reason only one Safety Barrier is present, all activities shall cease until two Safety Barriers are reestablished.

2. All Safety Barriers must be tested in accordance with approved procedures, or as specified in the

program prepared for the specific operation.

3. Activity Typical Independent Barriers:

• Drilling

A sufficient amount of mud or fluid of adequate density to control the well bore pressure, certified and tested BOP stack dressed with suitable rams; unperforated, cemented and pressure tested casing or liner; tested downhole plug; back pressure valve (BPV).

• Casing

A sufficient amount of mud or fluid of adequate density to control the well bore pressure; certified and tested BOP stack dressed with suitable Casing rams.

• Production

Christmas tree; surface controlled subsurface safety valve (SCSSV); downhole plug.

• Wireline

Christmas tree valves; wireline BOP; wireline lubricator.

18.1. Well Control Incident Report

The reportable incidents are as follows:

• When Hydrogen Sulphide (H2S) is detected during operations or samples of well fluid (not

applicable where H2S is known to be present).

• When a BOP or diverter is operated to control a flow from a well.

• When a failure of blowout prevention systems, wellheads or casings, leads to an interruption of

operations on the well to carry out immediate repairs.
