Torque and Drag

Overall friction can become so great in an extended-reach well or horizontal section that the drill string can only be rotated with great difficulty. Needless to say, this condition is conducive to stuck pipe. Obviously, this coefficient of friction will be significantly affected by the lubricating properties of the drilling fluid.

Many of the causes of torque and drag are mechanical, while others are related to hole geometry. Several, however, can be directly attributed to the drilling fluid. Since wall contact with the drill string will be extremely high in a horizontal hole, it is imperative that the lubricating characteristics

of the fluid be considered.

Formation Damage

The obvious reason for drilling a horizontal well is to expose more of the producing zone to the wellbore for increased production. Thus, the importance of preventing formation damage during drilling and completion of the horizontal well is just as important as it is in its vertical counterpart.

In fact, it may be more important since the increased cost of drilling the horizontal well must show additional production for its justification. A 50% damage or permeability loss in a potential 500 bbl/day horizontal well represents a considerably greater loss in production than a 50% damage in a 100 bbl/day vertical hole through the same reservoir.

Sandstone production is by far the most susceptible reservoir rock to damage or permeability loss during drilling and completion operations. Though formation damage may be caused by poor drilling and completion practices, one of the primary causes is due to exposure to the drilling and completion fluid.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

F – 20 Well Drilling Program Page 99 of 181

This loss, attributable to the fluid, can be caused by one or more of the following occurrences:

• Particle transport from the drilling fluid into the production zone, subsequently plugging pore throats.

• Fluid filtrate reacting with expandable clays in the rock to decrease pore throat diameters.

• Particle movement within the permeable rock due to dispersion of clays and other minerals from quartz surfaces.

• Wettability changes of the formation from exposure to the drilling fluid filtrate.

• Interaction of fluid filtrate with formation fluids to form water - insoluble precipitants.

The effect of these actions on the permeability of sandstones has been the subject of a considerable investigation. In almost all cases, some damage is caused by the drilling and completion fluid. The primary objective is to limit this damage as much as possible. Consequently, selection of the drilling and completion fluid becomes an extremely important function in drilling the horizontal well.

Recommended Fluid Parameters

• Velocity – One of the major obstacles to overcome in horizontal and ERD drilling is hole cleaning. In vertical holes, cuttings have room to settle without causing problems. In horizontal wells, cuttings only have to settle 4+ inches to form a cuttings bed. Research and practical experience has shown that cuttings bed formation is analogous to sand dunes on an ocean beach. The bed moves in a wave fashion up the hole. If sufficient annular velocity is

not present, the bed thickens until it reaches equilibrium, which usually occurs when turbulent flow conditions exist. With water, turbulent flow is easily obtained since viscosity is in the denominator of the turbulent flow equation, and water has a viscosity of 1. Fluids other than water require more pump output to approach turbulent flow conditions. Practical

experience in other industries has proven that materials can be transported in water slurries if the fluid velocity is between 3 and 7 ft/sec.

• Rheological Properties – Ideally one would want a true thixotropic fluid to drill horizontally.

In effect, two different conditions exist simultaneously. One occurs in the vertical portion of

the hole where larger diameter casing may be set, or wash-outs in the open hole occur. In that case, a fluid having a high Yield Stress, or if the fluid is visco-elastic, the initial gel strength needs to be elevated. The opposite is needed in the horizontal section from a hole-cleaning point of view. Here one wants water for the reasons pointed out earlier. Compromises are the result. If casing is set into the zone of interest, or if formations up-hole are not a problem, then water may be possibly combined with occasional sweeps.

• Surface Apparatus – Special attention must be placed on the solids removal equipment at the surface. Solids removal efficiency must be continually monitored so that unwanted particulate material is not retained in the fluid system that may negatively affect fluid weight

or filter cake quality, resulting in lost circulation or increased torque and drag. The cost of problems that may occur due to not doing this correctly may far outweigh the cost of equipment needed.

5.6 Hydrogen Sulphide Gas in Drilling Fluid

Description of Hydrogen Sulphide Gas

Hydrogen sulphide is a colourless gas, with an offensive odour and a sweetish taste. It is soluble in water, alcohol, oils, and many other solvents. It has a specific gravity of 1.1895 with reference to air. It is considered a weak acid, it is toxic to humans and corrosive to metals. Hydrogen sulphide can be dangerous to personnel on the surface as it is extremely toxic to human and even animal life, and is extremely corrosive to most metals as it can cause cracking of drill pipe and tubular goods, and destruction of testing tools and wire lines. When hydrogen sulphide enters the borehole during

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

F – 20 Well Drilling Program Page 100 of 181

drilling, completion, or testing for hydrocarbons, it creates several very detrimental problems. These problems are encountered regardless of the source of the hydrogen sulphide. Hydrogen sulphide has created unsolved problems in the oil field.

Origin of Hydrogen Sulphide

During oil and gas operations, hydrogen sulphide can be found as a component of formation gases, dissolved in water, hydrocarbons, or even liquid sulphur. Thermal degradation of organic materials and sulphate reducing bacteria (SRB) can create hydrogen sulphide along with other gases.

Problems Caused By Hydrogen Sulphide Gas Health and Safety of the Personnel

One of the main problems hydrogen sulphide causes is in respect to the health and safety and safety of the personnel. A maximum of eight hours exposure to concentrations greater than 100 ppm H2S will cause hemorrhage and death. Concentrations above 600 ppm can be fatal in three to five minutes. Highly stressed, high strength steel can fail in a matter of minutes in the presence of 50 ppm H2S. At high pressure, as little as 0.1 ppm H2S can greatly reduce the time to failure of highly stressed, high strength steel. Relying solely on its odour is not a good idea because at concentrations above 100 ppm it deadens a person’s sense of smell within a few minutes. The pure gas is heavier than air and can collect in low areas such as pit rooms and accommodation. below Table shows the potential hazards hydrogen sulphide can cause to the personnel from short-term exposures. There are many historical cases to document the ill effects of hydrogen sulphide exposure.

The documented cases reported in Table 2 indicate that hydrogen sulphide is very toxic and it takes only a matter of minutes to affect unprotected workers.

Health effects from short-term exposure to hydrogen sulphideConcentration (ppm) Health Effect0.01 – 0.3 Odour threshold1 – 20 Offensive odour, possible nausea, tearing of the eyes or headaches with prolonged exposure20 – 50Nose, throat and long irritation; digestive upset and loss of appetite; sense of smell starts to become fatigued; acute conjunctivitis may occur (pain, tearing and light sensitivity)100 – 200 Severe nose, throat and long irritation; ability to smell odour completely disappears.500Severe lung irritation, excitement, headache, dizziness, staggering, sudden collapse knockdown), unconsciousness and death within a few hours, loss of memory for the period of exposure (results in permanent brain damage if not rescued immediately).500 – 1000 Respiratory paralysis, irregular heart beat, collapse and

Effects of hydrogen sulphide on Metals

Hydrogen sulphide mainly cause corrosion problems to drill strings, transport pipes, storage tanks etc. Hydrogen sulphide causes sulphide stress cracking, hydrogen embrittlement and pitting corrosion in oil and gas operations. The corrosion of iron in the presence of hydrogen sulphide and water is dependent upon the dissociation of the hydrogensulphide molecule. Iron is oxidized to the ferrous form at the anode and hydrogen sulphide under- goes a two-step dissociation at the cathode. Tung et al22propose the following equilibrium reactions below.

At the anode:

Fe Fe2+ + 2eAnd at the cathode hydrogen is produced and either enters the steel or forms hydrogen gas and bubbles off:

If H2S is present:

2H+ + 2e- H° + H°

If H2S is not present:

H° + H° H2

Hydrogen enters the steel first by adsorption onto the water to steel interface and then by being absorbed into the steel as hydrogen. The amount of hydrogen entry depends on the corrosion rate of the steel surface and the concentration of anions such as HS- that reduce the tendency to produce hydrogen gas (as shown in second equation above) and promotes the hydrogen (Ho) to enter the steel. pH also has an influence on amount of corrosion damage. Basically, the term “sulphides” used in oil and gas operations includes all three water-soluble species, H2S, HS- and S2-, which coexist in a sulphide-water system. Shown in the ionization chart for hydrogen sulphide in figure 1, it can be observed that molecular H2S predominates in the acidic range, where the pH is below 7. In the range of 7 to 12, monovalent HSpredominates and above pH 12, divalent S2- predominates.

The illustration in figure 1 indicates that the most important practice is that when H2S enters in alkaline mud, it reacts to form an alkaline sulphide, most often sodium sulphide.17 While elevated pH is a good way to keep H2S from causing problems under certain conditions, it does not remove it from the fluid and any drop in pH can create a significant hazard. This then brought about the advent of sulphide scavengers in the history of oil and gas operations. The only safe method for the total removal of hydrogen sulphide or soluble sulphides is with a sulphide scavenger.

Effects of hydrogen sulphide on Drilling fluid

The first positive identification of soluble sulphide in the drilling fluids must be taken as a possible indication of H2S entering the fluid from some source. In the simplest case an increase in mud weight may be sufficient to control minor influxes. If levels persist chemical treatment will be required. This can take two forms; neutralization and scavenging. The two terms must not be confused. Neutralization of H2S in drilling fluid by caustic soda or lime is a common field approach. This alkalinity maintenance method has proved successful when small amounts of H2S enter the drilling fluid, for example, from drilling up pore spaces containing the gas.

This is not a suitable approach to the control on influxes of Hydrogen Sulphide. The alkalinity neutralization of H2S is instantly reversible by reduction in pH. Should the pH of the fluid decrease due to further influxes of H2S, Co2 or brine flows the sulphids may come out of solution as hydrogen sulphide gas. To ensure that such influxes are handled safely, it is essential to employ a sulphide scavenger. This term refers to any additive which is capable of reacting with one or more of the sulphide species and as a result, converting them to a more inert form. To be truly effective an irreversible and complete reaction must occur. As a mutual equilibrium exist between the three sulphide species in solution (H2S, HS‐ and S2‐) irreversible and complete removal of one serves to removal all three.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

F – 20 Well Drilling Program Page 102 of 181

To remove the problem it is necessary to precipitate the sulphide as an insoluble inorganic sulphide. Zinc or iron compounds are usually chosen because of the relative inertness of the sulphids formed. Zinc source (Zinc oxide or carbonate) has in the past been the preferred treatment. However, continuous treatment with Zinc carbonate will produce significant undesirable carbonate concentration (Carbonate contamination) which can adversely effect on drilling fluid rehology and fluid loss. See the below table:

Contaminant FV PV YP Gels FL pH Pm Pf Mf Cl‐ Ca2+Carbonate _ _H2S _ _

Quick reference for recognizing carbonate and H2S contamination

As a precaution against Hydrogen Sulphide influxes into the drilling fluid system should be pre‐ treated with Zinc Source. Zinc oxide can be used as an alternative, provided that the possible environmental payloads associated with its use are appreciated. pH and alkalinity tests (Pf/Mf) are a good first indicator of Hydrogen Sulphide influx. However, the use of scavenger is used up. It can be seen from this that while a scavenger increase safety levels, it also makes detection of small Hydrogen Sulphide influxes difficult by conventional methods. Measurement of the concentration of scavenger in the mud system is possible but the analysis method is not safe for use on the rig.

The most effective environmentally acceptable scavengers for Hydrogen Sulphide in water base muds are Zinc sources like Zinc Carbonate or Oxide, primarily because of their solubility which leads to very fast reaction rates compared to other scavengers.

Zinc Sources clearly reacts very much faster than the other scavengers. This is due to the fact that the iron in solution ensures a fast reaction with the sulphides and the chemistry in this case produces elemental sulphur as the reaction product. Elemental sulphur is completely insoluble in water. The iron is reduced from Fe+3 to Fe+2 in the process and some of this will be regenerated to produce Fe+3 when the mud comes in to contact with the air. Any regeneration of Fe+3 will aid in reducing product consumption without affecting is scavenging properties.

Recommended treatment levels of Zinc sources are as follows:

pre‐ emptive treatment is recommended at 1.0 lb/bbl treatment of a mud system in the event of gas influx should be made on the basis that 2.0 lb/bb; will treat approximately 100 ppm Hydrogen Sulphide.

Testing / Reporting/ Treatment for Hydrogen Sulphide

The active mud system must be regularly analyzed and monitored for the presence of active soluble Sulphide with the Garrett Gas train. This test must be carried out at the same time as each complete mud check, i.e.: three times per day while drilling.

Alkalinity checks should be carried out intermittently in between these full checks and any significant reduction in the pH and Mf/Pf should be followed up by testing for the presence of active soluble sulphides with the Garrett Gas Train.

For routine checks lead acetate paper can be used to give a qualitative check. Should this test be positive then it must be followed by a qualitative analysis with a Dragger tube.

The following actions must be taken after the initial positive test result:

1. Inform the Drilling Supervisor

2. Start adding H2S Scavenger to the active mud system. Active soluble sulphides can be analysed and monitored because of their characteristic of readily regenerating hydrogen Sulphide gas in reaction with mild acid. By adding citric acid to whole mud sample in a Garrett gas train detection of Hydrogen Sulphide on lead acetate paper indicates the presence of active Sulphides in the mud. When this qualitative test proves positive a dragger tube should be used to give qualitative results.

However it must be remembered that pre‐treating the mud with MILGARD Fe means that no

Sulphides will be delectable until all the scavenger has reacted, i.e.: it is impossible to detect small influxes of Hydrogen Sulphide in a system pre‐ treating with MILGARD Fe .

Contingency stock to be kept on hand on the rig

Zinc Carbonate or Oxide 120 Sxs 25 kg

Lime 200 Sxs 25 kg

As above mentioned Hydrogen Sulphide is a poisonous and dangerous acidic gas encountered in many formations. It can quickly deaden senses and can be fatal, even at low concentration. Hydrogen Sulphide is characterized by its typical “rotten egg” smell. For safety reasons, it should be neutralized immediately with caustic soda or lime to increase pH to &amp;gt;11.5 to form sulphide (S2‐), then precipitated with a source of Zinc.

Neutralization with caustic soda:

2 NaOH + H2S 2Na+ + S2‐ + 2H2O (at pH&amp;gt;11.5)

Neutralization with maintaining excess lime:

2 Ca(OH)2 + H2S Ca2+ + S2‐ + 2H2O (at pH&amp;gt;11.5)

Converting Hydrogen Sulphide into just sulphide by increasing pH is not a permanent reaction. If the pH were drop into the acid region, sulphide will be converting back into the poisonous H2S form. For this reasons H2S should always be precipitated by adding a source of Zinc such as Zinc Oxide.

Removal by precipitation with treatments of (ZnO):

H2S + ZnO ZnS + H2O

if H2S gas detected in mud following action should be taken to:

4. Immediately rise up the pH to at least 11.5 to 12 with caustic soda.

5. Buffer the pH with lime.

6. Begin treatment with Zinc oxide to remove sulphide (S2‐) from the system. (1 lb/bbl treatment of Zinc oxide removes approximately 1100 mg/lit of sulphide. No more than 2 lb/bbl of Zinc oxide should be used to pre‐treat the system for H2S)

If it appears that H2S bleeding in (flowing) form the formation, the mud density should be

increased to shut off the flow of gas into the well‐bore.

6.1 Drilling Waste Management Design

The contractor is responsible for designing the optimum practices for treating the produced waste during the operation. The initial technical waste management proposal should be included the practices for minimizing, treating and recovering of the wastes.

According to the below categories:

. Water based mud containing minerals and natural synthetic polymers, and

. Cuttings contaminated with WBM.

The contractor is encouraged to offer possible practices to minimize the drilling fluids waste and its regeneration.

6.1.1 Water Based mud containing minerals, naturals and synthetic polymers

. Primary operation

The proposed primary solids control package should be able to control drilling fluid properties, reducing of mud materials usage against conventional solid control equipment, and significantly reduce the number of excess fluids generated throughout drilling each phase of the well.

. Secondary Operation

All excess mud and spillage (water based) should be collected in rig site pits and free surface fluid should be treated using a built for propose flocculation station (has to join with centrifuge) consisting of integral dosing and pumps along with a centrifuge for efficient, quick and controlled separation of the solids before the cleaned fluids is returned to active system or buffer tanks.

This system should be able to remove colloidal sized particles that cannot be removed with primary solids control system.

This system may use to clean up the remaining water-based mud or decrease weight of oil base mud at the end of the drilling fluids programmed.

6.1.2 Cuttings Contaminated with WBM

Spud mud and water-based mud cuttings should be fixed and be ready for transport to disposal zone. For fixing the cutting, 100-150 kg cement shall be used for each cubic meters of cutting as well as 3-4-liter Sodium Silicate for each cubic meter of cutting. (Consumption of cement and sodium silicate varies in different formations). Gypsum is not allowed for cutting fixation. This method is physically Bonds Contaminants to Prevent Leaching to Environment. Final product will pass can test and in case of approval by company man it’ll send to landfill.

6.10.2.4 High Performance Filter Unit

Filtration plays an important role in the natural treatment of waste water as it percolates through the soil. It is also a major part of most water treatment. Groundwater that has been softened, or treated through iron and manganese oxidation, requires filtration to remove floc created by coagulation or oxidation processes. Since surface water is subject to run-off and does not undergo natural filtration.

it must be filtered to remove particles and impurities. Filtration can be compared to a sieve or micro- strainer that traps suspended material between the grains of filter media. However, since most suspended particles can easily pass through the spaces between grains of the filter media, straining is the least important process in filtration. Filtration primarily depends on a combination of complex physical and chemical mechanisms, the most important being adsorption. Adsorption is the process of particles sticking onto the surface of the individual filter grains or onto the previously deposited materials. Forces that

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

F – 20 Well Drilling Program Page 115 of 181

attract and hold particles to the grains are the same as those that work in coagulation and flocculation. In fact, coagulation and flocculation may occur in the filter bed, especially if coagulation and flocculation before filtration was not properly controlled. Incomplete coagulation can cause serious problems in filter operation.

General Procedure:

Prior to each cement job, the unit will be checked accurately. Fluid ends, engines, etc.

The lines will have to be flushed with the mixing water. Cementing heads, plugs will be inspected before the job.

The plugs will be inserted into the cementing head in presence of the Drilling Operation Representative.

Bumping the plug is MUST.

The cement density will be checked, using pressurized balance.

Volume calculations &amp;amp; displacement will be done by &amp;amp; cement engineer.

Rig pump should be used to displace the cement.

9.6 Material Selection

Casing

Corrosive Environment Analysis and Strength Check

Based on the data of offset wells in this oilfield, there is a certain degree of corrosive problems in the 4 layers to be produced. Corrosive medium is principally composed of 2 parts: one is the corrosive gases like H2S and CO2 existing in the produced fluid; and the other is the high salinity formation water. The contents of main corrosive fluids in offset wells are shown in Table.

1) Corrosion in this oilfield is a result of combined action of H2S, CO2 and high salinity formation water. The corrosive

mechanism is complicated, and the corrosive rate on the casing is difficult to determine. Based on the NACE standard and

the data from the Table, the producers result in severe corrosive environment. However, by the research on development

conditions and technical indices, it can be found that although the corrosive fluid contents are high in the oilfield, the

corrosive environment is not extremely serious as the following reasons:

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

F – 20 Well Drilling Program Page 137 of 181

2) In general, the temperature that cause the SSC/SCC is concentrated in the range from 20℃ to 30℃. The average depth of

the horizontal section is 2,730m with the reservoir temperature of 96℃, and tensional stress on the casing does not exist in

the horizontal section. Therefore, the influence of SSC/SCC may not be considered for the casing/liner.

3) Based on the RMDP, the production GOR in the first development phase should not be higher than the initial GOR,

therefore, the flowing pressure is higher than the bubble point pressure all the time, that is, degassing problems do not exist

in the horizontal section and some vertical section, the H2S and CO2 have no chance of separation out of oil phase, and it

is lack of prerequisite for casing corrosion.

4) Based on above all, the corrosive environment of the casing string is not severe. The optimal selection for the casing string

can be stated briefly as follows

Material Selection of Casing String

2) In this oilfield, the corrosion of production string obviously occurs in 2 regions. One is the region where

the pressure is above the bubble point; in which degassing problems do not exist, and the corrosion

environment is relatively weak. Another one is the region where the pressure is below the bubble point;

because of the decline of pressure, the concentration of corrosive gas will increase and the corrosion is

relatively serious. Considering the corrosive environment is not serious in the low water cut production

stage and the production practice in this oilfield has proved the L80 is fit for it, So, the L80 should be

taken as the material of 9-5/8″ casing, 7″, 5 1/2″ and 4-1/2″ liner. In order to prevent the hazard of gas

leakage after production degassing occurs, 9-5/8″ casing, 7″ and 4-1/2″ liner should be Gas tight

thread. 2) The 110S is selected as the material of 9-5/8″/7″/4-1/2″ casing rather than L-80 due to the

high strength requirement in Fahliyan wells, what’s more the 110S is fit for sour gas environment.

Selection of PR (Performance Requirement)

According to API Specification 6A 19th edition, performance requirements are specific nd unique to the product in the as-shipped condition. All products shall be designed to perform according to the requirements of API 6A clauses 4 and clauses 10 while in the pressure and temperature ranges and corrosion envirement. Other requirements include load capability, cycles, and operating force or torque. There are two performance requirement levels: PR1 and PR2. Valves operating as safety valves shall be of the PR2 performance level and meet the requirements of Annex I in API 6A For SA wells, the guideline for PR selection is that all parts not contacting well fluids in nomal production period are PR2, all parts contacting well fluids are PR2 as follow, Casing head housing and casing head spool assembly – PR2. Tubing head spool, tubing hanger and X-mas tree - PR2.

12.1 General Quality, Health, Safety &amp;amp; Environmental Requirements

 PPL/PEDEC’s committed to conducting operations in a manner which minimizes the risks to

the health and safety of those involved in, and affected by, such operations. PPL/PEDEC’s also

committed to conducting its operations in a manner which minimizes the impact on natural and

‘built’ environments in the area of operations.

 This section sets out minimum Quality, Health, Safety and Environmental (QHSE) requirements

for the WORK that MSA and subcontractors will be required to comply with whilst conducting

operations for PPL/PEDEC.

 PPL/PEDEC may perform audits and assessments of MSA’s and its subcontractors’

performance under the CONTRACT. PPL/PEDEC reserves the right without prior notice to

conduct quality, health, safety, security and environmental audits of the operations.

 MSA shall at all times be responsible for performing the WORK in a manner so as to protect

against loss of life, injury to people, damage to property and the environment. The detailed

manner means and methods of performing the WORK shall be under the control and direction

of MSA.

 Prior to the start of Operations, certain QHSE processes must be completed. These QHSE

processes include developing the final QHSE plan format and frequency of any QHSE audits,

permitting and licensing and PEDEC’s approvals. MSA shall ensure that sufficient resources are

dedicated to this task to ensure completion prior to mobilization.

 PPL/PEDEC may at any time stop the WORK or any portion of the WORK without penalty to

PPL/PEDE Cif the WORK is not conducted in accordance with the Quality, Health, Safety or

Environmental guidelines specified in this CONTRACT or by the laws of the appropriate

jurisdiction. PPL/PEDEC reserves the right to require MSA to remove any person from the

operations in the case of non-compliance with QHSE procedures. PPL/PEDEC may also

prohibit the use of equipment and plant in cases where that equipment or plant does not meet the

required standards or is deemed unsafe.

 MSA shall ensure that activities associated with this CONTRACT are conducted in compliance

with applicable national and local HSE laws and regulations, MSA’s standards and PEDEC’s

requirements and IADC documents.

 Limits of Authority

 PEDEC’s Representative(s) do not have the authority to relax health, safety or environment

standards. If they judge the operation to be inadequate with regards to any aspect of quality,

health, safety, security or the environment, then the operation may be immediately suspended.

associated risks. This plan shall, as a minimum, address topics included in the list detailed in

resulted. The following incidents shall be verbally reported immediately to the on-site

third parties, MSA/OEOC or its subcontractors; injury to personnel of PPL/PEDEC, third

parties, subcontractors or MSA/OEOC; near misses which may have had serious potential

consequences; environmental damage; media attention. An initial written report, containing

factual information only, shall be prepared by MSA/OEOC and delivered to the PPL/PEDEC

Representative within twenty-four (24) hours of the incident.

performance of the WORK.

12.8 Well Control

1. Installation Requirements of BOP Stack and Control System:

 The distance between BOP control lines and relief lines shall be not less than 1m. Steel Gap Bridge should

be placed in such a way to protect lines from damage by vehicle crossing. Sundries shall not be packed on the

control line shield, on which welding operations are forbidden.

 The air supply shall be separated from that of driller’s console and directly connected to the main air supply

system, and shall be equipped with liquid/gas separators. Excessive bending and pinching on air hoses are

forbidden.

 Electric power to BOP control system shall be directly from the main switch of the power board, and

controlled by independent switches.

 Accumulators shall be in good condition, charged at its rated value, and ready for work at any time.

2. Installation Requirements of Choke Lines and Kill Lines, and Relief Lines:

a) Beside the drilling spool, one manual and one HCR gate valves on the side of chock manifold and two

manual gate valves on the side of kill manifold shall be equipped, and the manual gate valve close to the spool shall

be always open.

b) The high-pressure co-flex hose shall be installed as straight as possible and fixed by anchor after

installation.

c) Relief lines (burning line and bleed line):

 No field welding is permitted on relief lines and the connecting style of relief lines must be flanged.

 The arrangement of relief lines shall take wind directions, dwellings, roads, oil tank areas, power lines and

other facilities into consideration.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

F – 20 Well Drilling Program Page 165 of 181

 While the two lines go in the same trend, the distance between the lines shall be at least 0.3m, and the two

lines shall be fixed independently.

 The outlets of bleed line connecting with choke manifold shall be in a safe area which is at least 300m.

The bleed line on the kill manifold side connecting with drilling spool shall be prepared and connected when

necessary (about 70m from the wellhead).

 At every 10m~15m, turning points, and outlets, the lines shall be supported and fixed by cement

foundations with anchor bolts or ground anchors. Hanging portions shall be supported firmly. If crossing the

stumbling blocks such as brooks or ponds is needed, metal bridging supports are necessary.

 Pre-buried anchor bolts for cement foundations shall not be less than 20mm or 3/4" in diameter, and

greater than 0.5m in length.

3. Pressure test value and requirements:

a) A pressure test shall be conducted successfully where there is no pressure decline in 5 minutes for a low-pressure

test and a minimum of 10 minutes for a high-pressure test.

b) Prior to each high-pressure test, a low-pressure test with 200-300 psi shall be carried out to verify sealing capability

at the circumstance of low pressure and avoid washing out sealing elements.

c) High pressure test should be to the rated working pressure of ram preventers or the rated working pressure of the

wellhead, whichever is the lowest, or to the rating required in DRILLING ROGRAM. Variable bore rams should be

initially pressure tested on the largest and smallest OD pipe sizes that may be used during the OPERATION.

Annular preventers, with a joint of drill pipe installed, should be tested to 70% of their working pressure. The high

test for Kelly cocks, kill lines and choke lines should be to their rated working pressures, each part in the choke

manifold is tested respectively to its rated working pressures, the relief lines be pressure tested to no less than

1,450psi (10Mpa).

d) When casing cup tester is used, the above test pressure should not exceed 80% of the internal yield pressure (burst

pressure) of the exposed casing.

e) The control system of BOP shall be pressure tested to 3,000psi (21Mpa) for its reliability before putting into use.

f)Except that the BOP control system is tested with hydraulic oil, other well control equipment shall be pressure tested

by clear water.

g) Testing tools

 All required sizes of the plug type testers, and cup type testers should be available for pressure testing

purpose.

 When the cup type tester(s) is used for pressure test, the connection of the cup testers has to be checked, to

ensure it will stand the load during the high pressures test. For surface casing, the cup tester is to be set in middle of

the first casing joint in the top, so the first casing connection (between wellhead and casing head housing) below

the well head is to be tested too while testing BOP and wellhead.

4. Pressure test frequency:

All ram type preventers, annular BOP, valves, choke and kill lines, choke manifold, Kelly valves and safety valves should be pressure tested at the following frequencies:

 Prior to installation where possible.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

F – 20 Well Drilling Program Page 166 of 181

 After installation of wellhead and BOP assembly and prior to drilling.

 After the disconnection or repair of any pressure containment seal in the BOP stack, choke line, or choke

manifold, but limited to the affected component.

 Prior to drilling into a confirmed or suspected high-pressure zone.

 At any time requested by the COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE.

 In any case, every one month or during the first trip after the one-month interval with a maximum interval

of 45 days. This frequency is not required for shear rams. As a minimum, the shear rams are to be tested prior to

resume drilling operation after 9-5/8” casing string has been set and adequate WOC.

5. Work Requirement of Well Control Equipment:

 With shut-in casing pressure lower than 1000psi, while snubbing with annular preventer, drill tools

shall have 18-deg shoulder tool joints, and the snubbing velocity shall not be greater than 0.2m/s.

 After shut off the annular preventer or ram preventer, with the shut-in casing pressure not greater than

2000psi, drill tools are allowed to pull up and down with the velocity less than 0.2m/s, however, rotating or tool

joint passing through are forbidden.

 While drilling through pay zone and thereafter, BOP function (close-open) test for the BOPs shall be

performed regularly.

 Kill manifolds shall not be used for drilling fluid fill-in.

 The maximum allowed shut-in casing pressure shall be remarkably indicated on choke manifolds.

 All gate valves of well control manifolds shall be tagged with serial numbers, and be indicated with

on/Off.

 In case shear rams were used, after shearing the drill pipe with shear rams, retrieve the upper sheared

drill pipe, lower a drill pipe joint with TIW valve installed into the hole and close pipe rams on it to prevent the

possibility of shear ram’s failure.

6. Management of Well Control Equipment:

 Well control equipment used by the drilling crew shall be managed and operated by designated personnel

with clear post responsibilities.

 Well site shall have specified component storeroom and rubber element storeroom with air conditioners

respectively. The temperature of storerooms shall meet storage requirements of components and rubber elements.

 At least 1 set is available as back-up for every type ram assembly in the well site. Ram preventer side

door seals and ram rubber, every type gasket and bolt etc. should be enough for backup.

7. Killing Method and Shut-in Method:

 Driller's method is recommended for well killing.

 The hard Shut-in method is recommended for shutting in the well in Fahliyan reservoir.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

F – 20 Well Drilling Program Page 167 of 181

8. Well Control during drilling:

a) Shut in Procedure in While on Bottom

 Position Kelly (if in use) and tool joint so that tool joints are clear of sealing elements.

 Shut off pumps, check for flow.

 If flow is noted, close the annular preventer and open remote-controlled choke line valve (HCR).

 If the well has been closed using the annular preventer, check space out (pipe rams vs. toll joint relative

position) and close pipe rams and ram locks

 Bleed off pressure between pipe rams and annular preventer (if possible).

 Record shut-in drill pipe and casing pressures.

 Record volume gain and mark pits.

 Weigh mud in suction pits.

 Check blowout preventer and manifold for leaks.

 Check flowline and choke exhaust for flow.

 Check accumulator pressure.

b) Shut in Procedure in While Tripping

 If a flow is detected, install full opening safety valve and close same.

 Position tool joints clear of the sealing elements and close annular preventer and open remote-controlled

choke line valve (HCR).

 Make up grey valve (dart type inside BOP on full open safety valve). Then Make up Kelly or top drive

(insert a pup joint or single between safety valve and top drive) and open safety valve.

 Record casing pressure.

 Check blowout preventer, stack, and manifold for leaks.

 Check valves for correct position.

 Check accumulator pressure.

 Begin stripping to bottom.

c) Shut in Procedure for Empty Wells

 Try to RIH with drill pipe as more as possible if hole condition permits, and the drill pipe must be

installed a Kelly cock or safety valve.

 Close the annular preventer and open remote-controlled choke line valve (HCR).

 If the well has been closed using the annular preventer, check space out (pipe rams vs. tool joint relative

position) and close pipe rams and ram locks

 Bleed off pressure between pipe rams and annular preventer (jf possible).

 Record casing pressure

9. Well Control During Running Casing:

The well control while running casing is important and critical, best practices shall be followed, including but not limited to:

 Change out pipe rams to casing rams prior to running casing into hydrocarbon bearing formation, if

possible.

 The crossover between casing and drill pipe has to be available, and good practice is to make it up with a

joint of DP and keep on V-door.

10.Shut in Procedure During Logging:

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

F – 20 Well Drilling Program Page 168 of 181

Cable shall be pull out of the hole immediately when overflow is found during logging. If pit gain exceeds the specified amount, the cable shall be cut immediately and treat the overflow in accordance with the shut-in procedure for empty wells. Continuing to pull the cable through the closed annular preventer is not recommended.

11.Well Control During Testing:

 No difference to while DRILLING OPERATION, since either there is testing string in the well (same as

Shut-in procedure while on bottom), or tripping the string. (Same as shut-in procedure while tripping).

 Likely there is some crude in the testing string, and precaution has to be taken while circulating the crude

out of hole during killing operations to ensure it is properly handled without causing environmental impact.

 To minimize the formation damage, the killing fluids used shall be weighted brine if possible, however

in well control case when it occurs, killing well safely will take priority rather than protecting formation from

damage on selection of killing fluids.

12.Well Control During Stimulation:

 Similar to during testing.

 For any residual or alive acid to be circulated out during killing operations, measures have to be taken to

treat the returned acid properly to avoid personnel from getting hurt, and without causing any environmental

damage.

13.Well Control Drills:

Drills shall be conducted only when hole conditions and other rig activities permit. Drills should be scheduled so that crews can practice drills while on bottom, while tripping in and while out of the hole. Each operating shift shall perform at least one BOP drill under different situations per month.

14.Basic Requirement of Well Control:

 For 13-5/8”, 10K BOP, BOP should be schemed as follows: upper rams 5”, middle rams are shear rams,

lower rams is variable rams (2-7/8” to 5”). For easily connecting, armored fire-resistant 10000psi and ID 4-1/16"

flexible hoses are recommended as kill/choke lines which connected with BOP directly.

 The BOP stack and choke manifold, kill line and choke line, HCR and manual gate valves, inside BOP

(including kelly cock) have to be H2S trimmed and stand the working temperature from -10 degrees C (in case of

doing N2 for DST) to the maximum up to 100 deg C (estimated highest temperature condition).

 The BOP equipment shall be visually inspected, function tested, and hydrostatically pressure tested

during commissioning and Acceptance of Drilling Unit prior to Commencement Date, then upon installation on a

wellhead, prior to drilling any hole section with a potential hydrocarbon bearing reservoir, after breaking any BOP

connection (such as after installation of an additional wellhead section after running casing), and at least every 14-

21 days while the BOP is installed on the Well.

 CONTRACTOR shall submit the current well control procedures manual of CONTRACTOR to

COMPANY for review and approval by COMPANY. Valid IWCF Well Control Certificates (or IADC equivalent)

must be held by all tool pushers, Drillers (optional) at Drilling Supervisor level and Drillers and Assistant Drillers

at Driller level, as further specified in CONTRACTOR Personnel HSE Requirements.

 The accumulator must be of sufficient capacity so that it is possible to close one (1) ram and the bag,

open a ram and the bag, re-close a ram and the bag and retain 1200psi accumulator pressure.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

F – 20 Well Drilling Program Page 169 of 181

 The “OPEN” and “CLOSED” operating positions of BOP activators of the rams, annular, and remote

actuated valves must be clearly identified on the BOP master control panel and remote panels, in English in

addition to the native language of the majority of the senior drilling crew.

 Shear-ram BOP activator must have a flap-cover to ensure only pre-meditated and deliberated activation

and to prevent accidental WORK.

 All lines and connections in the choke and kill manifold, standpipe manifold, choke and kill lines and

high-pressure mud lines should be welded hard-piping with weld-on FMC Weco “hammer-lug” 1502 unions (or

Western equivalent, such as Anson) or weld-on API flanges. The well control system should not include any

threaded screw-on hammer-lug unions, flanges, or other threaded screw-on connections.

 All adapter or spacer spools between the wellhead and BOP must be manufactured in accordance with

API 6A, and must be complete with all required studs, nuts, and ring gasket seals for both lower and upper

connections; minimum spare parts should include two (2) OEM spare studs complete with nuts and two spare OEM

ring gasket seals for both bottom and top connections.

 There should be a wide-bore gas vent line from the “poor-boy” degasser; the line and line outlet must be

securely anchored, the line outlet must be a safe distance from the well cellar, rig floor, choke manifold, and mud

logging unit.

 Well Control Equipment Welding: All welds in the well control system must be NDT inspected and

records maintained of all welding and weld inspections, including choke and kill manifold, standpipe manifold,

mud pump discharge manifold, choke and kill lines.

 Well Control Rig Floor Information: The following must be posted on the rig floor (in the Driller’s shack

/ “dog-house”): Well Shut-In Procedure, Well Information Sheet (showing casing and hole sizes, depths, and such

like), Kill Sheet (including most recent slow circulation rate pressures, formation integrity leak-off test information

and MAASP, present mud weight, present drill string and well volumes, and such like).

 The derrick substructure clear height (rotary table to ground level) needs to be enough for fitting in

above BOP configuration (including a tubing head and a bell nipple). This need to be double checked in rig tender

process. According to the calculation of height of BOP stack, the substructure clear height is at least 9 m.

 In the case if drilling 6-1/8" hole becomes necessary, or using 3-1/2" drill pipe for the cleanup run

(including drill 7" shoe track), then taper drilling string (5" DP + 3-1/2" DP) is to be run, so a pair variable ram be

installed in the single ram preventer. The defect installing variable ram in single ram preventer is that the ram may

be damaged and the string fall in hole bottom due to the ram hanging up too much weight when the drill pipe be

cut. If the pipe ram be installed in the single ram preventer and the variable ram be installed in the double ram

preventer, it would be very dangerous due to the variable ram failure in frequently using.

12.9 H2S Monitoring and Preventing Measure

As per PPL/PEDEC SOW South Azadegan oilfield contains H2S bearing formations, precautions shall be taken in place especially in 12-1/4” &amp;amp; 8-1/2” hole section (for typical Fahliyan vertical well) while drilling, completion and well testing operation.

H2S can be released any time while drilling, completion and well testing operation, therefore:

 The Rig shall be prepared for H2S (Training, procedures and protective gear).

 Make sure everyone on the Rig should be made aware of the hazard presented by H2S during

their induction when they first arrive on the rig.

 The mud shall be treated to protect the drill pipe and the casing.

 All training program shall be recorded and reported.

 H2S emergency drill must be conducted frequently.

 Adequate sensors and alarms must be installed for the scope of monitoring the H2S releases.

1.         General Information

1.1 Field Introduction

Azadegan South Oil Field is situated in West Karoun province on a large long-axis anticline with N-S trending with approximate dimensions about 20 km width and 60 km length near to Iran-Iraq border, to the east of Yaran Oil Field.

The trap area of the south Azadegan is limited to 43.2x17.2 km. The Azadegan Oil field was discovered in 1999, when Well AZN-1 was drilled vertically down to the Cretaceous Fahliyan Formation with total depth of 4,643m. The results of this well, revealed the reservoir characteristics of the field. Following to the result of the well no. AZN-1, another 5 exploration wells was drilled in different parts of this huge field down to Fahliyan Formation. In the later stage, the well No.10 assumed as exploration well for evaluation of deeper formations. This well was drilled in 2008, down to the depth of 5340m (Neyriz Fm.), mainly to evaluate the Jurassic formations.

Based on the exploration wells results, carbonate reservoir of Sarvak Formation is broadly developed in Azadegan Field. This formation was penetrated in all of seven exploration wells (AZN-1, AZN-2, AZN-3, AZN-4, AZN-5, AZN-6 and AZN-10). Clastic oil-bearing zones of Kazhdumi Formation developed in main anticline of Azadegan Field, extending from north to center of South Azadegan. The Clastic oil-bearing zones of Gadvan Formation developed only in crest area and south parts of South Azadegan Filed, which was discovered by AZN-1 in crest and AZN-4 in south parts. The carbonates of Fahliyan Formation also developed in Azadegan field, but the oil reservoir of this formation developed in South part of South Azadegan.

The Azadegan Field is an elongated anticline, trending in N-S direction, belonging to "Arabian Trend".

The stratigraphy sequence of the field includes AghaJari, Gachsaran, Fahliyan, Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan and Fahliyan Formations, from top to bottom. This sequence in well no AZN-10, the deepest up to now drilled well of the field, continues with Garau, Gotnia, Najmah, Sargalu, Alan, Mus and Neyriz formations.

The Dominant lithofacies of Sarvak Formation are Rudist-bearing pack stone and partially grain stone, which contains abundant bio clasts. Some other facies like matrix-dominated wackestone and mudstone are also found.

The AZADEGAN Oilfield is Located in Khuzestan Province and is Approximately Located 80 Kilometers West of Ahwaz City, near to Iran-Iraq Border. It is in The Northwest of The YADAVARAN Field and in The West of JUFEYR Field. The Average Monthly Temperature is 45ºc in summer, and Highest Temperature is 52ºc. The Lowest Temperature is -4.4ºc in winter. Maximum Rainfall is 78 mm in February, Winter Season.

2.         Formation Description

A brief description of the Sarvak units are as following:

·         **Sarvak Formation**

The Sarvak Formation developed a carbonate unit, which was gradually overlying the Kazhdumi Formation, and it is abruptly terminated by an erosion phase, covered by a various late Cretaceous sediment. The lithology of Sarvak consists of the dark grey fine-grained nodular argillaceous limestone interbedded with thin marls in the bottom.

Sarvak-1 mainly composed of brown to brownish grey moderately hard argillaceous limestone. With 10 meters interbed of pure limestone.

Sarvak-2 Contains Grey to Dark grey flaky, moderate hard slightly calcareous shale with thin layers of light grey-to-grey argillaceous limestone and light grey to off white moderate hard pure limestone.

Sarvak-3; mainly contains light grey to brownish grey, moderate hard sub-bulky pure limestone.

Sarvak-4_7; Contains cream to off white, partly microcrystalline limestone.

4.         AZNS-118 Well History

Well AZNS-118(Pad 26) was drilled by PDX204, spudded on 10 Jul 2016 @ 12:00 P.M. The Well Reached to TD at 4285m on 01 Oct 2015 @ 19:30, Rig was released on 20 Dec 2016 @ 06:00 A.M.

1.       30" conductor pipe was preset.

2.       26" hole was spudded @ 12:00 on Jul 10, 2016 &amp;amp; drilled to CSG point at 156m @ 18:00 p.m. Jul 11, 2016.

3.       20" CSG was run to 154m &amp;amp; cemented by inner stab-in string with slurry to surface.

4.       17-1/2" hole was spudded @20:00 on Jul 15, 2016 &amp;amp; drilled to 1396 @ 11:00 Aug 1, 2016.

5.       13-3/8" CSG was run &amp;amp; cemented @ 1395 with slurry to surface.

6.       12-1/4" hole was spud @17:00 on Aug 8, 2016 &amp;amp; reach section TD at 1778.5m @ 12:00 on Aug 14, 2016.

7.       9-5/8" CSG was run &amp;amp; cemented @ 1778m with slurry to surface.

8.       8-1/2" hole was spudded @05:00 Aug 20, 2016. KOP @ 3540m, after plug back, sidetrack the hole &amp;amp; KOP @ 3707m, explain more about the original &amp;amp; side tracked borehole (depth, reason of sidetrack, any probable fish LIH,) section TD @ 3929m @ 15:00 on 25 Oct 2016.

9.       7" liner was run &amp;amp; hanged from 1699 m to 3928.5 m MD.

10.   6 1/8" hole was spudded @00:00 Nov 08, 2016. It was drilled to 4285m MD (TVD: 3846.27 m AZ: 30 Inc. 90.2) @ 22:00 on 02 Dec 2016.

11.   4 1/2" liner run from 3870m to 3914 m by Blank 4 ½” liner then 3914 to 4284m by 4 ½” Slotted Liner.

12.    3 ½” x 4 ½” Standard Completion String was run while Packer set @ 3580.2m.

13.   Rig was released on Dec 20, 2016 @ 06:00 A.M

5.         Program Outline

General sequences of workover operation are as following:

1. Secure the Well.

2. POOH Completion String.

3. Clean out with 8 1/2", 5 7/8" &amp;amp; 2 7/8" BHA to TD.

4. Take Corrosion log &amp;amp; check 9 5/8" CSG &amp;amp; 7" Liner.

5. Perforate the Well.

6. Run 4 1/2" 3 1/2" completion string 5K.

7. Flow the Well as Pre-Acid Clean up.

8. Perform acid wash.

9. Flow the well as post-acid wash.

10. Displace the well with diesel.

11. Secure the well &amp;amp; close all valves of X-mass tree except BMV.

6.         Sequence of Operation

6.1 Objective:

De-complete the well in Gadvan production formation, Set CMT Plugs, Perforate and Re-complete the well in Sarvak formation as per the following:

6.2 Detail sequence of workover operation

1.      Check the wellhead for any damage or leakage. Record wellhead pressures; check the all

annulus pressure. Check the return fluid &amp;amp; Bleed off any annulus pressure to Zero upon client’s approval and recheck the well status.

Note: New section C (T.H.S) and new XMT should be used in the well. Change spool to be planned in due time.

2.      R/U CT and Well test equip. RIH with CT, Kill the well with proper Kill Mud.

Note1: Perform DHSV Function test and check for proper P.S before CT Running

Note2: Obstruction removal with CT Chemical wash may be required in case of any asphaltene or other obstruction.

Note3: Bull heading method may be considered as a contingency plan

3.      RIH with SL, set plug in landing NO-GO, POOH to surface. Set BPV inside Tubing Hanger.

Note: Subjected to the well condition and safety concerns, decision may be changed to set or not set the plug&amp;amp;prong in NO-GO landing nipple.

4.      N/D XMT. N/U BOP and pressure test. Retrieve BPV &amp;amp; check pressure.

5.      R/U CSG Handling Eq., Apply over pull to unset the production packer. POOH with completion string.

**Note 1: If the unset operation was not successful, next plan will be issued in due time.**

**Note 2: Next plan's time does not consider in operation time duration.**

****

6.      RIH with 8 1/2” bit (P/U DP's JT by JT) and clean out BHA to 7" Liner lap (1699m), CBU till shakers clean, POOH to surface.

7.      RIH with 5 7/8” bit and clean out BHA (P/U DP's JT by JT) to 4.5" Liner lap (3870m), CBU until shakers clean, POOH to surface.

8.      RIH with 2 7/8” bit and clean out BHA (P/U DP's JT by JT) to bottom (4284m) for TD check, CBU until shakers clean, POOH to surface.

9.      RIH with clean out BHA including 7” ~ 9 5/8” Tandem scraper to 4 ½” L.Lap (3870m) POOH to surface.

10.  RIH with Wire line Corrosion Logging Tools to check 9.625’’ CSG &amp;amp; 7’’ LNR, log up to surface.

Note1: Although 7’’ L.Lap Dry test was OK according to the well history, it may be required to perform any positive test or Dry test again as per Corrosion Log result.

Note2: REMEDIAL PLAN should be proposed in due time in case of any abnormal condition as per corrosion Log

11.   Re-log (SBT,CAST,…) to Check 7’’ LNR CMT Bonding quality and confirm isolation for perforation area

12.  RIH and Set the first **T-Cement plug** inside &amp;amp; above 4.5’’ L.Lap, WOC, RIH and Tag CMT, Perform positive press. Test

13.  RIH and Set the second **Cement plug** inside 7’’ LNR, WOC, RIH and Tag CMT, Perform positive press. Test

Note: Compatibility of Fluid in hole to be considered before CMT job.

14.  Displace perforation area with proper fluid and Perforate the well

Note: Sequence of perforation operation should be considered as Under-balanced.

15.  RIH with GR-CCL log to confirm perforation intervals.

16.  RIH 7” casing scraper and scrap production packer setting area and displace the well with completion fluid (NaCL). POOH and L/D DP's.

17.  RIH w/ DP's and DC's, POOH and L/D same.

8.1.3.3       Mixing Procedure

**Kill Mud Mixing Procedure:**

1. Fill tanks with calculated amount of Drill Water 0.8 bbl/bbl

2. Treat Drill Water with Caustic soda and Soda Ash by 0.3pbb.

3. Mix 5-6 ppb Starch HT, at rate of 1 sack per 7 min

4. Mix NaCl at 88 ppb.

5. Add Xanthan-Gum by 1.5pbb.

6. Add CaCO3-F (96ppb) to reach MW of ±84 pcf

Ä  In case of foaming use Alcohol-Based Defoamer.

**Note**: Use Hi vis pill to clean hole if necessary

8.1.3.4       Downhole Losses

Losses/Differential sticking will be minimized/avoided by the planned use of properly sized bridging/weight material (and Polymer) in conjunction with appropriate drilling practices. If seepage losses are noted on the well no specific action will be taken but close monitoring of the loss rate is to be made. For moderate loss rates addition of CaCO3 50 micron and 150 micron is recommended to ensure that there is adequate correctly sized material to act as bridging agents.

++**Seepage losses Less than 10 bbl/hr.**++

No specific action will be taken, but close monitoring of the probable loss rate is made.

++**Losses from 10-30 bbl/hr.**++

Ø Load CaCO3-M (150-300 micron) in system up to 5 ppb

**If loss not cured and even tends to increase, then:**

§  Pump 40-60 bbl of pill made by 7-10 ppb CaCO3 150-300μ &amp;amp; 7-10 ppb CaCO3 600μ

++**Losses from 30-50 bbl/hr.**++

Ø Load CaCO3-M (150-300 micron) in system up to 5 ppb

Ø Since some of the CaCO3-M will be discarded over the shakers, CaCO3-M to compensate the separated amount on the shakers.

**If loss not cured and even tends to increase, then:**

§  Pump 40-60 bbl of pill made by

§   10-20 ppb CaCO3 200-300μ

§   10-20 ppb CaCO3 600 μ

§   10pbb Oyster Shell-F

§   10pbb Oyster Shell-M .

++**Losses from 50-100 bbl/hr.**++

Ø  Load CaCO3-M (150-300 micron) in system up to 5 ppb

Ø  Load CaCO3-C (600-100 micron) in system up to 5 ppb

Ø  Since some of the CaCO3-M&amp;amp;C will be discarded over the shakers, add CaCO3-M&amp;amp;C to compensate the separated amount on the shakers.

**If loss not cured and even tends to increase, then:**

Ø  Pump 40-60 bbl of the following pill:

§  10-20 ppb CaCO3 200-300 micron

§  10-20 ppb CaCO3 600 micron

§  7-10 ppb of each CaCO3 1000 micron &amp;amp; CaCO3 2000 micron

§  5-10 pbb Oyster Shell -F

§  5-10 pbb Oyster Shell -M

++**Losses more than 100 bbl/hr.**++

High concentrated LCM pill of various sizes of Calcium Carbonate and Oyster Shell-F&amp;amp;M&amp;amp;C should be pumped and spotted and gently squeezed over the loss zone.

**++Spotting Procedure++**

1.      After spotting LCM pill, pull the bit above the calculated top of the pill. Wait 30 minutes and monitor the annulus.

2.      After 30 minutes, attempt to fill the annulus, if not already full. If the hole can be filled, close BOP and squeeze 10 bbl LCM pill into formation without exceeding 200 psi.

3.      If the hole remains stable, continue to drill ahead.

4.      Should the LCM pill fail to reduce the losses or the hole cannot be filled, then mix and spot another 50 bbl of LCM pill.

5.      Attempt to fill the annulus. If successful, close the BOP and squeeze 20 bbl of LCM pill into the formation without exceeding 200 psi.

6.      If a squeeze pressure develops, hold the pressure for 1 hour before running the drill string back to bottom.

++****++

++**Notes:**++

Ä  LCM pills must be thoroughly homogenised and viscous enough before being pumped.

Ä  Pumping high-concentrated LCM pill is subject to use of open-end DP or Mule-Shoe.

Ä  Remove filter screens from the drill pipe (if there is any) and if necessary, remove strainers from the mud pump suction lines.

Pit levels should be monitor throughout the displacement operation to catch and prevent an influx entering the well contributing to an incident.

9. Perforation Program

9.1 Perforation Gun

TCP (tubing conveyed perforating) shall be the first priority and WCP (wireline conveyed perforating) shall be the back-up method if TCP could not be safely conducted. Perforation will be done in underbalanced pressure.

9.2        Perforation Gun and Charges/CCL-GR

Perforation gun and charges shall be provided according to Table 7. CCL-GR shall be provided in requested sizes. Guns can be run on wireline or TCP be performed depending on total perforation length.

In order to get higher productivity from perforation, underbalanced perforating can be considered such as static or dynamic underbalanced perforation, which the results heavily depend on perforation design according to the length of perforation, well pressure, mud content, gun pressure following detonation of perforation charges, and the well bottom hole pressure after perforation tunnels are created.

10.4              7″ Scraper Run

10.4.1         Risk Evaluation

•           Junk falls in hole

•           Debris on top of Liner hanger

•           BHA stuck in the hole in perforation interval

•           Fish scraper parts in well.

10.4.2         HSE Focus Points

•           Well has to be stable before running the BHA.

•           Monitor well for loss/gain over the trip tank.

•           Good communication among all parties responsible for well control.

•           Pre-job meeting will focus on well control, contingency procedures to be understood by all involved parties.

•           Volume and well control shall be focused upon throughout running/pulling. Fill out kick sheet prior to run in hole.

•           On a positive indication of a kick, unexpected pit gain or flow return rate increase, well shall be shut in without performing flow check

•           A kickstand shall be readily available at all times

•           Kick assembly with proper cross over to 3 1/2" and 4 1/2" shall be prepared before starting operation.

10.4.3         Operation Sequence

1.         P/U &amp;amp; M/U 5 7/8” Bit + 7” Scrapper + 4 ¾” DC or 3 ½” HWDP + enough length of 3 ½” &amp;amp; 5” DP

2.         Scrape packer depth interval 3900m to 4000m Several times while pumping.

3.         Displace well with completion fluid as displacement procedure. (From 4146 to Surface)

4.         POOH to surface while observe the well to make sure well is static. L/D all DPs &amp;amp; DCs.

5.         Retrieve wear bushing, M/U jet sub and flush BOP stack &amp;amp; wellhead with fresh water.

6.         Hold a pre-Job safety meeting on rig floor to instruct running speed and other critical installation procedures.

7.         Lift all emergency well control subs on the rig floor and make up to cock valve.

10.5              Completion Installation

10.5.1         Objectives

The objective is to install the upper completion, landing nipple, 4 1/2” &amp;amp; 3 ½” production tubing, tubing hanger and X-mas tree.

10.5.2         Risk and Quality

Quantitative Risk Assessment, QRA, has been carried out on all main issues in the planning phase. The purpose was to guide the work according to identified risks for the operations, as well as to reduce the probability for incidents with potential HSE or commercial exposure. In the detailed planning phase, QRA has been an integral part of the work. All potential risks identified have been evaluated and mitigating actions have been implemented to reduce the risks to acceptable levels.

10.5.3         Main Concerns

•           Junk falls in the well before or during running completions string.

•           Well/completion fluid not cleaned prior to running completion string.

•           Over-torque tubing connections.

•           Missing to tight all stud bolts on X-Tree bottom section

•           Tubing head wear/damage while RIH equipment, due to off centered derrick.

•           Taking kick/inflow during completions operation (when well is perforated)

•           Damaging Tubing Hanger while running through riser/BOP.

•           Unnecessary personnel on rig floor while running completion string.

•           Use excess amount of dope on each connection, Use of Improper Tong &amp;amp; elevators.

•           Damaging DHSV control line with manual.

•           Damage to injection lines while running in hole.

•           Loosing pressure on DHSV control line while RIH.

•           H2S detection during operation

•           Packer fails to pressure test

•           Poor make up graphs due to poor supervision

•           Slick line operation failure

•           Tie down screws function problem

10.5.4         HSE

HSE focus points are:

•           Well shall be in stable condition prior to running completions string.

•           Monitor well for loss/gain over the trip tank while RIH completions string.

•           Good communication among all parties responsible for well control is essential.

•           Perform kick drill with focus on the use of kickstand (Kick string assembly) prior to RIH completions string.

•          Kick assembly with proper cross over to 3 1/2 and 4 1/2 shall be prepared before starting operation

•           Pre-job meeting will focus on well control &amp;amp; contingency procedures to be understood by all involved parties.

•           Perform pre-job meeting with all involved personnel at critical stages of the operation.

•           Volumes and well control shall be focused throughout running completions string.

•           Fill out kick sheet prior to RIH.

•           On a positive indication of a kick such as unexpected pit-gain or flow return rate increase, well shall be shut-in without performing flow check.

•           A kickstand shall be readily available at all time on rig floor.

•           Maintain good housekeeping on the rig floor at all times.

•           Special care must be taken in running scraper and polish mill to make sure considered intervals are clear to run and Set production packer.

•           Sufficient lighting on Wellhead/ Well cellar is essential.

•           The power tong and jam unit prior to starting the job should supplied a recent calibration certificate

•           Scaffolding shall be installed on wellhead for ease of operation during X-Tree installation and tests.

•           All personnel working on rig floor, BOP &amp;amp; X-Tree shall be wearing safety harness.

10.5.5         Thread cleaning, compound application and make up

Storage compounds are not suitable as running compounds, so they must be removed and the connections cleaned prior to application of thread running compound for make-up.

•           Never use barite or wire brush to clean connections as damage can occur.

•           Never use diesel to clean the connections as this will leave a film that can cause make up problems or affect the performance.

Use steam cleaner or water jet to clean the threads.

Rack one row of tubular on pipe rack, open the protectors, clean the box and pin connections out of storage dope, hand tight the clean protectors and rack another row of tubular on top. Continue the above procedure until all connections are cleaned and racked consecutively.

Rack the tubular in staggered configuration with drill-tech wraps (plastic spacers) in between.

Connections should be completely dry before application of thread compound.

All compounds conforming to API 5A2 and API5A3 are acceptable as running compounds.

These API modified thread compounds are harmful to the environment and can cause skin problems.

Do not use expired running thread compounds. If excess thread compound has been left from a previous job and it has been stored properly, then it is acceptable to use. Ensure that the compound is free of foreign particles.

Never use drill pipe compounds for tubing and casing and vice-versa.

Thread compounds are all required to be regularly mixed during use.

Evenly apply the correct quantity of compound (as per below table) to all the thread seal and shoulder areas with fine brush. The compound must reach the bottom of the thread. Thread compound must not extrude from the connections during make up as this indicates extra dope applied.       Use steam cleaner or water jet to clean the threads.

Rack one row of tubular on pipe rack, open the protectors, clean the box and pin connections out of storage dope, hand tight the clean protectors and rack another row of tubular on top. Continue the above procedure until all connections are cleaned and racked consecutively.

Rack the tubular in staggered configuration with drill-tech wraps (plastic spacers) in between.

Note: Open all the tubing protectors in the rack, wash and clean all the threads.

Note: Back up for tubing hanger-running tools must be provided

Note: pump-in sub (kill sub) must be provided for slick line operations and lubricator pressure tests.

Note: Haskel pump must be provided for offline tests

10.6              Clean up procedure

This program describes the procedure to clean up and displace the cased hole from water based mud brine as safely and effectively as possible prior to running the completion equipment. Clean working practices and good housekeeping as always are important. All rig pits, ditches, and lines (including gun lines) should be cleaned using solvents and detergents. If it is practical, lines should be opened to check for any mud solids that might have settled in them. All the pits, sand traps, and under the shale shakers should be cleaned out and washed down using high pressure cleaning equipment. In the pit room, all gratings should be cleaned; all the lights and beams should be washed down. All cleaning should be done well in advance wherever possible. To clean pits and lines, 15 m3 of water containing 1 to 2 drums of CLEAN SURF should be mixed up and circulated through all lines, gun lines, mixing lines etc. This can also be used to clean the tank system initially.

·         Pump should be worked at the maximum safe rate.

·         The below checklist should be filled by the supervisor in the site.

·         It should be noted that all dump valves should seal with grease to ensure they are in good order.

·         All ditch gates should be sealed with silicon on each side of the gate. This will need to be replaced if the gate is opened.

·         Under no circumstances should barite, bentonite or polymers be used to seal anything.

·         All pump packing should be examined before starting the cleaning

10.7              Displacement Design

To ensure effective mud displacement and water wetting of the casing, the displacement pill needs to be designed carefully. The use of a weighted push pills with a viscosity greater than that of the mud, will minimize channeling and ensure good cleaning of the low side of the well bore.

The best fluid for thinning the mud is the continuous phase of the mud. In addition, SPERSEEN CFL could be used to reduce the yield point and gel strengths. The yield point should be between 8 to 10 Pa and the 10 minute gel to &amp;lt;10 Pa.  The actual quantity of material required to do this must be determined by the pilot testing performed by the mud engineer to determine the most cost-effective treatment.

Throughout the drilling fluid conditioning process, the flow rate used should be the maximum practical rate.

The drill string should be reciprocated and rotated during the operation. The combined effect of scrapers being run in the hole, the high flow rate and the reciprocation/rotation will help to remove/disperse large quantities of mud solids and general debris. The reciprocation stroke should be +/- 10 m. and the rotation speed should be +/- 60 RPM

During this operation, as much of the surface volume of mud as possible should be removed from the pits to accommodate the inhibited water and the well clean up pills. Once the mud has been back-loaded, surface preparation can be done.

At least 150 m of pill/spacer coverage or 3 min contact time at the highest pump rates should be considered.

Pit levels should be monitor throughout the displacement operation to catch and prevent an influx entering the well contributing to an incident.

10.8.1         Completion Fluid Mixing Procedure:

1.      Make sure that all pits and lines involved with completion fluid are thoroughly cleaned, flushed and free of any fluid and solid.

Ä  Make sure that at least one large pit is kept empty for transferring ready brine into after given time for settling. After transferring one pit to empty pit, the first one is to be flushed and cleaned for accommodating the brine of next ready pit, and so on to the last pit.

Ä  Depends on the rig facilities and structure, mud engineer on board may find it better to prepare the fluids pit-by-pit.

2.      Fill tanks with calculated amount of Drill Water 0.883 bbl/bbl

3.       Mix Sodium Chloride (Salt) by 96pbb for saturated Brine.

4.      Mix Corrosion Inhibitor into pits at concentration of 3.5pbb(1% by volume).

5.       Mix H2S Scavenger Liquid into pits at concentration of 0.5% by Volume.

6.      Mix Lime into pits at concentration of 0.5 ppb.

Ä  At least one hour after finishing first pit, check its pH to see if it is ±10. If not, then mix another 0.5 ppb. Repeat the procedure once or twice only if required.

7.      Do not add Oxygen Scavenger at this stage as it should be added directly from the top of the pit, just prior to pump the fluid into the well.

8.      Shut down all agitators and mixing pumps, and leave the mixed fluid in the pits for at least 12 hours to let any solid particle inside (mostly insoluble Lime) settles down.

9.      Start transferring the clear fluid of the first pit to the empty pit by means of an air-powered Wilden pump.

Ä  Make sure that the suction hose of the Wilden pump is not put deep close to the bottom of the pit, otherwise, settled solids are sucked in.

Ä  After finishing the first pit, stop Wilden pump, wash, flush and clean the pit, use it as the empty pit for accommodating the fluid of second pit using the and same above method.

Based on well readings and the operation, mud weight may be varied

10.9              X-Mass Tree body pressure test before installation

X-Mass Tree body pressure test shall be performed direction flow at well site and before installation.

NOTE

·         All steps shall be done with considering all safety issues and under HSE officer presence.

·         Check if pressure gauges have validate calibration certification.

·         Connect crossover test flange to the pump truck.

·         Turn all inner valves to half open

1.      Pressure test for tubing hanger

Pressure test the annular space between S seal of tubing hanger body &amp;amp; the annular space between the S seal of the tubing hanger neck &amp;amp; gasket ring for 4000psi. Hold and monitor the pressure for 15 minutes. In the event of leakage, remove the tubing hanger and replace the seals as required.

Pressure test the annular space between the upper and down S seal of the tubing hanger upper neck for 4000 psi. Hold and monitor the pressure for 15 minutes. In the event of leakage, remove the wellhead and replace the spare parts as required.

2.      Pressure test for X-Mas Tree

After installation X-Mas Tree, replace left-wing companion flange by crossover test flange and connect to the pump truck.

3.      Pressure test for two-way valve

·         Take apart the Tree-cap and make up the two-way check valve by running tools. Then, make up the Tree-cap.

·         Turn on all valves.

·         Pressure test for the seal of two-way check valve, hold and monitor the 4000 psi for 15 minutes. Without visible leakage and pressure, increase in the pressure gauge of pump truck is acceptable.

4.      Pressure test for S.S.V.

·         Turn off the mainly S.S.V.

·         Decrease the annular space pressure between the production valve &amp;amp; swab valve &amp;amp; pump truck &amp;amp; S.S.V. to 1000 psi.

·         Keep the pressure of annular space between two-way check valve and mainly SSV at 4000psi. Hold and monitor for 15 minutes.

·         Without visible pressure increase appeared in the pressure gauge of pump truck is acceptable

5.      Pressure test for upper master-valve

·         Turn off the upper master-valve

·         Turn on the mainly S.S.V. and decrease the annular space pressure between the production valve &amp;amp; swab valve &amp;amp; pump truck &amp;amp; upper master-valve to 1000 psi.

·         Keep the pressure of annular space between two-way check valve and upper master-valve at 4000psi. Hold and monitor for 15 minutes.

·         Without visible pressure increase appeared in the pressure gauge of pump truck is acceptable.

6.      Pressure test for down master-valve

·         Turn off the down master-valve.

·         Keep the annular space pressure between the production valve &amp;amp; swab valve &amp;amp; pump truck&amp;amp; down master-valve to 1000 psi.

·         The pressure of annular space between two-way valve and down master-valve at 4000 psi .Hold and monitor for 15 minutes.

·         Without visible pressure increase appeared in the pressure gauge of pump truck is acceptable.

·         Reduce the annular space pressure to 0.

·         Turn on the down master-valve and swab valve, take apart the Tree-cap, then take out the two-way check valve and make up the Tree-cap.

7.       Pressure test for the down master-valve.

·         Turn off the down master-valve &amp;amp; swab valve.

·         Test the annular space between the down master-valve &amp;amp; swab valve &amp;amp; production valve &amp;amp;pump truck for 4000 psi.

·         Hold and monitor 15 minutes. Without visible pressure increase appeared in the pressure gauge of pump truck is acceptable.

8.      Pressure test for the upper master-valve.

·         Turn off the upper master-valve.

·         Turn on the down master-valve.

·         Test the annular space between the upper master-valve &amp;amp; swab valve &amp;amp; production valve &amp;amp;pump truck for 4000psi.

·         Hold and monitor for 15 minutes. Without visible pressure increase appeared in the pressure gauge of pump truck is acceptable.

9.      Pressure test for the S.S.V.

·         Turn off the S.S.V,

·         Turn on the upper master-valve.

·         Test the annular space between the upper master-valve &amp;amp; swab valve &amp;amp; production valve &amp;amp;pump truck connection pipe for4000 psi.

·         Hold and monitor 15 minutes. Without visible pressure increase appeared in the pressure gauge of pump truck is acceptable.

·         Reduce the pressure to 0 and turn off the all valve.

10.   Pressure test for Swab valve and production valve

·         Turn off S.S.V, production valve and swab valve.

·         Close kill valve and decrease pressure form pump truck to 1000psi.

·         Hold and monitor 15 minutes, without visible pressure increase appeared in the pressure gauge of pump truck is acceptable.

·         Reduce the pressure to 0 and turn off the all valve.
