14.1              General Quality, Health, Safety &amp;amp; Environmental Requirements

Ø  PPL/PEDEC’s committed to conducting operations in a manner which minimizes the risks to the health and safety of those involved in, and affected by, such operations. PPL/PEDEC’s also committed to conducting its operations in a manner which minimizes the impact on natural and ‘built’ environments in the area of operations.

Ø  This section sets out minimum Quality, Health, Safety and Environmental (QHSE) requirements for the WORK that MSA and subcontractors will be required to comply with whilst conducting operations for PPL/PEDEC.

Ø  PPL/PEDEC may perform audits and assessments of MSA’s and its subcontractors’ performance under the CONTRACT. PPL/PEDEC reserves the right without prior notice to conduct quality, health, safety, security and environmental audits of the operations.

Ø  MSA shall at all times be responsible for performing the WORK in a manner so as to protect against loss of life, injury to people, damage to property and the environment.  The detailed manner means and methods of performing the WORK shall be under the control and direction of MSA.

Ø  Prior to the start of Operations, certain QHSE processes must be completed. These QHSE processes include developing the final QHSE plan format and frequency of any QHSE audits, permitting and licensing and PEDEC’s approvals. MSA shall ensure that sufficient resources are dedicated to this task to ensure completion prior to mobilization.

Ø  PPL/PEDEC may at any time stop the WORK or any portion of the WORK without penalty to PPL/PEDE Cif the WORK is not conducted in accordance with the Quality, Health, Safety or Environmental guidelines specified in this CONTRACT or by the laws of the appropriate jurisdiction. PPL/PEDEC reserves the right to require MSA to remove any person from the operations in the case of non-compliance with QHSE procedures. PPL/PEDEC may also prohibit the use of equipment and plant in cases where that equipment or plant does not meet the required standards or is deemed unsafe.

Ø  MSA shall ensure that activities associated with this CONTRACT are conducted in compliance with applicable national and local HSE laws and regulations, MSA’s standards and PEDEC’s requirements and IADC documents.

Ø  Limits of Authority

Ø  PEDEC’s Representative(s) do not have the authority to relax health, safety or environment standards. If they judge the operation to be inadequate with regards to any aspect of quality, health, safety, security or the environment, then the operation may be immediately suspended.

Ø  MSA shall be required to develop a project-specific QHSE plan to manage the WORK and associated risks. This plan shall, as a minimum, address topics included in the list detailed in Item 7. Where existing MSA QHSE publications detail the topics listed, it is sufficient to either include them verbatim, or provide reference to where they may be found in MSA’s QHSE Manuals. The final project-specific QHSE plan shall satisfy MSA standards, PPL/PEDEC requirements and applicable HSE laws and regulations.

Ø  MSA should establish an effective HSE system and implement it strictly.

Ø  MSA must adhere to the standards and regulations of Health, Safe and Environment constituted by the local government.

Ø  MSA must strictly adhere to the procedures / standards and regulations of Health, Safety and Environment promulgated by NIOC.

Ø  MSA should comply with all applicable local government regulations including guidelines and recommended practices and any other Iranian authorities having jurisdiction.

Ø  All personnel should respect the local culture, traditions and social values of the indigenous population of the Iran and South Azadegan region.

Ø  MSA shall hire qualified and experienced worker and familiar his personnel with hazards especially with H2S and Mine and UXO (unexploded ordinance) according to related procedure.

Ø  MSA shall conduct proper training about UXO (unexploded ordinance) and mine awareness to all personnel

14.2              Health &amp;amp; Safety Management

As per national/local and client (PPL/PEDEC) standards and MSA/OEOC HSE plan. Following are minimum requirement for the AZNS project:

Ø  MSA/OEOC shall take all necessary safety measures in relation to the WORK to be provided and shall conduct itself and its work force in such a way as to comply at all times with the provisions of the national and local health and safety regulations pertinent to the contracted Scope of WORK.

Ø  MSA/OEOC shall also comply with all and any of PPL/PEDEC’S safety standards and requirements as particularly applicable to the Operating Area and/or as may be imposed by PPL/PEDEC from time to time.

Ø  MSA/OEOC and its subcontractors shall take all necessary steps to provide a safe and healthy working environment for employees, PPL/PEDEC’s personnel and third parties in the performance of the WORK.

Ø  MSA/OEOC shall operate a management system that ensures:

Ø  MSA/OEOC’s and sub contractors’ personnel operate safe systems of work at all times for the performance of the WORK.

Ø  Hazards associated with the work are identified and appropriate actions are taken to prevent accidents.

Ø  Risks to safety and health of personnel involved in the WORK are identified and assessed, and any actions and measurements are implemented to either eliminate or reduce these risks to a level that is considered as low as reasonably practicable, given the nature of the WORK.

Ø  Personnel are aware of the identified hazards and risks to their safety and health and to the safety and health of others. The detailed safe working procedures established by MSA/OEOC to ensure that the WORK will be conducted with due regard to the QHSE aspects, shall be detailed or referenced in the QHSE plan. Copies of the source documents shall be provided to PPL/PEDEC if the procedures are referenced only.

**QHSE Representative:**

Ø  MSA/OEOC shall provide a dedicated, on-crew QHSE Representative. The primary responsibility of the QHSE Representative shall include, but not be limited to, the maintenance and monitoring of the implementation of HSE guidelines and procedures and where required provide HSE awareness training for the crew. Such activities shall be approved and actively supported by MSA/OEOC at corporate management level.

**Training and Competence:**

Ø  MSA/OEOC shall ensure that its employees and those of its subcontractors are trained and competent to perform the WORK in a safe and environmentally responsible manner. Such training and demonstration of competence will include but not be limited to vocational, safety, emergency, environmental and other training required by regulatory agencies and IADC/OGP guidelines. MSA/OEOC’s senior staff shall have received training in safety management.

**Accident/Incident Reporting:**

Ø  MSA/OEOC shall report all incidents. Any hazardous incident/near miss involving PPL/PEDEC, MSA/OEOC’s, or any third-party personnel, plant or equipment, shall be reported to PPL/PEDEC, whether or not injury to personnel or damage/loss to plant or equipment resulted. The following incidents shall be verbally reported immediately to the on-site PPL/PEDEC Representative(s): damage to property or equipment belonging to PPL/PEDEC, third parties, MSA/OEOC or its subcontractors; injury to personnel of PPL/PEDEC, third parties, subcontractors or MSA/OEOC; near misses which may have had serious potential consequences; environmental damage; media attention. An initial written report, containing factual information only, shall be prepared by MSA/OEOC and delivered to the PPL/PEDEC Representative within twenty-four (24) hours of the incident.

Ø  PPL/PEDEC reserves the right to participate in the investigation of any incident arising out of performance of the WORK.

Ø  MSA/OEOC and all subcontractors shall have an accident and incident reporting system, details of which shall be included in the QHSE plan.

Ø  MSA/OEOC shall maintain and forward to PPL/PEDEC, a monthly summary of its safety performance.

Ø  MSA/OEOC shall prepare and forward to PPL/PEDEC, a weekly report stating all incidents and near misses that occurred during that week.

Ø  All MSA/OEOC and subcontractor personnel and PPL/PEDEC Representative shall attend safety meetings on a regular basis. PPL/PEDEC Representative shall be given a copy of the minutes of the meetings.

**Safety Equipment &amp;amp; Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements:**

Ø  MSA/OEOC shall ensure that appropriate PPE compliant to national standards is supplied to MSA/OEOC’s personnel involved in the WORK. PPL/PEDEC intends to use water-based mud and hence MSA/OEOC’s Personnel that may be exposed to this must be provided with appropriate PPE.

Ø  MSA/OEOC shall be solely liable for all costs in equipping its own and all other personnel on contract to, or under the control of, MSA/OEOC with the required safety equipment. MSA/OEOC will provide to all MSA/OEOC’s Personnel appropriate PPE throughout the WORK. Any defective PPE will be replaced without delay. Personnel without the correct PPE will not be allowed to continue work, until replacement PPE has been issued. If any person is disallowed to work owing to inadequate PPE, then PPL/PEDEC will deduct his day- rate from MSA/OEOC’s invoice.

Ø  MSA/OEOC shall detail in the QHSE plan the PPE proposed for issue to the crew. This proposal should include the arrangements for replacement (due to wear and tear and damage) of this equipment.

Ø  This well is committed to develop for oil in a responsible manner that promotes employees' and local inhabitants' health.

Ø  A trained Paramedic and proper MEDIVAC equipment and ambulance shall be stationed on the drilling rig during the drilling campaign.

Ø  An emergency medical evacuation plan shall be coordinated, and shall keep in touch with emergency response centers manned by qualified doctor 24-hours per day in Tehran or Ahwaz city.

Ø  Medical emergency report and investigation shall be performed as soon as possible in accordance with Medical Emergency Procedures.

Ø  MSA/OEOC shall, as a minimum, conduct the WORK and provide personnel, equipment, facilities and services consistent with good oil field practices and OGP Guidelines. An assessment of the Contract Area with regard to “Environmental and Occupational Health Risks” and “Local Medical Support” shall be provided by MSA/OEOC in the QHSE plan. This assessment and the resulting “Health Risk Assessment Score” will be discussed with PPL/PEDEC, and a final assessment will be agreed.

Ø  To ensure the fitness of those personnel engaged to undertake the WORK, MSA/OEOC shall conduct periodic medical examinations of its staff and ensure that its subcontractors’ personnel are also subject to periodic medical examination. As a minimum this shall include pre-hire medical examinations of temporary local personnel and bi-annual medical examinations of its permanent and expatriate staff. Evidence should be made available to PPL/PEDEC to verify an appropriate program of immunizations consistent with the recommendations of the World Health Organization for the area of operations.

Ø  MSA/OEOC shall be responsible for the cost of medical examinations as required to provide PPL/PEDEC with medical certificates which confirm the fitness of MSA/OEOC’s assigned personnel for the WORK. Each drilling rig shall be equipped with a hospital, doctor and an ambulance type-2 level.

**Drug Abuse and Control:**

Ø  MSA/OEOC warrants that it shall obtain valid written consent of all Personnel to a search of property of such Personnel when PPL/PEDEC suspects that such Personnel have in their possession drugs and/or other prohibited substances or any other item likely to prejudice safety or security. PPL/PEDE will provide a representative to attend the search.

Ø  MSA/OEOC warrants that it shall obtain valid written consent of all Personnel to medical testing for the presence of drugs or other prohibited substances.

Ø  MSA/OEOC further agrees that any Personnel who refuse to provide such consent or consents or withdraws such consent or consents shall at PPL/PEDEC’s option be removed from the WORK and shall not, at PPL/PEDEC’s option, be assigned to any future services to be provided by MSA/OEOC for PPL/PEDEC.

Ø  MSA/OEOC further agrees that it shall immediately notify PPL/PEDEC in the event that MSA/OEOC becomes aware that any of its Personnel has been found in possession of drugs and/or any other prohibited substance. MSA/OEOC is required to notify PPL/PEDEC in the event that any Personnel provided for the WORK have previously been found in possession, or have abused drugs and/or other substances prohibited at Location. The acceptance of such Personnel for the WORK shall be at the sole discretion of PPL/PEDEC.

**Camp Standards:**

Ø  MSA/OEOC shall abide by all statutory Iranian governmental health and safety regulations, and maintain acceptable standards for cleanliness and hygiene for quarters, camps and the Operating Area(s) in general. MSA/OEOC shall detail the standards and facilities proposed for its camp in the QHSE plan.

**Emergency Preparedness:**

Ø  MSA/OEOC and its subcontractors shall have emergency preparedness and response plans plus procedures available at all times throughout the duration of the CONTRACT.

Ø  MSA/OEOC shall take all necessary measures to ensure that:

I. Potential emergency situations have been identified and assessed;

II. An emergency response plan, including clear responsibilities, is established;

III. MSA/OEOC’s management, employees and third parties are aware of response procedures and responsibilities;

IV. Regular drills and exercises are carried out to test the emergency response organization and procedures and that any resultant issues are properly addressed.

MSA/OEOC shall notify PPL/PEDEC immediately with respect to any emergency situation and shall provide regular updates on emergency planning procedures, tests etc.

MSA/OEOC shall detail in the QHSE plan a list of potential contingencies for which emergency response procedures are planned. The QHSE plan should also detail a schedule of proposed exercises and drills to verify the effectiveness of the proposed arrangements in place. Development and implementation of the above plan shall incorporate any PPL/PEDEC assigned personnel to the project.

14.3              Environmental Management

Ø  COMPANY shall comply with any and all laws, rules and regulations of governmental agencies having jurisdiction, which now exist or may be promulgated during the term of the CONTRACT, relating to the control and prevention of damage to the environment.

Ø  Without prejudice to above, COMPANY shall ensure that all personnel use the highest prevailing standards of care and diligence to prevent unlawful disposal of all waste oil, water and other waste materials or fluids which may accumulate or be caused by COMPANY’s performance of the CONTRACT.  COMPANY shall not dispose of any objects, scrap, waste, rubbish, equipment, fluids or fuel into the surrounding area or allow anything to be stored loose where it can be driven into surrounding areas by wind. COMPANY shall take all reasonable precautions to prevent pollution of any nature or kind from its performance of the WORK. COMPANY shall have contingency plans and procedures in place for such events.

Ø  In the event of any disposal prohibited by Item 3.2 above, whether by dumping, spilling, emission or otherwise arising from COMPANY’s performance or non-performance of the CONTRACT, COMPANY shall be fully liable for and bear the costs of removal of any such item(s) dumped, spilled, emitted or otherwise disposed regardless of the sole, concurrent or contributory negligence or breach of duty (statutory or otherwise) of PPL/PEDEC. In the event of any such disposal, COMPANY shall immediately undertake all reasonable remedial and protective measures required in such circumstances.

Ø  COMPANY shall notify PPL/PEDEC immediately with respect to any pollution, loss, damage, claim or demand (or occurrence which may give rise to the same) resulting from the CONTRACT. COMPANY shall report to PPL/PEDEC any incidents of non-compliance with legislative and regulatory environmental requirements that occur during the performance of the WORK. Without relieving COMPANY of any of its obligations under Item 3.2, if COMPANY does not promptly proceed to perform its obligations under this Item 3, PPL/PEDEC may take part to any degree it deems necessary in the control and removal of any pollution, dumping, spillage or contamination which is the responsibility of COMPANY under this Item 3.2, or which is due to any act or omission of COMPANY. COMPANY shall reimburse PPL/PEDEC for costs arising from such actions of PPL/PEDEC upon receipt of invoice from PPL/PEDEC. PPL/PEDEC shall have the right to deduct such costs from any sum due or becoming due to COMPANY under the CONTRACT.

Ø  COMPANY shall operate a management system that is able to demonstrate compliance with environmental laws, rules and regulations applicable to its activities, products and services.

Ø  MSA/OEOC and its subcontractors shall take all necessary steps to ensure that the environmental impacts of their work are responsibly managed and shall take all necessary measures to ensure that:

Ø  COMPANY’s personnel are aware of the environmental impact of the COMPANY’s operations and are sufficiently trained and competent to perform the WORK.

Ø  COMPANY’s personnel operate systems, which will ensure that significant environmental impacts of WORK are identified and managed in accordance with a commitment to legal compliance and continual improvement.

Ø  The environmental risks of operations associated with the WORK are evaluated and appropriate actions are taken to prevent accidents and reduce pollution, and that contingency plans are in place in the event of an incident.

Ø  COMPANY will have adequate processes for monitoring the environmental performance of their WORK.

Ø  COMPANY will, as a minimum, conduct the WORK and provide personnel, equipment, facilities and services consistent with IADC Environmental Guidelines. COMPANY’s proposals for environmental protection should be detailed in the QHSE Plan. This should include, but not be limited to:

·         procedures and precautions to minimize damage to crops and vegetation, the local ecology and disturbance of wildlife and farm animals;

·         recycling and waste disposal;

·         Clean-up and restoration of seismic lines, Rig sites access roads and trails, fixed sites occupied during the survey.

Ø  An ecological team shall be set up by COMPANY, with the purpose of collecting all waste, rubbish, food scraps, office waste and other discarded material from camps, created by the WORK. Such activities shall be performed on a daily basis. Such material shall be appropriately disposed of, according to PPL/PEDEC approved methods or existing methods established by COMPANY, which are proven to be acceptable to PPL/PEDEC. Well location and camp site shall be delivered to PPL/PEDEC without any waste, rubbish, food scraps, office waste and other discarded material. PPL/PEDEC has the right to hold Completion certificate till cleaning the well location and camp site by COMPANY.

Ø  The access road and well location construction shall be accorded with construction program of well location. It minimizes any impacts on the local residents, prevent all soil contamination, prevent all ground water contamination, and prevent all surface water contamination. Cutting and waste water pit shall be lining and drainage system shall be good and to avoid farm and season canal contamination.

Ø  Management regulation for transportation truck, drilling operation machine and tools shall be carried out strictly to avoid damage farm and trees, etc.

Ø  Well site shall be flat and clean. All the equipment, materials, drilling tools shall be put in order.

Ø  Control the rig noise to decrease the influence to surroundings while drilling at the inhabitation area.

Ø  COMPANY shall perform on site segregation of wastes prior to transfer to the transfer area and/or delivery to the transportation COMPANY in accordance with the following waste hazard classification.

Ø  Non-Hazardous Wastes (Re-usable, Recyclable and Recoverable Wastes)

Ø  Ferrous and non-ferrous metals, plastics, and wood wastes, PETs and potentially paper and glass

Ø  Materials shall be separately segregated and provision may be made for size reduction and containerization equipment.

Ø  The COMPANY/Generators are encouraged to seek for recycle/re-use alternatives based on the Local available facilities, for final disposal of these materials.

Ø  It should be noted that landfill disposal of metal waste materials and wood wastes shall be prohibited. For wood wastes re-use of and/or salvage of commercial timber, or deliver/release to

Ø  local community are recommended.

**Hazardous Wastes:**

Ø  Hazardous Waste, such as clinic waste, oil waste, waste produced by painting, insulation works shall be duly segregated.

**Facilities of environment protection supplied to well site:**

Ø  Mud purifying circulation system

Ø  Cooling water spraying and circulating system for drilling pump

Ø  Special recovery tank for deposed oil

Ø  Reserve house for valuable mud chemicals

Ø  Automatic mud weighting supply system

Ø  BOP stack is equipped according to drilling design

Ø  Define a separation area for gathering all waste according to waste management procedure.

Ø   Requirement of environment protection on location Sewage pit Area of the sewage pit: 1500 m2

Ø  Prior to spud mud pit and sewage pit must comply with the standard. Install cooling water spraying and circulating system for drilling pump and sewage circulating system for cleaning rig floor and equipment.

Ø  Install BOP stack and pressure test shall be operated according to the drilling design to avoid blowout.

Ø  Install oil supply lines and check whether there is any leakage.

Ø

**Management of environment protection on location:**

Ø  In drilling operation keep mud and sewage from overflowing. If it happens, clean up timely.

Ø  Mud chemicals shall be stored according to the standard and shall not be scattered around well site. If mud chemicals scatter while loading or unloading, clean it up at once. The sack of mud chemicals shall be recovered. Do not dispose it on site.

Ø  Enhance water management at well location and do not wash equipment with fresh water. Stop water flowing for long time. Overhead tanks shall be utilized.

Ø  Oil management shall be carefully at the well site. No oil dirt on site, no dripping and leaking at oil tank and manifold system area.

Ø  After the well is completed, reinforce the sewage pit ，solidify the disposed mud and have environment procedure fulfilled.

Ø  Install fuel supply lines and keep them in good condition.

Ø  All the drilling fluid materials shall be recovered and shall not be left at the well site after completion.

Ø  The environmental protection personnel from COMPANY and operator side shall check and accept the well site environment according to the regulation after completion. Only well site environment is qualified, the well can be delivered.

Ø  Transition Area for Hazardous Waste shall also be provided by each COMPANY in his allocated area,

Ø  PPL/PEDEC shall approve each area before use as well. The transition area of hazardous waste shall be:

·         Paved, fenced, marked and illuminated

·         Equipped with appropriate Fire Extinguisher and other emergency response equipment (e.g., Eye-Wash and Emergency Shower, appropriate First Aid kits, neutralizer substances etc.).

·         In compliance with the requirements of handling, transportation and storage of hazardous waste (based on usage chemical MSDS).

·         Configured to accommodate a safe physical separation of incompatible waste materials (e.g., acids, and alkalis, organic materials and strong oxidizing agents).

·         Capable enough to provide storage for the entire range of hazardous wastes generated during the work.

·         The area shall be provided with Spill Containment and means of preventing run off to and from the area.

·         All waste containers to be stored shall be appropriately labeled.

·         Hazardous Waste shall be transferred in a timely manner, within a maximum period of 48 hours, for any period in excess of this permission shall be granted from PPL/PEDEC.

Ø  Standard of utilization and discharging of wastes on location

Ø  Conduct drilling operation according to the design, drilling mud is needed before spud.

Ø  Sewage that cannot be recovered shall be put into the pit， do not discharge

Ø  Make full use of waste water. Water in mud pump and water brake must be utilized by circulating. Water that is used to wash drill floor, shall be recovered after deposition. The recovery rate of waste water shall reach 85％.

Ø  Disposed oil shall be recovered entirely. Recovery rate shall be 100％. Dumping of waste oil shall be prohibited.

Ø  In drilling operation, non-chrome thinner high temperature mud system shall be used often if engineering is qualified.

Ø  While drilling in special area adopt mud creation inhabitation techniques to decrease the waste mud creation.

Ø  After completion, all the mud chemicals, bentonite, clays shall be recovered and shall not be left at the well site. Mud in purifying tank shall also be recovered after completion.

Ø  In case of any flammable or noxious gas encountered, steps shall be taken at once to prevent kicks and blowout. Gas shall be guided into ignition equipment to burn it away.

Ø  Burning material that may result in serious smog or horrible smell at the well site is not allowed. For cement or barite that may result in granular dust pollution, operation shall be performed in a closed system.

Ø  For abandoned well, filled with cement plugs to seal the oil, gas or water formation.

Ø  COMPANY/Generators are required to transport all generated wastes to the location/facilities designated, and licensed by authorities and/or approved/verified by the PPL/PEDEC (as appropriate).

Ø  All wastes shall be transferred by approved Sub‐ COMPANY (which could be a 3rd party Sub-COMPANY of the COMPANY/Generator itself). The Waste Transporter and any other waste management service COMPANY shall be licensed in accordance with local regulations and are in compliance with such regulations. PPL/PEDEC shall verify and approve the Waste Transportation COMPANY by checking licenses and qualifications, audit and inspections, verification of human resources and received trainings etc.

Ø  The transportation COMPANY shall ensure that all wastes are transported in a safe and responsible manner.

As per PPL/PEDEC as main client and MSA/OEOC agreed plan.

14.8              Well Control

**1. Installation Requirements of BOP Stack and Control System:**

Ø  The distance between BOP control lines and relief lines shall be not less than 1m. Steel Gap Bridge should be placed in such a way to protect lines from damage by vehicle crossing. Sundries shall not be packed on the control line shield, on which welding operations are forbidden.

Ø  The air supply shall be separated from that of driller’s console and directly connected to the main air supply system, and shall be equipped with liquid/gas separators. Excessive bending and pinching on air hoses are forbidden.

Ø  Electric power to BOP control system shall be directly from the main switch of the power board, and controlled by independent switches.

Ø  Accumulators shall be in good condition, charged at its rated value, and ready for work at any time.

**1.       Installation Requirements of [Choke Lines and Kill Lines](#_Toc207016945), and Relief Lines:**

a)         Beside the drilling spool, one manual and one HCR gate valves on the side of chock manifold and two manual gate valves on the side of kill manifold shall be equipped, and the manual gate valve close to the spool shall be always open.

b)        The high-pressure co-flex hose shall be installed as straight as possible and fixed by anchor after installation.

c)         Relief lines (burning line and bleed line):

Ø  No field welding is permitted on relief lines and the connecting style of relief lines must be flanged.

Ø  The arrangement of relief lines shall take wind directions, dwellings, roads, oil tank areas, power lines and other facilities into consideration.

Ø  While the two lines go in the same trend, the distance between the lines shall be at least 0.3m, and the two lines shall be fixed independently.

Ø  The outlets of bleed line connecting with choke manifold shall be in a safe area which is at least 300m. The bleed line on the kill manifold side connecting with drilling spool shall be prepared and connected when necessary (about 70m from the wellhead).

Ø  At every 10m~15m, turning points, and outlets, the lines shall be supported and fixed by cement foundations with anchor bolts or ground anchors. Hanging portions shall be supported firmly. If crossing the stumbling blocks such as brooks or ponds is needed, metal bridging supports are necessary.

Ø  Pre-buried anchor bolts for cement foundations shall not be less than 20mm or 3/4" in diameter, and greater than 0.5m in length.

**2.       Pressure test value and requirements:**

a)         A pressure test shall be conducted successfully where there is no pressure decline in 5 minutes for a low-pressure test and a minimum of 10 minutes for a high-pressure test.

b)        Prior to each high-pressure test, a low-pressure test with 200-300 psi shall be carried out to verify sealing capability at the circumstance of low pressure and avoid washing out sealing elements.

c)         High pressure test should be to the rated working pressure of ram preventers or the rated working pressure of the wellhead, whichever is the lowest, or to the rating required in DRILLING ROGRAM. Variable bore rams should be initially pressure tested on the largest and smallest OD pipe sizes that may be used during the OPERATION. Annular preventers, with a joint of drill pipe installed, should be tested to 70% of their working pressure. The high test for Kelly cocks, kill lines and choke lines should be to their rated working pressures, each part in the choke manifold is tested respectively to its rated working pressures, the relief lines be pressure tested to no less than 1,450psi (10Mpa).

d)        When casing cup tester is used, the above test pressure should not exceed 80% of the internal yield pressure (burst pressure) of the exposed casing.

e)         The control system of BOP shall be pressure tested to 3,000psi (21Mpa) for its reliability before putting into use.

f)         Except that the BOP control system is tested with hydraulic oil, other well control equipment shall be pressure tested by clear water.

g)         Testing tools

Ø  All required sizes of the plug type testers, and cup type testers should be available for pressure testing purpose.

Ø  When the cup type tester(s) is used for pressure test, the connection of the cup testers has to be checked, to ensure it will stand the load during the high pressures test. For surface casing, the cup tester is to be set in middle of the first casing joint in the top, so the first casing connection (between wellhead and casing head housing) below the well head is to be tested too while testing BOP and wellhead.

**3.       Pressure test frequency:**

All ram type preventers, annular BOP, valves, choke and kill lines, choke manifold, Kelly valves and safety valves should be pressure tested at the following frequencies:

Ø Prior to installation where possible.

Ø After installation of wellhead and BOP assembly and prior to drilling.

Ø After the disconnection or repair of any pressure containment seal in the BOP stack, choke line, or choke manifold, but limited to the affected component.

Ø Prior to drilling into a confirmed or suspected high-pressure zone.

Ø At any time requested by the COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE.

Ø In any case, every one month or during the first trip after the one-month interval with a maximum interval of 45 days. This frequency is not required for shear rams. As a minimum, the shear rams are to be tested prior to resume drilling operation after 9-5/8” casing string has been set and adequate WOC.

**4.       Work Requirement of Well Control Equipment:**

Ø With shut-in casing pressure lower than 1000psi, while snubbing with annular preventer, drill tools shall have 18-deg shoulder tool joints, and the snubbing velocity shall not be greater than 0.2m/s.

Ø After shut off the annular preventer or ram preventer, with the shut-in casing pressure not greater than 2000psi, drill tools are allowed to pull up and down with the velocity less than 0.2m/s, however, rotating or tool joint passing through are forbidden.

Ø While drilling through pay zone and thereafter, BOP function (close-open) test for the BOPs shall be performed regularly.

Ø Kill manifolds shall not be used for drilling fluid fill-in.

Ø The maximum allowed shut-in casing pressure shall be remarkably indicated on choke manifolds.

Ø All gate valves of well control manifolds shall be tagged with serial numbers, and be indicated with on/Off.

Ø In case shear rams were used, after shearing the drill pipe with shear rams, retrieve the upper sheared drill pipe, lower a drill pipe joint with TIW valve installed into the hole and close pipe rams on it to prevent the possibility of shear ram’s failure.

**5.       Management of Well Control Equipment:**

Ø Well control equipment used by the drilling crew shall be managed and operated by designated personnel with clear post responsibilities.

Ø Well site shall have specified component storeroom and rubber element storeroom with air conditioners respectively. The temperature of storerooms shall meet storage requirements of components and rubber elements.

Ø At least 1 set is available as back-up for every type ram assembly in the well site. Ram preventer side door seals and ram rubber, every type gasket and bolt etc. should be enough for backup.

6.       Killing Method and Shut-in Method:

Ø  Driller's method is recommended for well killing.

Ø  The hard Shut-in method is recommended for shutting in the well in Fahliyan reservoir.

**7.       Well Control during drilling:**

a)        Shut in Procedure in While on Bottom

Ø  Position Kelly (if in use) and tool joint so that tool joints are clear of sealing elements.

Ø  Shut off pumps, check for flow.

Ø  If flow is noted, close the annular preventer and open remote-controlled choke line valve (HCR).

Ø  If the well has been closed using the annular preventer, check space out (pipe rams vs. toll joint relative position) and close pipe rams and ram locks

Ø  Bleed off pressure between pipe rams and annular preventer (if possible).

Ø  Record shut-in drill pipe and casing pressures.

Ø  Record volume gain and mark pits.

Ø  Weigh mud in suction pits.

Ø  Check blowout preventer and manifold for leaks.

Ø  Check flowline and choke exhaust for flow.

Ø  Check accumulator pressure.

b)        Shut in Procedure in While Tripping

Ø  If a flow is detected, install full opening safety valve and close same.

Ø  Position tool joints clear of the sealing elements and close annular preventer and open remote-controlled choke line valve (HCR).

Ø  Make up grey valve (dart type inside BOP on full open safety valve). Then Make up Kelly or top drive (insert a pup joint or single between safety valve and top drive) and open safety valve.

Ø  Record casing pressure.

Ø  Check blowout preventer, stack, and manifold for leaks.

Ø  Check valves for correct position.

Ø  Check accumulator pressure.

Ø  Begin stripping to bottom.

c)         Shut in Procedure for Empty Wells

Ø  Try to RIH with drill pipe as more as possible if hole condition permits, and the drill pipe must be installed a Kelly cock or safety valve.

Ø  Close the annular preventer and open remote-controlled choke line valve (HCR).

Ø  If the well has been closed using the annular preventer, check space out (pipe rams vs. tool joint relative position) and close pipe rams and ram locks

Ø  Bleed off pressure between pipe rams and annular preventer (jf possible).

Ø  Record casing pressure

8.       **Well Control During Running Casing**:

The well control while running casing is important and critical, best practices shall be followed, including but not limited to:

Ø  Change out pipe rams to casing rams prior to running casing into hydrocarbon bearing formation, if possible.

Ø  The crossover between casing and drill pipe has to be available, and good practice is to make it up with a joint of DP and keep on V-door.

**9.       Shut in Procedure During Logging:**

Cable shall be pull out of the hole immediately when overflow is found during logging. If pit gain exceeds the specified amount, the cable shall be cut immediately and treat the overflow in accordance with the shut-in procedure for empty wells. Continuing to pull the cable through the closed annular preventer is not recommended.

**10.   Well Control During Testing:**

Ø  No difference to while DRILLING OPERATION, since either there is testing string in the well (same as Shut-in procedure while on bottom), or tripping the string. (Same as shut-in procedure while tripping).

Ø  Likely there is some crude in the testing string, and precaution has to be taken while circulating the crude out of hole during killing operations to ensure it is properly handled without causing environmental impact.

Ø  To minimize the formation damage, the killing fluids used shall be weighted brine if possible, however in well control case when it occurs, killing well safely will take priority rather than protecting formation from damage on selection of killing fluids.

**11.   Well Control During Stimulation:**

Ø  Similar to during testing.

Ø  For any residual or alive acid to be circulated out during killing operations, measures have to be taken to treat the returned acid properly to avoid personnel from getting hurt, and without causing any environmental damage.

**12.   Well Control Drills:**

Drills shall be conducted only when hole conditions and other rig activities permit. Drills should be scheduled so that crews can practice drills while on bottom, while tripping in and while out of the hole. Each operating shift shall perform at least one BOP drill under different situations per month.

**13.   Basic Requirement [of Well Control](#_Toc207016944):**

Ø  For 13-5/8”, 10K BOP, BOP should be schemed as follows: upper rams 5”, middle rams are shear rams, lower rams is variable rams (2-7/8” to 5”). For easily connecting, armored fire-resistant 10000psi and ID 4-1/16" flexible hoses are recommended as kill/choke lines which connected with BOP directly.

Ø  The BOP stack and choke manifold, kill line and choke line, HCR and manual gate valves, inside BOP (including kelly cock) have to be H2S trimmed and stand the working temperature from -10 degrees C (in case of doing N2 for DST) to the maximum up to 100 deg C (estimated highest temperature condition).

Ø  The BOP equipment shall be visually inspected, function tested, and hydrostatically pressure tested during commissioning and Acceptance of Drilling Unit prior to Commencement Date, then upon installation on a wellhead, prior to drilling any hole section with a potential hydrocarbon bearing reservoir, after breaking any BOP connection (such as after installation of an additional wellhead section after running casing), and at least every 14-21 days while the BOP is installed on the Well.

Ø  CONTRACTOR shall submit the current well control procedures manual of CONTRACTOR to COMPANY for review and approval by COMPANY. Valid IWCF Well Control Certificates (or IADC equivalent) must be held by all tool pushers, Drillers (optional) at Drilling Supervisor level and Drillers and Assistant Drillers at Driller level, as further specified in CONTRACTOR Personnel HSE Requirements.

Ø  The accumulator must be of sufficient capacity so that it is possible to close one (1) ram and the bag, open a ram and the bag, re-close a ram and the bag and retain 1200psi accumulator pressure.

Ø  The “OPEN” and “CLOSED” operating positions of BOP activators of the rams, annular, and remote actuated valves must be clearly identified on the BOP master control panel and remote panels, in English in addition to the native language of the majority of the senior drilling crew.

Ø  Shear-ram BOP activator must have a flap-cover to ensure only pre-meditated and deliberated activation and to prevent accidental WORK.

Ø  All lines and connections in the choke and kill manifold, standpipe manifold, choke and kill lines and high-pressure mud lines should be welded hard-piping with weld-on FMC Weco “hammer-lug” 1502 unions (or Western equivalent, such as Anson) or weld-on API flanges. The well control system should not include any threaded screw-on hammer-lug unions, flanges, or other threaded screw-on connections.

Ø  All adapter or spacer spools between the wellhead and BOP must be manufactured in accordance with API 6A, and must be complete with all required studs, nuts, and ring gasket seals for both lower and upper connections; minimum spare parts should include two (2) OEM spare studs complete with nuts and two spare OEM ring gasket seals for both bottom and top connections.

Ø  There should be a wide-bore gas vent line from the “poor-boy” degasser; the line and line outlet must be securely anchored, the line outlet must be a safe distance from the well cellar, rig floor, choke manifold, and mud logging unit.

Ø  Well Control Equipment Welding: All welds in the well control system must be NDT inspected and records maintained of all welding and weld inspections, including choke and kill manifold, standpipe manifold, mud pump discharge manifold, choke and kill lines.

Ø  Well Control Rig Floor Information: The following must be posted on the rig floor (in the Driller’s shack / “dog-house”): Well Shut-In Procedure, Well Information Sheet (showing casing and hole sizes, depths, and such like), Kill Sheet (including most recent slow circulation rate pressures, formation integrity leak-off test information and MAASP, present mud weight, present drill string and well volumes, and such like).

Ø  The derrick substructure clear height (rotary table to ground level) needs to be enough for fitting in above BOP configuration (including a tubing head and a bell nipple). This need to be double checked in rig tender process. According to the calculation of height of BOP stack, the substructure clear height is at least 9 m.

Ø  In the case if drilling 6-1/8" hole becomes necessary, or using 3-1/2" drill pipe for the cleanup run (including drill 7" shoe track), then taper drilling string (5" DP + 3-1/2" DP) is to be run, so a pair variable ram be installed in the single ram preventer. The defect installing variable ram in single ram preventer is that the ram may be damaged and the string fall in hole bottom due to the ram hanging up too much weight when the drill pipe be cut. If the pipe ram be installed in the single ram preventer and the variable ram be installed in the double ram preventer, it would be very dangerous due to the variable ram failure in frequently using.

14.9              H2S Monitoring and Prevention Measure

As per PPL/PEDEC SOW South Azadegan oilfield contains H2S bearing formations, precautions shall be taken in place especially in 12-1/4” &amp;amp; 8-1/2” hole section (for typical Fahliyan vertical well) while drilling, completion and well testing operation.

H2S can be released any time while drilling, completion and well testing operation, therefore:

ü  The Rig shall be prepared for H2S (Training, procedures and protective gear).

ü  Make sure everyone on the Rig should be made aware of the hazard presented by H2S during their induction when they first arrive on the rig.

ü  The mud shall be treated to protect the drill pipe and the casing.

ü  All training program shall be recorded and reported.

ü  H2S emergency drill must be conducted frequently.

ü  Adequate sensors and alarms must be installed for the scope of monitoring the H2S releases.

1. General Information

1.1 Field Introduction

The South Azadegan Oil Field is located in Khuzestan province and is approximately located 80 kilometers west of Ahwaz city, near to Iran-Iraq border. The Field has an approximate area of 900 square kilometers. It is estimated to have 27.937 billion barrels of oil in-place (STOIIP), which makes it one of the largest developing oil fields in the world in terms of oil-in-place.

COMPANY has a plan to perform work over operation and Convert the 25 Sarvak wells from the natural flow production to the artificial lift production by installing ESP in the 25 Sarvak wells in the CONTRACT AREA. The wells are classified as oil producer wells with vertical or directional/horizontal profiles. Well production rate has been varied in a wide range between different wells distributed across the field. Initial production of vertical wells was 1400 -3000 BPD while production of horizontal wells was about 500-4000 BPD. The main objectives of Field Development are highlighted as follow:

 Phase 1: Daily Production rate of 320,000 barrels of crude oil

 Phase 2: Increasing the daily production rate of crude oil to 600,000 barrels (incremental

Production rate of 280,000 BOPD in phase2)

The development of South Azadegan Oil Filed Phase 1, is awarded to Petropars as General CONTRACTOR by Petroleum Engineering and Development Company (PEDEC).

The current oil production rate is declined due to high pressure drop as the main drive mechanism of the Sarvak reservoir is the fluid expansion. In order to keep the stable production rate, the application of ESP system is highly recommended in Sarvak reservoir of Azadegan oil field.

This scope of work is related to Phase 1 of Field Development.

Area Distribution

According to the drilling history, the CONTRACT AREA is distributed into three blocks as per the geological features with regard to DRILLING OPERATION. This distribution may differ according to knowledge accumulated in the future WORK.

Contract area is as per below:

X (m) Y (m)185640 3434275188020 3477361205224 3476408202842 3433327

Table 2: Area Distribution

Block I is located on the north part of the CONTRACT AREA in north of well AZN-010. Gachsaran formation is characterized by abnormal high pressure in this block.

Block II is located between well AZN-010 and AZN-011. In this block, Gachsaran formation is characterized by pressure tending to normal

Block III is located on the south of line well AZN-011. In this block, Gachsaran formation is characterized by normal pressure and all drilled wells in this block suffered from complete loss at Pabdeh formation.

The CONTRACT AREA is a plain desert degraded from a wetland with few human activities. The elevation varies from 1~4-meter AMSL (above mean sea level) from the west to the east.

Temperature: The climate in summer is quite torrid with the highest temperature 52°C, and it can drop to - 4.4°C in winter.

Rainfall: The maximum rainfall is 78 mm in the winter season (February), and there is no rainfall in summer season.

Relative humidity: Maximum: 96 %; Minimum: 25.9 %.

Prevailing wind: Maximum: 30 m/s (NW); annual average: 2.6 m/s; Monthly average: 2.0 m/s (January), 3.3 m/s (July).

2. Geological Information

2.1 Formation Stratigraphy and Lithology

The CONTRACT AREA is completely covered by the alluvium of Holocene age; the penetrated Formation from top to bottom is Aghajari, Gachsaran, Asmari, Pabdeh, Gurpi, Tarbur, Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan, Fahliyan and Garau.

1) The Aghajari Formation consists of a repetition of brown to grey calcareous sandstones, chert debris

and gypsum-veined red marl. A fauna of brackish to freshwater was observed, together with more

marine fauna.

2) The Gachsaran Formation with a thickness ranging from 400 m to 600 m, thicken towards the north.

Deposition of the Gachsaran Formation is cyclic. The cycle began with a deposition of shallow-water

marine carbonates, and then it was overlain by a thick evaporitic phase. The evaporites were capped by

red to variegated marl, which represented the end of the cycle.

3) The Asmari Formation in Azadegan Field developed a massive sandstone interval, with a few thin

argillaceous layers in the upper sections. Sands are clear, fine to medium-sorted, and poorly

consolidated. On the other hand, the lower sections consist of intercalation of sandy, chalky, slightly

dolomitic high-energy limestone with sands layers.

4) Pabdeh Formation is divided into two parts in the Azadegan field. The upper part is made of grey to

dark-brown argillaceous limestones and marls. Planktonic fauna dates that this part was deposited in the

Oligocene. The lower part is composed of dark-brown, slightly argillaceous limestone. Pelagic fauna,

mostly Globigerina and Globorotalia, indicates that this part was formed during the late Paleocene to

late Eocene in age. It seems that no early Paleocene Formation exists in the Azadegan area.

5) The Gurpi Formation in the Azadegan Field consists of grey to dark-brownish, slightly argillaceous

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

General –Procurement and Providing

ESP Running Services using

Truck-Mounted Rigs and Snubbing

Units (25 Wells)

micritic limestone with Maestrichtian to Campanian aged fauna. At Well AZNS-031, about 60 meters

of argillaceous limestones were encountered in the middle of the Gurpi formation, which contains

abundant fragments of rudists, bryozoa, corals, and Orbitoides.

6) Tarbur Formation: In the western Abadan Plain about 50 meters thick chalky limestone was encounteredin the middle part of the Gurpi Formation, which contains abundant fragments of bioclasts, suggesting a very shallow depositional environment. This interval is equivalent to the Tarbur Formation with reservoir quality in other regions.

7) In the Azadegan Field, the Ilam Formation consists of grey micritic limestone, often argillaceous, rarelypyritic, limestones. Microfauna, mostly pelagic, including rotalids and oligostegina assemblage, a few algae, bryozoa, and rudist fragments exist.

8) The Laffan Formation developed a thin greenish-grey pyritic shale layer, capping the Sarvak Formation. It was encountered in the Azadegan wells and only ostracods were found. It is a cap rock for the upper part of the Sarvak reservoir.

9) The Sarvak Formation developed a carbonate unit which was gradually overlying the Kazhdumi

Formation, and it was abruptly terminated by an erosion phase and covered by various late Cretaceous sediments. A Typical geological section of the Sarvak Formation in Azadegan reveals that dark grey fine grained nodulary argillaceous limestone interbedded with thin marls in the bottom, and graded upward into a white-to-buff massive chalky limestone with siliceous nodules;it was developed a very massive tan-to-brown limestone containing abundant rudist debris in the middle part; the upper part is made up of rubbly limestone with red staining and leached zones of breccia and the top of Sarvak Formation is very ferruginous.

10. Health, Safety and Environments

6.1 WELL CONTROL

All the drilling operation shall obey the requirement of Well Control Manual of MSA and contractor’s well control manual; under no circumstances should the deviation from well control policy be permitted without prior approval through MSA. If the contractor’s well control manual or anywhere has conflict with Well Control Manual of MSA, take Well Control Manual of MSA as the standard.

6.1.1WORK Requirement of Well Control Equipment

 With shut-in casing pressure lower than 1,000psi, while snubbing with annular preventer, drill tools

shall have 18-deg shoulder tool joints, and the snubbing velocity shall not be greater than 0.2m/s.

 After shut off the annular preventer or ram preventer, with the shut-in casing pressure not greater

than 2,000psi, drill tools are allowed to pull up and down with the velocity less than 0.2m/s,

however, rotating or tool joint passing through are forbidden.

 While drilling through pay zone and thereafter, BOP function (close-open) test for the BOPs shall be

performed regularly.

 Kill manifolds shall not be used for drilling fluid fill-in.

 The maximum allowed shut-in casing pressure shall be remarkably indicated on choke manifolds.

 All gate valves of well control manifolds shall be tagged with serial numbers, and be indicated with

on/Off.

 In case shear rams were used, after shearing the drill pipe with shear rams, retrieve the upper sheared

drill pipe, lower a drill pipe joint with TIW valve installed into the hole and close pipe rams on it to

prevent the possibility of shear ram’s failure.

6.1.2Management of Well Control Equipment

 Well control equipment used by the drilling crew shall be managed and operated by designated

personnel with clear post responsibilities.

 Well site shall have specified component storeroom and rubber element storeroom with air

conditioners respectively. The temperature of storerooms shall meet storage requirements of

components and rubber elements.

 At least 1 set is available as back-up for every type ram assembly in the well site. Ram preventer

side door seals and ram rubber, every type gasket and bolt etc. should be enough for backup.

6.2 Recording Reference

All BOP tests, drills, function tests, any malfunctions, repair or maintenance to the mud System and well control equipment shall be recorded in the IADC daily reports and shall be signed by both the Drilling Contractor's Tool Pusher and Drilling Supervisor on the well site. They shall also be recorded in the Daily Drilling Report.

6.3 Flow Check Procedure

To avoid a kick situation, it is recommended that a flow check be conducted at specific times during the drilling operation.

While drilling (any warning sign).

Prior to tripping the drill string.

While tripping (any warning sign).

While out of hole (continuously).

Trip out:

After pulling 5% of the drill pipe

At the midpoint depth of the wellbore

Prior to pulling the first stand of drill collars

After all the drill string is out of hole.

Trip in:

Upon reaching surface casing shoe

At midpoint of the wellbore

6.4 Primary Control Reference

It is the responsibility of the Drilling Contractor to keep the hole full at all times by using all the available equipment. The Drilling Supervisor shall monitor that the correct preventive practices are being implemented and/or conducted at all times.

Extreme care shall be taken to monitor mud volume, drilling breaks and gas cut mud.

The MACP (Maximum allowable casing pressure) shall be confirmed by the Drilling Supervisor, either after setting each new casing string or, whenever the density of the drilling mud changes.

The MACP shall be clearly written on a kick control sheet that will be posted near the choke control panel.

The predetermined distance at which the Tool Joint is to be pulled above the rotary should be posted on rig floor near the BOP control panel.

The Driller is responsible for carefully measuring and recording the slow pump pressure.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Units (25 Wells)

Awareness of these values is an important element in killing operations, in order to avoid formation breakdown.

Take a measure and record the slow pump pressure at three different flow rates with all pumps at the following times:

Once per tour.

Whenever changes occur in the mud density/rheology.

Whenever changes occur in the dimension and characteristics of the string, BHA, jet size, jet plugged or jet lost, etc.

6.5 Secondary Control Reference

Any time a drilling break is noticed, drilling shall stop and a static monitoring of the well shall be carried out. Space-out for all Pipe Rams and Annular Preventer must be known to the Driller at all times to keep tool joints clear of annular preventer and rams.

6.6 Well control during drilling and completion operation

The drilling design shall be strictly implemented by the drilling contractor and when it is discovered there is incompliance of downhole situation with design and the design will be amended, the procedure for amendment of design shall be followed. If emergency is encountered, and safe operation can be affected, after the discussion between drilling rig manager and the drilling supervisor, practical technical measures can be taken first and then report to the top management. The Company shall approve and notice in time as per the drilling program amendment procedure.

The curve of well equivalent mud weight as per predicted formation pressure, curve of mud weight in drilling program and curve of actual mud weight must be drawn during drilling operation. For exploratory well and key well, the curve of dc index while drilling formation pressure equivalent mud weight for sandstone, mudstone and shale shall be drawn by the comprehensive mud logging crew.

When entering oil and gas formation or drilling master reservoir, high diameter nozzle shall be selected for the drilling bit to treat well killing and mud loss.

SCR (Slow Circulation Rate) shall be conducted at the start of drilling activity, pump strokes, pumping rate and circulating pressure should be recorded. While drilling in pay zone, SCR is required to be conducted with all pumps separately as follows, pump strokes, pumping rate and circulating pressure shall be recorded in Daily Drilling Report and Kill Sheet.

Once for every 12 hours in general;

After bit change or BHA change; 3) Mud weight change exceeds 3.75pcf.

Oil and gas invasion and overflow shall be checked with wiper trip and shall be conducted under the following situation:

Each time before POOH after drilling oil and gas formations.

Severe invasion of oil and gas occurs during drilling, but overflow does not occur before POOH.

POOH after killing well.

POOH after lowering mud weight in wellbore.

POOH after curing mud loss during drilling oil and gas formation.

POOH after drilling oil and gas formation and a prolonged period of time is needed for other operations (E logging, running casing, running tubing and DST etc.).

Units (25 Wells)

Regarding the shut-in methods selection

Soft shut-in method is recommended for gas well;

Hard shut-in method is recommended for oil well;

Hard shut-in method is recommended for the well of which the well has strong formation strength in EMW as per FIT test;

Soft shut-in method is recommended for the well of which the well has weak formation strength in EMW as per FIT test.

Main technical measures for prevention of kicking and blowout during tripping.

Before POOH, circulation duration of mud in wellbore shall not be less than one and a half cycles. The observation time after wiper trip shall be no less than one and a half cycles. The density differential of inlet and outlet shall not exceed 1.248 pcf.

Flow check shall be conducted regularly via trip tank as follows

Prior to POOH (keep string rotation at 10 rpm for preventing stuck pipe)

POOH to last casing shoe

Before POOH BHA through BOP stack

Note: Tripping should be shut-off immediately and flow check shall be performed later on when any suspected well kick is observed.

During POOH, fill up hole every 3-5 stands of DP and every stand of DC. If the nozzle is plugged, during POOH, mud shall be filled full for each joint or continuous filling shall be conducted and trip sheet shall be recorded carefully.

When the bit is in the oil and gas formation and 300m above top of oil and gas formation, POOH speed shall be controlled to maintain the excellent well building property and rheological property of mud to avoid severe swabbing in the wellbore.

During RIH, the running speed shall be controlled to avoid the loss of circulation due to down hole pressure surge.

During tripping, check and repair of the equipment shall be arranged at the time when running to the casing shoe. if equipment have to be checked and repaired during POOH, due blowout prevention measures shall be taken during and after the check and repair, drill string shall be run to bottom and circulate for one and a half cycles. After everything is normal, drilling shall be resumed. Equipment check and repair shall not be conducted for empty well condition.

Treatment measures for invasion of gas during normal drilling:

When invasion of gas is discovered, it shall be discharged with circulation in time. The gas invaded mud shall not be pumped in the hole before eliminating gas.

Increasing mud weight shall be conducted when stop drilling and after invaded gas eliminated from mud. Mud weight incremental of each circulation cycle shall be controlled within 3.121 pcf

"In-post" policy

"In-post" will be initiated after the surface casing is cemented.

The "in-post" personnel must be trained and verified qualified by the technical staff of drilling rig.

During drilling, specific personnel shall be arranged to be "in-post", the mud logging personnel shall monitor the level of the circulating tank etc. as per the requirements. During tripping, other auxiliary

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

General –Procurement and Providing

ESP Running Services using

Truck-Mounted Rigs and Snubbing

Units (25 Wells)

operation or drilling suspension, specific personnel for "in-post" shall be arranged by the drilling and mud logging personnel in the meantime.

"In-post" requirements:

For drilling operation, variation of the outlet flow, drilling time, lithology, bubble, smell, showings, pit volume, density and mud viscosity, gas measured values and content of chloride etc. shall be carefully monitored. The level of the circulating tank shall be observed and recorded each 15 minutes and if special situation occurs, the measurement and record shall be intensified. If anomaly occurs, it shall be reported to the driller in time.

For tripping operation, trip sheet shall be filled accordingly. If anomaly occurs, it shall be reported to the driller.

For other operations, it shall be observed whether there is overflow of mud at the wellhead or mud level from wellhead. If anomaly occurs, it shall be reported to the driller.

Treatment of loss of circulation

Before cementing non-target zone or pay zone, if loss of circulation occurs during drilling, POOH shall be carried to run open ended drill pipe for cement plug job if condition allows. During RIH, mud shall be filled from annulus to balance formation pressure to avoid blowout.

Treatment of loss of circulation during drilling after production casing cemented

Mud level not at wellhead after loss of circulation. Stop drilling, pick up TDS or Kelly, stop pumps and observe with moving the drill string and prepare well control related work. Each 10 minutes, mud with density no lower than the drilling weight shall be reversely filled up from the annulus. Each time, the filling up shall be 1~2m3, or continuous reserve injecting mud with small speed to maintain that the column pressure of mud in wellbore is higher than the formation pressure. POOH to casing shoe or safety interval for observation. Additional treatment shall be made as per the situation of loss of circulation.

Mud level at wellhead after loss of circulation. Stop drilling, pick up TDS or Kelly, stop pumps and move the drill string to observe with well control well prepared. When the well is static, pull the bit upward to the casing shoe or safe interval for observation. If no anomaly is observed, circulate with slow pump rate. The measures such as plugging back job, POOH or condition mud etc. shall be carried out as per the situation of loss of circulation. If loss of circulation occurs to pay zone, mud weight shall be acquired by static pressure. After pulling out to casing shoe and observing for one tripping cycle, when no more loss of circulation occurs after running to bottom, drilling operation can be resumed.

Well control for E logging, cementing and DST

Before E logging, down hole condition shall be stable and static. If it takes long time for electrical logging, one more condition trip shall be conducted between logging. Shooting nipple is required for logging. Logging service shall be furnished with tools for cutting the cables.

Continuously fill the well during performing wireline logging, and keep closely monitoring for the well via trip tank.

Before running casing, ensure the well is in static condition without any flowing. Pipe ram shall be changed to casing ram with proper size. Casing circulating head or crossover sub between casing and in used DP shall be kept at rig floor at all times during casing running.

The hydrostatic pressure shall be kept balance with formation pressure during whole cementing job to avoid blowout due to loss of circulation, loss of balance for pressure and cement weight loss during WOC.

6.7 HEALTH

This well is committed to develop for oil in a responsible manner that promotes employees' and local inhabitants' health.

A trained Paramedic and proper MEDIVAC equipment and ambulance shall be stationed on the drilling rig during the drilling campaign.

An emergency medical evacuation plan shall be coordinated, and shall keep in touch with emergency response centres manned by qualified doctor 24-hours per day in Ahwaz city.

Medical emergency report and investigation shall be performed as soon as possible in accordance with Medical Emergency Procedures.

6.8 SAFETY

Due to high concentration of H2S in Sarvak, Kazhdumi and Gadvan reservoirs, Make detail H2S operation procedures, in particular, and carry it out strictly.

Lifesaving equipment like SCBA, Escape Mask, H2S detectors (Multi portable and personal detector) and implement the H2S Services system during drilling activity should be provided.

All lifting equipment and cranes must be certified by approved 3rd party (approved by Institute of Standards &amp;amp; Industrial Research of Iran)

All electrical equipment should be designed for such locations, and listed by nationally recognized testing laboratory. All wiring components and electrical equipment should be maintained in accordance with the manufacturers’ recommendation.

PSSR (Pre-Startup Safety Review) before spud-in and penetrating into oil and gas formations are mandatory by contractor under the supervision of Company and approved by Company.

6.9 ENVIRONMENT

Requirement on location

The access road and well location construction shall be accorded with construction program of well location. It minimizes any impacts on the local residents, prevent all soil contamination, prevent all ground water contamination, and prevent all surface water contamination. Cutting and waste water pit shall be lining and drainage system shall be good and to avoid farm and season canal contamination.

Management regulation for transportation truck, drilling operation machine and tools shall be carried out strictly to avoid damage farm and trees, etc.

Well site shall be flat and clean. All the equipment, materials, drilling tools shall be put in order.

Control the rig noise to decrease the influence to surroundings while drilling at the inhabitation area.

Contractor shall perform on‐site segregation of wastes prior to transfer to the transfer area and/or delivery to the transportation Contractor in accordance with the following waste hazard classification.

Non-Hazardous Wastes (Re-usable, Recyclable and Recoverable Wastes)

Ferrous and non-ferrous metals, plastics, and wood wastes, PETs and potentially paper and glass.

Materials shall be separately segregated and provision may be made for size reduction and containerization equipment.

The Contractor/Generators are encouraged to seek for recycle/re-use alternatives based on the Local available facilities, for final disposal of these materials.

It should be noted that landfill disposal of metal waste materials and wood wastes shall be prohibited. For wood wastes re-use of and/or salvage of commercial timber, or deliver/release to.

Local community are recommended.

Hazardous Wastes

Hazardous Waste, such as clinic waste, oil waste, waste produced by painting, insulation works shall be duly segregated.

Facilities of environment protection supplied to well site

Mud purifying circulation system.

Cooling water spraying and circulating system for drilling pump.

Special recovery tank for deposed oil.

Reserve house for valuable mud chemicals.

Automatic mud weighting supply system.

BOP stack is equipped according to drilling design.

Define a separation area for gathering all waste according to waste management procedure

Requirement of environment protection on location

Sewage pit Area of the sewage pit: 1500 m2.

Prior to spud, mud pit and sewage pit must comply with the standard. Install cooling water spraying and circulating system for drilling pump and sewage circulating system for cleaning rig floor and equipment.

Install BOP stack and pressure test shall be operated according to the drilling design to avoid blowout.

Install oil supply lines and check whether there is any leakage.

Management of environment protection on location

In drilling operation keep mud and sewage from overflowing. If it happens, clean up timely.

Mud chemicals shall be stored according to the standard and shall not be scattered around well site. If mud chemicals scatter while loading or unloading, clean it up at once. The sack of mud chemicals shall be recovered. Do not dispose it on site.

Enhance water management at well location and do not wash equipment with fresh water. Stop water flowing for long time. Overhead tanks shall be utilized.

Oil management shall be carefully at the well site. No oil dirt on site, no dripping and leaking at oil tank and manifold system area.

After the well is completed, reinforce the sewage pit solidify the disposed mud and have environment procedure fulfilled.

Install fuel supply lines and keep them in good condition.

All the drilling fluid materials shall be recovered and shall not be left at the well site after completion.

The environmental protection personnel from contractor and operator side shall check and accept the well site environment according to the regulation after completion. Only well site environment is qualified, the well can be delivered.

Transition Area for Hazardous Waste shall also be provided by each Contractor in his allocated area, Company shall approve each area before use as well. The transition area of hazardous waste shall be:

Paved, fenced, marked and illuminated

Equipped with appropriate Fire Extinguisher and other emergency response equipment (e.g. Eye-Wash and Emergency Shower, appropriate First Aid kits, neutralizer substances etc.).

In compliance with the requirements of handling, transportation and storage of hazardous waste (based on usage chemical MSDS).

Configured to accommodate a safe physical separation of incompatible waste materials (e.g. acids, and alkalis, organic materials and strong oxidizing agents).

Capable enough to provide storage for the entire range of hazardous wastes generated during the work.

The area shall be provided with Spill Containment and means of preventing run‐off to and from the area.

All waste containers to be stored shall be appropriately labelled.

Hazardous Waste shall be transferred in a timely manner, within a maximum period of 48 hours, for any period in excess of this permission shall be granted from Company and/or PEDEC.

11. H2S Monitoring &amp;amp; Prevention Measure

7.1 Monitoring H2S

Somewhere on the well site is apt to accumulate H2S, such as mud pit, shale shaker, and drilling platform, should be installed one set of. Make sure H2S monitor and alarm system can be used. Alarm threshold setting for H2S warning indicator: the first warning level is 10mg/m3, unable warning sound, just show present value of H2S content to operators. The second warning level is 20mg/m3, when the H2S content in air exceed 20mg/m3, H2S warning indicator can give an alarm automatically, and warning sound should be heard by everyone work in well site. The audible alarm should be installed on Kelly board.

Equip enough gas masks on drilling platform, shaker screen (total amount should large than 24), and equip 12 sets of 30min positive pressure Air Aspirators 2 sets of portable H2S monitor and appropriative H2S warning indicator. Arrange a person specially assigned for taking charge all the protective apparatus. This man must do periodical check to keep these equipment in a good condition.

H2S monitor should be done weekly check and compulsory examination.

After drilling into the pay zone, strengthen the detection of H2S content in mud.

7.2 Measures for H2S prevention

Windsocks shall be set on the drill floor and in the monsoon direction or/and prevailing wind direction of Azadegan oil field, off well site. In emergency, employees must follow the evacuation procedure.

Explosion-proof blowers shall be installed around the rig, shale shaker, and drilling fluid tanks to blow away toxic and flammable gas at the well site.

The rig crew in the H2S area shall be furnished with H2S monitors and adequate protective apparatus. Everybody shall be able to use, maintain, and check the apparatus.

The technicians of rig crew are responsible for H2S proof training and the tool pusher is in charge of the supervision and examination.

The pH value of drilling fluid in the H2S area shall be kept over 9.5. Pay attention to measurement of H2S concentration in drilling fluid. The H2S concentration shall be kept at less than 50mg/cm3 by using sulphur removal agents and degassers.

Personnel safety and protection shall be carried out according to SY/T5087 during operations in polluted areas where H2S content exceeds the critical concentration.

When the rig crew makes decision to bleed and fire because well control cannot be performed due to well site conditions, operations shall be performed according to procedures in SY/T5087.

Once blowout occurs, the incident shall be reported to the higher level department as soon as possible and firefighting trucks, ambulances, medical care personnel and technicians shall be on duty at the well site.

After the blowout is controlled, H2S concentration should be measured in the places where H2S is possible to gather.

The personnel are not allowed to access until the H2S concentration is below the critical concentration.

A.1. Introduction

The AZADEGAN Oilfield is Located in Khuzestan Province and is Approximately Located 80 Kilometers West of Ahwaz City, Near to Iran-Iraq Border. It is in The Northwest of The YADAVARAN Field (Fig A.1). The Average Monthly Temperature is 45ºc in summer, and Highest Temperature is 52ºc. The Lowest Temperature is -4.4ºc in winter. The water for the work in the south of the AZADEGAN will be supplied by tank truck from the water designated channel.

According to the drilling history, the Southern AZADEGAN Oilfield is distributed into three blocks as per the geological features with regard to drilling operation (Fig A.2). This distribution may differ according to knowledge accumulated in the future.

 Block I is located in the north part of the Southern AZADEGAN Oilfield in north of

drilled well AZA-10. In this block, Gachsaran formation is characterized with abnormal

high pressure.

 Block II is located between drilled well AZN-10 and AZN-11. In this block, Gachsaran

formation is characterized with pressure tending to normal.

 Block III is located to the south of line drilled well AZN-11. In this block, Gachsaran formation

is characterized with normal pressure and all drilled wells in this block suffered from complete

loss at Pabdeh formation.

The plan is to drill total 5 appraisal wells with vertical profiles on 5 well pads and all will be of producer wells. Totally, 6 wells had been assigned to be drilled throughout the South Azadegan oil field which Appraisal well No.1 (AZNS-030) was drilled to total depth of 3055m MD in Pad-27 in Sarvak formation and completed on 23 July 2013. The 5 remaining Appraisal wells should be drilled. These 5 wells are categorized to 1 Gadvan well and 4 Fahliyan wells.

APP-04 Well is the appraisal well in south Azadegan oilfield, Iran. This well shall be considered to drill to the Fahliyan formation. Plan is to drill the depth of ±4300 mt to 5” liner setting depth. Then 5” liner will be run and cemented. Tarbur, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Gadvan and Fahliyan formation will be perforated and tested by FBDST and finally complete well and released the rig.

A.3. Well Objectives

APP-04 well is located on pad 44 (Coordinate (UTM): 194483, 3454673, Zone: 39). This well is the appraisal well in south Azadegan oilfield, Iran, and shall be considered to drill vertically to the Fahliyan formation. Plan is to drill the depth of ±4300 mt to 5” liner setting depth. Then 5” liner will be run and cemented. Tarbur, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Gadvan and Fahliyan formation will be perforated and tested by FBDST and Collect PVT Sample from Reservoirs Fluid, then complete the well.

It is planned to take core from the specific intervals in Tarbur, Ilam, Sarvak and Kazhdumi Formations.

Petrophysical Logs (Full Suite, MDT and DSI) shall be taken through reservoir intervals.

VSP log shall be run throughout this well from target depth to surface to get more data and update velocity and structural model.

Default production formation is Fahliyan formation. But after perform all mentioned tests and interpret mentioned logs, production formation will be determined.

Fig A.3 shows the location of APP-04 on Sarvak top map.

A.4. Pore and Fracture Pressure Prediction

As above mentioned (section A.1. Introduction) the Formation Pressure of Gachsaran Formation is Different between North Area and South. This Oilfield is divided into three Areas:

 Area I (North of AZN-10): Area I located in north of Y-Coordinate: 3452051, in this

area, Gachsaran Formation is characterized with abnormal high pressure.

 Area II (Between AZN-10 and AZN-11): Area II located between Y-coordinate:

3452051 and Y-Coordinate: 3443549, in this area, the pressure of Gachsaran formation

decreases greatly.

 Area III (South of AZN-11): Area III located the south of Y-Coordinate: 3443549, in

this area, the pressure of Gachsaran formation decreases greatly and all existing wells

occurred complete loss at Pabdeh formation.

The area division shall be adjusted according to further actual drilling operation, and quantity of wells in different areas could be also adjusted accordingly.

APP-04 well is located in area I and Gachsaran formation has abnormal pore pressure. Fig A.4 shows the pore pressure and fracture gradient of area I. The actual formation pressure will be determined during drilling operation of APP-04 well.
