A.5. Program Outline

It is planned to drill and complete a Fahliyan Vertical Producer well to evaluate the Tarbur, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Gadvan and Fahliyan formation and finally complete the well as producing well.

A.5.1. 26” Hole Section

This section will be drilled ±151 mt through Aghajari formation. Aghajari formation consists of a marl, Anhydride sand-shale. For drilling this section 65-68 pcf Bentonite mud/Hi-Vis pill gel will be used for hole cleaning. Also Hi-Vis pill will be used to clean the hole and since bentonite has the best cake around the well bore, it will make a good cake for hole stability. According to previous wells in this field, this section is almost problem free. The 20" casing will be set at ±150 mt and it will be cemented in one stage with stinger (S.W.: 115 pcf, Accurate CMT program will be issued in due time). N/Up 20- 3/4" 3K C.H.H. &amp;amp; 20-3/4" 3K annular BOP and double rams.

A.5.2. 17-1/2” Hole Section

The 17-1/2” hole section will be drilled from ±151 mt to ±1256 mt through Aghajari formation and 55 mt inside Gachsaran formation. According to previous wells in this field, in this section there is a possibility of complete loss with No Return mud. Due to the Claystone and marl characteristic of the formation, bit balling is one of the main problems. Also tight hole might be experienced in this interval, so good inhibition will be helpful to provide stable hole condition. Drill this section with 67-79 pcf Saturated KCL Polymer Mud (CLAY-BOND mud). Run CDR/GR/CALIPER and Sonic log. Run 13-3/8" casing to ±1255 mt and its shoe will be set at this depth to case off full soft unconsolidated formation of lower Aghajari and drill the next hole section with higher mud density. It will be cemented in one stage (Lead: S.W.: 95 pcf &amp;amp; Tail: 118 pcf - Accurate CMT program will be issued in due time). N/Up C.H.S. 20-3/4" 3k x 13-5/8” 5k. N/Up 13-5/8" 10k BOP stack (13-5/8" 5k annular preventer + 13-5/8" 10k double rams with shear rams + 13-5/8" 10k single rams).

South Azadegan

APP-04 Drilling Program

Doc No.: NDCAZD-EN-WP-004-0 General Information Contract No.: MTN-94-854

August 2016 Page 11 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

A.5.3. 12-1/4” Hole Section

This Section will be drilled from ±1256 to ±1555 mt through Gachsaran. Gachsaran Contain Anhydrite, Limestone, Dolomite, Marl with High Pressure Salt Aquifer, Salt Bed and Salt Water. For Drilling this Section the 90-105 pcf Salt Saturated Heavy Weight Polymer Mud should be used. The Risks of Drilling this Section is Gachsaran formation has the potential of salt water flow. In the upper part of Gachsaran a weak zone has been experienced. Layers interbedded in the salts in Gachsaran Members 2 &amp;amp; 3 can have normal pressure, and therefore a reduced fracture gradient compared to the salt layers therefore Heavy losses might be experienced in Gachsaran. Also Tight hole/stuck pipe in this hole section is typically isolated to the Shale/Clay stones and salt beds. CDR/GR/Caliper and DSI will be run in open hole. 9-5/8" casing shoe will be set at ±1554 mt at the bottom of Gachsaran (5 mt above Asmari formation) to isolate Gachsaran high pressure salt water formation. It will be cemented in one stage (Lead: S.W.: 115 pcf &amp;amp; Tail: 118 pcf. Accurate CMT program will be issued in due time). Due to existence of salt beds at this section salt saturated water will be used for cement job. N/Up T.H.S. 13-5/8” 5k x 11" 10k. N/Up 13- 5/8” 10k BOP stack. (13-5/8" 5k annular preventer + 13-5/8" 10k double rams with shear rams + 13-5/8" 10k single rams). CBL/VDL/CCL/GR will be run to evaluate the cement quality behind casing.

A.5.4. 8-1/2” Hole Section

The 8-1/2” hole section will be drilled from ±1555 to ±3958 mt through Asmari, Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Dariyan and Gadvan formations which consist of Sandstone, Limestone, Marl and Claystone Contains H2S, CO2, Hydrocarbon and salt water. The risks of drilling this section is heavy drilling fluid loss (especially at Pabdeh formation), tight hole and stuck pipe based on offset wells. Also there is possibility for existence of H2S and CO2 Gases in the reservoir zones (Sarvak, Kazhdumi and Gadvan). 75- 84 pcf KCl –Polymer Mud (ULTRA-INHIBIT) mud will be used for drilling this section. Core will be taken through Tarbur, Ilam, Sarvak and Kazhdumi formation as per program. CDR/GR/Caliper, Full Suite, MDT and DSI will be run in open hole. Then 7” liner will be run to ±3957 mt (25 mt above Top of Fahliyan, Liner Lap @ ±1484 mt) and cemented in one stage (lead: S.W.: 105 pcf &amp;amp; Tail: 115 pcf. Accurate CMT program will be issued in due time). SBT-RBT /CCL/GR will be run to evaluate the cement quality behind casing.

South Azadegan

APP-04 Drilling Program

Doc No.: NDCAZD-EN-WP-004-0 General Information Contract No.: MTN-94-854

August 2016 Page 12 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

A.5.5. 5-7/8” Hole Section

A.5.5.1. Main Section

The 5-7/8” hole section will be drilled from ±3958 to ±4300 mt through Fahliyan formations which consist of Limestone, Marl and Claystone Contains Hydrocarbon. The risks of drilling this section is mud loss, tight hole and stuck pipe based on offset wells. Also there is possibility for existence of H2S and CO2 Gases. 95-110 pcf KCl-Polymer Mud (SHALE-DRILL mud) will be used for drilling this section. CDR/ Full Suite, MDT, DSI will be run in open hole. Then 5” liner will be run to ±4299 mt (Liner Lap @ ±3887 mt) and cemented in one stage (S.W.: 115 pcf. Accurate CMT program will be issued in due time). SBT-RBT/CCL/GR will be run to evaluate the cement quality behind casing. Finally VSP Log (Zero Offset) will be run from TD to Surface.

A.5.5.2. Testing Section

Perforate and perform FBDST at Tarbur, Sarvak (S3-6), Kazhdumi, Gadvan (G5) and Fahliyan (F1, F4, F5) by TCP-APR assembly from BTM to upper interval (Tarbur). Using CTU to stimulate the well if required. After finishing FBDST of each interval all perforations will be isolated by bridge plug and CMT (if possible) and then perforate and test next interval.

A.5.5.3. Final Section

Finally, after finishing FBDST of all intervals, all CMT plugs and bridge plugs will be drill out and clean the hole. 5” tieback will be run to previous 5” liner tieback sleeve (±3887 mt) and tieback liner to 50 mt above Tarbur perforation. Run completion string as per program (completion program will be issued in due time). N/Up well head and X-mass tree. Secure the well and release the rig.

B.1. Formation Description

A brief description of the stratigraphic units expected to be drilled in South Azadegan typical well has been presented in the following breakdown.

 Aghajari Formation

From Surface to 1201 m MD, Thickness: 1192 m.

Aghajari Formation exposes in the surface, this formation overlays continuously Gachsaran formation. Aghajari lithology consists of sandstone, siltstone, marl and clay stone layers so that it comprises of reddish marls interbedded with sandstone and siltstone layers.

 Gachsaran Formation

From 1201 to 1560 m MD, Thickness: 359 m.

This formation is composing of anhydrite interbedded with gray and red marl, salt beds of variable thickness and some thin limestone beds.

The Gachsaran Formation with a thickness ranges from 400 m to 600 m, thicken towards the north. Deposition of the Gachsaran Formation is cyclic. The cycle began with a deposition of shallow-water marine carbonates, and then it was overlain by a thick evaporate phase. The evaporates were capped by red to variegated marl, which represented the end of cycle.

 Asmari Formation

From 1560 to 1870 m MD, Thickness: 310 m.

The Asmari Formation in Azadegan Field developed a massive sandstone interval, with a few thin argillaceous layers in the upper sections. Sands are clear, fine to medium-sorted, and poorly consolidated. On the other hand, the lower sections consist of intercalation of sandy, chalky, slightly dolomitic high-energy limestone with sands layers.

South Azadegan

APP-04 Drilling Program

Doc No.: NDCAZD-EN-WP-004-0 Geological Information Contract No.: MTN-94-854

August 2016 Page 43 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

 Pabdeh Formation

From 1870 to 2253 m MD, Thickness: 383 m.

Pabdeh Formation is made of grey to dark-brown argillaceous limestone and grey marl, partly Claystone at the top and gradually argillaceous lime stones with marl, grey, buff, brown, soft, sticky with some nodular Chert increase at the base.

 Gurpi Formation

From 2253 to 2555 m MD, Thickness: 302 m.

This is formation consists of three main units:

a) Upper Gurpi Member

b) Tarbur member

c) Lower Gurpi Member

 Upper Gurpi Member

From 2253 to 2368 m MD, Thickness: 115 m.

This Member begins with light gray, gray, off white, soft to medium, sticky argillaceous limestone. The Upper Gurpi Member is mostly consisting of gray buff to gray with partly buff gray, dark gray, medium hard to hard argillaceous.

 Tarbur member

From 2368 to 2443 m MD, Thickness: 75 m.

Tarbur Member consisting of cream to light gray, light brown, buff, medium hard, II, A Limestone interbedded with chalky limestone and marl beds.

 Lower Gurpi Member

From 2443 to 2555 m MD, Thickness: 112 m.

The Member consisting of dark gray to gray, light gray, soft to medium hard Argillaceous limestone and light cream and soft. II, A. Chalky Limestone beds.

South Azadegan

APP-04 Drilling Program

Doc No.: NDCAZD-EN-WP-004-0 Geological Information Contract No.: MTN-94-854

August 2016 Page 44 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

 Ilam Formation

From 2555 to 2670 m MD, Thickness: 115 m.

This formation begin with off white, cream, soft to medium hard, pure lime stone and continue with marl grey, soft, sticky, red to reddish brown, clay stone, interbedded with Argillaceous grey limestone, at the base of this formation appear pure lime stone, white to whitish grey, medium hard to hard, some chalky with oil stained.

 Laffan Formation

From 2670 to 2677 m MD, Thickness: 7 m.

This formation is mostly consisting of shale interbedded with clay stone beds. The Shale green gray to light green gray, mostly brown gray medium hard, pyritic, medium hard, slightly calcareous.

 Sarvak Formation

From 2677 to 3344 m MD, Thickness: 667 m.

This formation is mostly consisting of off white, cream, buff to cream and white to cream, soft, soft to medium hard, chalky limestone interbedded with argillaceous limestone.

 Kazhdumi Formation

From 3344 to 3518 m MD, Thickness: 174 m.

In the South Azadegan Field, the upper part of the Kazhdumi Formation is made up of darkgrey to dark-brown Shale and marl, dark grey, the middle part developed light-grey and micritic to chalky limestone. The lower part is clean channel sands interbedded with argillaceous sands with streaks of shale and some anhydrite. This part is equivalent with Azadegan member.

South Azadegan

APP-04 Drilling Program

Doc No.: NDCAZD-EN-WP-004-0 Geological Information Contract No.: MTN-94-854

August 2016 Page 45 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

 Dariyan Formation

From 3518 to 3718 m MD, Thickness: 200 m.

This formation is started with grey to light grey, some cream limestone, which mostly are argillaceous. These layers are followed with off-white to cream, mostly argillaceous limestone. Some pyrite is probably occurred in this formation.

 Gadvan Formation

From 3718 to 3983 m MD, Thickness: 265 m.

The Gadvan formation divided to three part.

 The upper part appear with occurrence of terrigenous rock. The lithology is

composed og grey Claystone and some shale.

 The Khalij member appear with pure limestone, cream, light brown and in some

intervals oil stain.

 The lower part consisting of alternating of marl, argillaceous limestone, limestone,

Claystone, sandy Claystone and sandstone beds.

 Fahliyan Formation

From 3983 to 4300 m MD (TD),

This formation is start with light gray, light green gray, soft Limestone interbedded with Marl and Argillaceous Limestone and sticky Claystone beds. This formation at continue is consisting of medium argillaceous Limestone and medium hard Chalky Limestone beds.

C.3. Lesson Learned and Recommendations

26” Hole Section:

This section generally being drilled without any major drilling problem, Bits with Center Jet Application (18-20/32) would reduce Bit balled up possibility.

17 ½” Hole Section:

Pipe stuck and tight holes during drilling of Aghajari Formation and while tripping out for running 13-3/8” casing running observed in 17-1/2” Hole Section of nearby wells.

One of the main drilling challenge in 17 ½” Hole section is instability of Aghajari Formation in Red &amp;amp; Green Marl of this formation, Control Mud FL and adding KCl (as per mud program) by application of Polymer Mud From Below 20” casing point is highly recommended. The FL should be gradually lowered in Control range while combination of KCl with Long Chain Polymer would effect to Marl Activation properties. Time dependent behavior of Marl in this section should be considered and try to reduce operation time duration. Each 350 meter condition trip is required to find certainty about time dependent behavior of Aghajari Formation.

12 ¼” Hole section:

According to caliper logs, there was washout in Gachsaran Formation and should be considered in CMT program.

While drilling with inclination in the formation alternated with anhydrite and marl (Hard formation interbedded with soft formation), the well inclination is easy to vary, so check well inclination by Totco more than normal in top hole.

While drilling in massive salt formation of Gachsaran Formation, be careful of well trajectory and the salt’s cave-in/dissolving.

The Gachsaran will probably contain abnormal pressured brine due to combination of overburden pressure compaction and tectonic forces. So, high mud weight is required to prevent brine flow into the well bore. This is supported by the occurrence of several flows from the Gachsaran Formation in some wells of the field, where the mud weight was raised to kill the well effectively. Calcium ion contamination should be monitored more than 3 times a day.

South Azadegan

APP-04 Drilling Program

Doc No.: NDCAZD-EN-WP-004-0 Nearby Wells Contract No.: MTN-94-854

August 2016 Page 57 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

Well flowing in 12-1/4” hole section occurred. Adjust mud weight to prevention well flow and increasing in CA++ concentration.

8 ½” Hole Section

Erratic torque in some intervals and pipe stuck observed in 8-1/2” Hole section. Adjust mud weight, perform hole condition and spot pill periodically and optimize hydraulic of bit and HSI &amp;amp; JIF to solve mentioned problems.

Well flowing, gas flowing and observe methane gas occurred in this wells in 8-1/2” Hole Section. Monitor well carefully and Adjust mud weight.

Lost circulation is the main downhole problem in this part of south Azadegan field. The losses occurred in Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam and Sarvak formations. Adjust mud weight, pump LCM periodically.

The drilling cutting is very difficult to move from the bottom hole to the surface due to improper mud properties, especially in deeper depths. Then the cutting is easy to be deposited and cause sticking, particularly while stopping the pump.

Formation gas from Asmari, Pabdeh, Ilam and Sarvak formations containing harmful hydrogen sulfide (H2S) has the risks to harm site personnel during the operation. All site personnel should pay more attention on H2S hazards, and all H2S equipment should be on site and in good conditions.

Glycol/polymer mud is proposed for this section to combat with mechanical/chemical bore hole instability of Ilam &amp;amp; Lafan Shale. KCl &amp;amp; GlyCol percentage should be keep as per mud program and try by maximum GPM &amp;amp; Adjusting Mud rheology (based on Mud Program) to find good cutting transport and reduce pack off type stuck risk.

6 1/8” Hole Section

Mud weight cut is also possible in Fahliyan formation while BTMs UP without any gain observation in static. That is recommended prior each trip place HI Vis at BTM to eliminate gas migration. Any increasing MW without confirming with Office is not recommended, in some cases increasing MW would show reversed effect.

D.2.2. Sequence of 26” Hole Section Operation

 Make up 26” BHA as per BHA design. Tag formation at ±14m

 Drill ahead formation down to 151 mt (20” casing point in Aghajari formation) using hivis bentonite pill. Pay more attention to drill straight hole.

 Note:

 26" TD is based on 151 mt inside Aghajari formation.

 TD should be adjusted to have 1m of rat hole below casing shoe.

 The exact TD will be determined based on casing tally.

 Run TOTCO inclinometer at 151 mt or each trip to evaluate the verticality of the

hole.

 Ensure that all drilling tools and equipment are on well site and are in serviceable

condition.

 Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this section of hole are available.

 Enough mud material, LCM and cement should be available.

 Mud logging unit should be available from Rig Spud.

 At TD, Circulate and clean the hole. Check the shaker to ensure hole cleaning. Drop

TOTCO to check hole straightness. POOH to surface. Check Bit.

 Perform a condition trip including 26” reamer due to conditioning the hole prior to run

casing. If observe any indication of drag, run back to bottom. Wash and ream to make sure

that the hole condition is good.

 Perform casing running pre job safety meeting.

 R/up casing running equipment.

 Run ±151 mt (Approx. 15 Jts) 20”, 94 ppf, K-55, BTC casing with duplex shoe (Float Shoe,

20", K-55, 94#, BTC, stab-in type, dual valves) to bottom as per casing program. Casing

shoe should be adjusted to have 1 mt of rat hole and enough stick up (1.5 mt on rig floor).

Fill casing by non LCM fresh mud.

 Note:

 Take care when running casing not to set down excessive weight if tight hole or

ledges are encountered.

 Use 26" x 20" bow centralizer on each 3 joints, (Approx. 6 No.)

 Visually and mechanically check the float shoe for proper operation.

 Ensure that all casing joints have been drifted, including 20" Swage (If required to

wash Casing down)

 M/up 20", 94 lb/ft, K-55, Buttress, duplex shoe. If it is not already made up on joint,

soft make up on first joint, P/up and make up to the optimum torque. Do not engage

the tong close to bottom of shoe. Use thread lock compound for shoe connection.

 P/up &amp;amp; run stinger using the “C” plate and 5” x 18-3/4” centralizer. Sting in. M/up and test

cementing lines. Circulate for one casing annulus volume. While circulating, check the DPs

annulus for any return and ensure stinger sealing. Use more DPs weight on the string if

observing any minor leakage through DPs annulus.

 Cement casing as per program. Any minor adjustment will be done in due time. Displace

with mud (2-5 bbls Short Displace). Monitor for pressures. Record pressure. Sting out.

Check the float. POOH one stand, Circulate to flush/clean drill pipe.

 After cement returns to cellar floor, open the port on conductor &amp;amp; flush it.

 POOH to surface. L/D stinger.

 Keep the casing on the elevator until cement surface samples get hard. Check for casing to

be center inside conductor pipe.

 If there is no cement return to surface, a top-up job should be performed to fill the annulus.

Use same slurry weight as the primary cement slurry. Ensure the availability of adequate

X-over for connecting line pipe to cement line. The cement should be accelerated with max.

(2%) Calcium Chloride and no other additives. Wait for the top job cement to get hard.

 Check cement hardness by slack off weight.

 Note:

 Run pilot lab test for cement slurry.

 Take sample from pumped cement.

 Based on the results obtained from cementing, decision will be made to perform

top jobs.

 Cut conductor pipe. Rough cut landing joint and L/D C.P. and L.J. Dress and bevel 20”

suitable to install and to weld casing head housing.

 Install and weld Casing Head Housing 20-3/4" – 3000 psi on casing stub and test the sealing

of welded Casing (limit pressure to a maximum of 80% of the collapse strength of the

casing or maximum 400 psi). Align C.H.H. outlets with Cellar stairs.

 According to cellar height (3.4 mt) which is not standard, the top of C.H.H. should not be

more than 85 cm upper than the floor of cellar, distance between its top flange and ground

level must be 2.55 mt (If cellar is standard the distance between its top flange and ground

level must be 1.73 mt).

D.3.2. Sequence of 17-1/2” Hole Section Operation

 Make up 17-1/2” BHA as per BHA Design. RIH, tag top of cement. Drill out cement &amp;amp;

shoe and rat hole cement.

 Take special care for abnormal torques while drilling the Casing Shoe to minimize the risk

of shoe back off. Report problem immediately.

 Drill ahead formation down to 175 mt (25 mt below 20” casing shoe) with hi-vis pill.

 Circulate and clean hole, POOH to surface and P/up the same bit &amp;amp; BHA @ according to

BHA program, RIH to bottom.

formation), at the top of Gachsaran to case off full soft unconsolidated formation of lower

Aghajari and drill the next hole section with higher mud density and Provide sufficient kick

tolerance for drilling to next section.

or burning line.

 Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this section are available.

 Ensure that enough amount and type of LCM are available and keep ready to mix

and pump LCM Pills to cure losses.

 Before each condition trip and when the ROP become low, clean the hole with

circulating Salt water.

above Asmari) to isolate Gachsaran high pressure salt water formation in order to open the

D.5.2. Sequence of 8-1/2” Hole Section Operation

 Make up 8-1/2” BHA as per BHA design include Junk Sub, RIH to top of CMT (Top Plug).

 Drill out plugs, float collar, cement to 7 mt top of shoe.

 If During Cementing Operation, Bumping did not observe during cementing,

perform CIT W/3000 psi for 15 min.

 Displace new mud according to mud program.

 Continue drill out Float shoe and rat hole to 3-5 mt below shoe at new formation. Clean out

the rat hole, circulate clean. Work on junk sub. Watch carefully for any indication of

abnormal torque, since there might be the risk of shoe back off.

 Perform FIT at new formation (EMW should be equal to max. planned mud weight for 8-

1/2” hole section plus 2 PCF, Approx. 86 PCF based on mud program).

 Continue drilling Formation to 25 mt below shoe (±1579 mt).

 Circulate and clean hole. Work on junk sub. POOH to surface. L/down junk sub.

 Run CBL/VDL/CCL/GR log through 9-5/8” Casing to evaluate cement behind Casing.

 P/up new bit &amp;amp; string stabilizer @ 20 mt, RIH to bottom.

 Resume drilling formation to Tarbur Coring Point @ ±2368 mt (Top of Tarbur Formation).

 RIH W/8-1/2” Coring Assembly (as per coring program) to bottom. Start coring 54 m core

inside Tarbur formation to ±2422 mt. POOH to surface and recover core. L/down coring

equipment.

 RIH W/8-1/2” drilling BHA to ±2422 mt. Wash &amp;amp; Ream coring interval.

 Resume drilling formation to Ilam Coring Point @ ±2555 mt (Top of Ilam Formation).

 RIH W/8-1/2” Coring Assembly (as per coring program) to bottom. Start coring 27 m core

inside Ilam formation to ±2582 mt. POOH to surface and recover core. L/down coring

equipment.

 RIH W/8-1/2” drilling BHA to ±2582 mt. Wash &amp;amp; Ream coring interval.

 Resume drilling formation to Sarvak Coring Point @ ±2705 mt (Sar-3 Formation).

 RIH W/8-1/2” Coring Assembly (as per coring program) to bottom. Start coring 189 m core

inside Sarvak formation to ±2894 mt. POOH to surface and recover core. L/down coring

equipment.

 RIH W/8-1/2” drilling BHA to ±2894 mt. Wash &amp;amp; Ream coring interval.

 Resume drilling formation to Kazhdumi Coring Point @ ±3484 mt (Kaz-2 Formation).

 RIH W/8-1/2” Coring Assembly (as per coring program) to bottom. Start coring 27 m core

inside Sarvak formation to ±3511 mt. POOH to surface and recover core. L/down coring

equipment.

 RIH W/8-1/2” drilling BHA to ±3511 mt. Wash &amp;amp; Ream coring interval.

 Resume drilling formation to 7” Liner Point @ ±3958 mt (25 mt above top of Fahliyan).

 Note:

 Due to possibility of losses, 8-1/2" B.Bit, enough mud material &amp;amp; LCM should be

available in well site.

 Due to high H2S Amount in this field H2S services should be available on the rig

site.

 Test BOP’s and related equipment as per NIOC policy each 7 Days.

 Adjust mud weight according to nearby wells and as hole condition dictation.

 The Section TD maybe changed based on formation tops detected by the well site

geologist.

 TD should be adjusted in such a way to have 1 meters of rat hole for probable

fillings, before running liner.

 Material balance to determine the theoretical concentrations of additives in the mud

should be calculated and reported to WSS. Significant deviations from program

should be explained.

 Ensure that all drilling tools and equipment are on well site in serviceable condition.

 Ensure that adequate fishing tools are available for this section.

 Do not forget to perform SLM pipes while POOH.

 Do not forget to take Slow Pump each 12 hours.

 At section TD, circulate, clean hole. Perform wiper trip to shoe and observe well @ shoe.

RIH, Check for any fill. CBU on bottom. Spot 60 bbls Polymer Hi-Vis. Pill @ bottom. Use

5-10 lbs/bbl LCM (shell fish) if necessary.

 POOH to surface. If observed any indication of drag, run back to bottom. Wash and Ream

to make sure that the hole condition is good.

 Retrieve Wear Bushing. Perform pre-job safety meeting.

 Run Full Suite/CDR Logs (Based on well condition, TLC method shall be applied).

 Run DSI log (Based on well condition, TLC method shall be applied).

 RIH with 8-1/2” BHA to bottom, Circ Btm's up, Condition hole prior to logging, POOH to

surface.

 Run MDT Log (Based on well condition, TLC method shall be applied).

 RIH with 8-1/2” BHA to bottom, Circ Btm's up, Condition hole prior to run 7” liner, POOH

to surface.

 RIH with 9-5/8” scraper BHA to bottom, Circ Btm's up, Scrap 7” top PKR setting depth,

POOH to surface.

 Change top rams to 7”.

 R/up liner running equipment.

 Run &amp;amp; hang (With Top Packer) 7” liner as per liner program. Run ±2473 mt (Approx. 220

Jts) 7", 35 ppf, T-95, HSM3 liner (liner lap: ±1484 mt, liner Shoe: ±3957 mt).

 Liner shoe depth should be adjusted in such a way to have 1 meters of rat hole.

 Note:

 Ensure that the all Liners is drifted; cleaned, tallied and spaced out priors to RIH.

 Check Wiper Plug and Pump Down Plug with LDC for any leakage.

 Fill Liner by non LCM fresh mud every 10 joints.

 7”, 35 lb/ft, T-95, HSM3 Float Collar should be installed two joint above the float

shoe.

 Use 8-1/2" x 7" bow centralizer on each 3 joints (75 No.)

 7” x 9-5/8” Rigid Centralizers on third and fourth joints from top.

 Use thread locking compound for Shoe track.

 7” Hyd. Liner Hanger must be suitable for inside 9-5/8” CSG 53.5 ppf.

 Do not forget to remove wear bushing before running log &amp;amp; liner.

 7” Liner running procedure:

 After making up the shoe track, lower through rotary table and check that the floats

are holding. Fill up with mud and pick up to check float functionality. Circulate for

10 min.

 Run liner in at controlled speed to minimize pressure surges (approx. 12 joints/hr).

Check returns constantly.

 Fill up liner completely every 10 joints run.

 When the required numbers of liner joints have been made up, make up the liner

hanger with Top Packer, running tool as per liner hanger engineer’s instructions.

 Run the liner with 5” DP to 9-5/8” CSG, Mud Circulation to check String, Liner

hanger engineer should be on rig floor while running liner into open hole.

 NOTE :

 Check the loss while RIH if need Decrease the Speed of the RIH. SLM &amp;amp;

drift the drill pipe while RIH the liner.

 Continue running Liner to Btm. Tag Btm. 1 mt move up string. Circulate mud as

150% of string capacity.

August 2016 Page 78 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

 Drop ball and M/up combination plug dropping head to the last joint. Use pup joint,

if necessary.

 The Hanger will be set about ±70 mt above 9-5/8" Shoe.

 Try to avoid setting Hanger on Casing coupling. Pressurize inside Liner and Set the

Hanger as per Hanger engineer procedure and Shear LDC and circulate mud.

Release Setting tool and ensure that the setting tool is free of the Liner Hanger

(work string 0.5 mt up and down – record loss of weight as the hanger sets) before

start Cement job.

 Cement 7" Liner as per cementing program.

 Displace the cement with the cementing pump to the Liner Wiper Plug. Shear Liner

Wiper Plug (Record the volume pumped and shearing pressure). Displace

combined Wiper Plugs to Latch down Collar.

 Bump the Plug with 500 psi over final displacement pressure and 1500 psi for

bumping pressure. (Record and report final displacement pressure prior to bump

the Plug). If there is no bump, do not displace more than 25% of the shoe-track

volume. Displace with Cementing Pump and record cement losses.

 Hold bumping pressure for 5 minutes (If the Plugs bumped).

 If plugs bumped, pressure up and test the liner to 3000 psi for 15 minutes.

 Bleed off pressure carefully and check for back-flow.

 Pull out setting tool for two meters, check for U tube F/DPs. Set Packer &amp;amp; N/down

Cementing Head.

 POOH to top of CMT slurry estimated depth and flush string.

 Cement Liner as per Program and bumping with 3000 psi while perform casing integrity

test for 15 minutes. (While Mud Engineer should have level of mud Tanks and announce

any Loss or flow).

 Pull out Setting Tools. Set Top Packer. POOH 3-5 mt. Circ as 1.5 times annulus volume.

POOH to surface while WOC.

 RIH with 8-1/2" R.Bit to 7" Liner Lap while D/Out Cement of above Liner Lap. Clean the

hole. Perform Pressure test to 2000 psi. POOH to surface while L/Down last BHA and

excess 5" DPs.

 Note:

 Run pilot lab test for cement slurry.

 Take sample from pumped cement.

 If cement of above 7" L.Lap was soft, WOC to get hard, then D/Out cement.

D.6.4. Completion

 RIH with 5-7/8" J. Mill (M. Mill) to top of first cement plug, drill out all plugs and bridge

plugs to 5" liner lap, circulate bottom's up, POOH to surface.

 RIH with 5" Polish and Dress mill to top of 5" liner lap, circulate bottom's up, RIH to 5"

tie back receptacle, polish and clean inside the same, POOH to surface.

 RIH with 5" liner tie back assembly to liner lap (±3887 mt) and tie back liner 50 m above

Tarbur formation perforations (±2318 mt) and cement the same. POOH to surface and lay

down setting tools.

 RIH with 5-7/8" R.Bit and Clean well to new 5" liner lap (approx. = ±2318 mt), POOH to

surface.

 RIH with 4-1/8" mill and Drill out P.O.Bushing and clean out inside 5" Liner, drill out

cement plug and bridge plug to LDC. RIH to TD and Check TD. POOH to liner lap, perform

liner lap pressure test w/2000 psi, POOH to surface.

 RIH with 5-7/8" R.Bit + 7" scraper, Scrape 7" Liner (both Dry Test and completion packer

setting depth), POOH to surface.

 RIH with Dry Test tools and adequate water cushion to and perform dry test from liner lap.

POOH to surface and L/Down Dry Test tools.

 Run Completion string, Set the packer and test the same (Accurate completion string and

program will be issued in due time).

 N/Down BOP, N/Up well head and test. Complete and secure the well.

F.1.1.1. Drilling Fluids Formulation

This is a large diameter hole and the hole cuttings removal mechanism will be a combination of high annular velocities and hi-viscous sweeps.

Bentonite Mud / Hi-Vis Pill has been planned to overcome the drilling problems and increase the rate of penetration. Rheological properties of the system will be increased and kept in the optimum range by adding BENTO-GEL API at the concentration of 20 – 30 lb/bbl.

Soft dispersive clays and unconsolidated sands can be expected whilst drilling this interval. The formation is mainly composed of unconsolidated sands with some mudstone.

 Mixing Procedure

1. Fill the tanks with the required volume of Drill water.

a. Note: Drill water should be tested before mixing and if its hardness is more than

400mg/l, it should be treated.

2. Add 0.5-1 lb/bbl of CAUSTIC SODA to prepare brine to pH 10-10.5.

3. Add 0.7-1 lb/bbl SODA ASH to treat out any hardness greater than 400 mg/l.

4. Add 20-30 lb/bbl of Bentonite and allow hydrating for as long as possible.

5. Add 1 lb/bbl LIME to system to adjust pH

F.1.1.2. Interval Key Issues

 Loss Zone: There is a possibility of complete loss in this interval with No Return mud, so LCM pill should be prepared before drilling of this section as contingency.

 Hole Cleaning: Hole cleaning problems could be avoided by pumping hiviscous pill more frequently and of greater volume.

F.1.1.3. Engineering Outline &amp;amp; System Maintenance

 To achieve better Ca++ settling, pH have to be kept above 10.

 The Plastic Viscosity value should be minimized by optimum usage of the solids

control equipment and by dilution with pre-mix where applicable, to generate new

volume and / or reduce mud rheology.

 Yield point should be kept high (the program range) to reduce the annular flow

rates and gel value required to reach to maximum hole cleaning.

 It is essential to remove drilled solids rather than dilute with water to acceptable

levels. Therefore every effort must be made to maximize the efficiency of the

solids control equipment.

 Due to the hole size, and the likely pump rates available, a 6 rpm in excess of 12

is advised. In order to achieve this, a quantity of pre-hydrated BENTO-GEL API

will be needed in the system make up.

F.1.2.1. Drilling Fluids Properties

To solve problems associated with this interval and increase the ROP, Saturated KCL Polymer Mud (CLAY-BOND FLUID SYSTEM) has been designed to drill the formation and inhibit clay and marl problems in this section.

CLAY-BOND L has also been successfully used to drill clay interbeds in both saline and nonsaline systems. It is very important to determine MBT of mud during drilling and keep it in the program range. Controlling of MW could be done by running SCE and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens, start with 67 pcf MW and increase every 90 meter 1 pcf using salts and required BARA-WATE API up to 79 pcf.

Mixing Procedure

1- Fill the tanks with 100 bbl of Drill water.

2- Add 65-70 lb/bbl of SODIUM CHLORIDE AC (NaCl).

3- Add 0.5-1 lb/bbl of CAUSTIC SODA to adjust pH around 10-11.

F.1.2.4. Interval Key Issues

 Loss Zone: There is a possibility of complete loss in this interval in Pabdeh Formation

with No Return mud, so LCM pill should be prepared before drilling this section as

contingency.

 Bit Balling: Due to the clay and marl characteristic of the formation, bit balling is one

of the main problems. It is required to keep the KCL R-UPG percent between 2 – 5 %

and use CLAY-BOND L to provide cutting encapsulation during drilling.

 Clay &amp;amp; Marl Inhibition: Tight hole might be experienced in this interval due to

existence of clay &amp;amp; marl in the formation. Good inhibition will be helpful to provide

stable hole condition.

 Salt Water Flow: There is a possibility of salt water flow. Therefore close monitoring

is required to maintain Ca++ and pH level.

F.1.2.5. Engineering Outline &amp;amp; System Maintenance

 Mud weight to be kept between 67 and 75 pcf unless hole dictates, salts and BARAWATE API will be used to rise the mud weight. Controlling of MW could be done by

running SCE and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens (150/ 200 mesh size)

if possible.

 Dump and dilution is one of the best ways to keep the MW on the guideline especially

with clean mud systems. Running all solids equipment and dump and dilution

would be the best way to control the MW (after drilling each stand , 25 bbl can be

dumped from sandtrap).

 Rheological properties of the mud should be monitored to ensure maximum hole

cleaning.

August 2016 Page 106 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

 Contamination with cement will increase the rheological properties of the mud especially

the yield point. Therefore, prior to cement, YP should be reduced to the minimum level

if practical.

F.1.2.6. Lesson Learned and Recommendation

These recommendation were prepared based on lesson learned of previous drilled wells, they can be useful to drill this well if used.

 It is very important to determine MBT of mud during drilling and keep it in the program

range.

 Running all solids equipment and dump and dilution would be the best way to control

the MW.

 Due to undesirable hole condition and hard casing running, regular wash and ream should

be performed on each drilled stand.

 Increasing mud weight smoothly, improve hole condition in previous well.

 Regarding high ROP, pre-treatment is a critical item while drilling this section.

 Based on the reports of wells 84 &amp;amp; 93 (nearby wells of APP4), 17.5” hole section of these

wells were drilled with Bentonite mud system, at the end of this section while POOH

&amp;amp; RIH tight hole occurred. Improvement in hole conditions can be seen with

optimization of fluid properties and the use of appropriate inhibitive additives and fluid

systems such as CLAY BOND SYSTEM.

 Due to in the previous wells ,bit balling was occurred so Hi Vis Pill (periodically) and

Salt Water (optional) should be pumped in the hole for hole cleaning also TORQUE

FREE GB M600 &amp;amp; TORQUE FREE GB M300 should be added to system.

F.1.3.1. Drilling Fluids Formulation

To drill this section a Salt Saturated Polymer Mud with 115-125 pcf would be used. Salt would be used up to the saturation level (75 pcf) to prohibit the thin inter bedded layers of Salt in member 7 &amp;amp; 2 from being washed and also will act as a strong shale inhibitor in the system and maintain MW as per pore pressure curve dictates in the drilling program using BARAWATE API.

Mud Weight should be increased 1 pcf every 02m up to 105 pcf, more than 105 pcf should be done with company man permission.

Rheology of the system would be raised by using BIO-XCD (As Optional).

AMYLOSE LV, a modified starch would be used as a filtration control agent in this section. The main concern in this section is the effect of the formation water on the mud properties. If any problem rises during the drilling, AMYLOSE LV should be replaced with the PAC ULV at the concentration between 1-1.5 lb/bbl.

F.1.3.2. Interval Key Issues

 Salt Water Flow: Gachsaran formation has the potential of salt water flow. The

hardness of this water is between 35000-53000 mg/l, so any increase in the hardness

of mud would be an indication of possible salt water flow. Therefore, during drilling

this section, hardness of the system must be checked and monitored three times per

day for any increase in Ca++ ions.

 Losses: In the upper part of Gachsaran a weak zone has been experienced. Layers

interbedded in the salts in Gachsaran Members 2 &amp;amp; 3 can have normal pressure, and

therefore a reduced fracture gradient compared to the salt layers. Heavy losses

might be experienced in Gachsaran.

Losses have also been seen in the first shale layer of Cap Rock, its second layer from the top, so it is very important not to drill deeper than approximately one meter into this Member.

 Stuck Pipe: Tight hole / stuck pipe in the 12 1/4" hole section is typically isolated

to the Shales/Clay stones and salt beds. The stuck in Shales and clay stones as far

as the MW is adjusted correctly and FL is tight and the salinity is up to saturation

is not a matter of concern.

F.1.3.3. Engineering Outline &amp;amp; System Maintenance

 Mud Weight

In the initial mixing, salt would be the first weighting agent up to 75 pcf, then BARA WATE API will be used to reach to 105 pcf as hole conditions dictate. Controlling the mud weight meanwhile drilling would be done by running all SCE and dump and dilution. Pore pressure is expected to be marginally above the normal pressure in the Jurassic / Upper Triassic.

Mud weight selection is critical in this interval. In some offset wells, excessive losses may occur in the Gachsaran member 7 when the mud weight is higher than the optimum. On the other hand, in some offset wells, water flow could be encountered when the mud weight is allowed to fall down below optimum MW.

It is important to drill this section with the mud weight being kept as per the guide line, also by running all solids control equipments and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens; it is possible to minimize the ECD and the potential for induced losses.

 Shale Inhibition

Salt would be used for shale inhibition to combat the Gachsaran Marl/Shale’s. However, the very tight FL would be the other shale inhibition property of the system. Controlling the salinity up to saturation is vital to drill into Gachsaran formation against troublesome Shales/Marls.

 Rheological Properties

PV is always to be kept as low as possible by reducing the drilled solids concentrations of mud using the proper installation of the solids control equipment so that the hydraulics is optimized.

High gel values are required to support the high quantity of weighting agents while tripping, making connections and during survey times. PV should be kept in the range mentioned in the drilling fluid program.

A thin salt bed in Gachsaran member 2 is a red flag for Geologist that means reaching to cap rock is imminent, salinity below the saturation will cause the salt samples to be dissolved in the system resulting in no salt sample over the shakers.

F.1.3.4. Lesson Learned and Recommendation

These recommendation were prepared based on lesson learned of previous drilled wells, they can be useful to drill this well if used.

 Due to undesirable hole condition while tripping and casing running, performing wash

and ream on each drilled stand is the best way to have good hole condition.

 Availability and running decenter centrifuge to remove LGS in this section is critical.

 It is important to drill this section with the mud weight being kept as per the guide line.

Also by running all solids control equipment and dressing the shakers with finest mesh

screens; it is possible to minimize the ECD and the potential for induced losses.

 A low as PV is required in this section to eliminate Mud Gel Up by suitable SCE layout.

 Based on the reports of wells 93(nearby well of APP4) in this section flow observed

that changed the mud properties such as increasing hardness and Ca++, in order to

prevent flow, at the start drilling of this section MW should be adjusted 90 pcf and

increased it every 20 m 1 pcf up to 105 pcf at the end of section.

F.1.4.2. Interval Key Issues

 Swab possibility

Special care must be taken when the BHA is inside the previous casing. In contrary to popular belief, pressure does travel easily in drilling fluids, so tripping speed must be controlled to avoid swabbing.

 Stuck Pipe

The combination of different size of CARBO-WATE incorporated into the mud will form a thin and slick filter cake in borehole and prevent the risk of stuck pipe.

 Drilling Issues

When drilling through fractured lime stones, swabbing of hydrocarbons can be experienced. Influx due to overpressure vs. influx due to swabbing must be differentiated.

 Losses

Pressure differences between the different reservoir zones in this section can cause lost circulation problems. It is recommended to drill with as low as possible mud weight through the reservoir.

South Azadegan

APP-04 Drilling Program

Doc No.: NDCAZD-EN-WP-004-0 Mud &amp;amp; Cement Program Contract No.: MTN-94-854

August 2016 Page 116 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

 H2S &amp;amp; CO2 Gases

There is possibility for existence of H2S and CO2 Gases in the reservoir zons (Asmari,Pabdeh, Ilam and Sarvak), it is recommended to keep the pH around 9.5 to 10 and also using H2S SCAV P to prevent mud properties from being changed.

F.1.4.3. Engineering Outline &amp;amp; System Maintenance

 Mud Weight

A mud weight of 75-84 pcf will be used to drill this section, a mixture of Calcium Carbonate different grades will be used to reduce the filter cake thickness. It is preferred to use CARBOWATE bridging agent rather than the conventional Calcium Carbonate.

 Rheology

Mud Rheology was justified to ensure maximum hole cleaning in both dynamic and static conditions. Using BIO-XCD/ PAC UHV would help to adjust the YP and 6/3 RPM.

PV is always to be kept as low as possible by reducing the drilled solids concentrations of mud using the proper installation of the solids control equipment so that the hydraulics is optimized.

YP is selected to be in the programmed range. High YP values are recommended to reduce the annular flow rates required and consequently less hole erosion.

 Shale Inhibition

To provide maximum inhibition during drilling this section, KCL R-UPG concentration should be kept at 3%-5% Wt and GLYCO-DRILL and CLAY-BOND L should be added before entering to the shale interval.

 pH

During normal drilling operations, pH should be kept above a minimum of 9.5 in an attempt to minimize polymer degradation, to neutralize any H2S gas in the mud and to reduce the corrosion rate of the drill string.

 API Fluid Loss

This hole section will be drilled using ULTRA-INHIBIT FLUID SYSTEM. It is recommended to maintain the fluid loss below 3 cc/30 min using FL control polymers to minimize the filter cake thickness.

 Reduced Dilution Rates

GLYCO-DRILL GP improves the inhibition and stability of clays and shales and field data has shown that much lower dilution rates are required to maintain optimum mud properties. In some cases, the fluid can even be recycled to give further cost and environmental savings.

South Azadegan

APP-04 Drilling Program

Doc No.: NDCAZD-EN-WP-004-0 Mud &amp;amp; Cement Program Contract No.: MTN-94-854

August 2016 Page 117 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

GLYCO-DRILL GP improves filter cake quality and reduces fluid loss as the cloud point threshold is exceeded, the micro-emulsion formed by the now insoluble Glyco-Drill will help to reduce the HPHT fluid loss. This improvement in filter cake quality and the lower fluid loss will significantly reduce the chances of differential sticking.

F.1.4.5. Lesson Learned and Recommendation

These recommendation were prepared based on lesson learned of previous drilled wells, they can be useful to drill this well if used.

 Previous Wells show rheological drop may be occurred while drilling Asmari

Formation. Keeping YP in desired range avoids probable washout in this formation.

 Gas and oil influx have been recorded in previous wells, mud weight should be designed

to prevent influx in Gurpi and Ilam formations.

 The combination of different size of CARBO-WATE incorporated into the mud will

form a thin and slick filter cake in borehole and prevent the risk of stuck pipe.

 High level of inhibition is critical while drilling Pabdeh, Gurpi, Laffan and Kazhdomi

formations. Sloughing shale has been recorded in previous wells.

 Due to the importance of drilling this section, after drilling each stand in shale and clay

intervals the same stand should be Wash and Ream completely before connection and

continuing drilling.

 It is recommended to maintain the fluid loss below 3 cc/30 min using the FL control

polymers to minimize the filter cake thickness.

 Loss circulations may happen during drilling Ilam and Sarvak Formations. In case of

happening, LCM pills should be prepared and pumped to cure the loss circulation.

F.1.5.1 Drilling Fluids Formulation

SHALE-DRILL FLUID SYSTEM has been design to drill this section for increasing the performance of shale inhibition and reduce the torque and drag. This fluid system improves ROP during drilling by reducing friction factor.

The mud weight should be adjusted to 75 pcf using SODIUM CHLORIDE AC and raised up to 110 pcf using BARA WATE API.

F.1.5.2 Interval Key Issues

 Swab possibility

Special care must be taken when the BHA is inside the previous casing. In contrary to popular belief, pressure does travel easily in drilling fluids, so tripping speed must be controlled to avoid swabbing.

 Drilling Issues

When drilling through fractured lime stones, swabbing of hydrocarbons can be experienced. Influx due to overpressure vs. influx due to swabbing must be differentiated.

 Losses

Pressure differences between the different reservoir zone in this section can cause lost circulation problems. It is recommended to drill with as low as possible mud weight through the reservoir.

 H2S &amp;amp; CO2 Gases

There is possibility for existence of H2S and CO2 Gases in the reservoir, it is recommended to keep the pH around 9.5 to 10 and also using H2S SCAV P to prevent mud properties from being changed.

F.1.5.3 Engineering Outline &amp;amp; System Maintenance

 Shale Inhibition

To provide maximum inhibition during drilling this section, KCL R-UPG concentration should be kept at 5% Wt and GLYCO-DRILL and ASPHA SHALE NHP should be added to system.

 pH

During normal drilling operations, pH should be kept above a minimum of 9.0 in an attempt to minimize polymer degradation, to neutralize any H2S gas in the mud and to reduce the corrosion rate of the drill string.

South Azadegan

APP-04 Drilling Program

Doc No.: NDCAZD-EN-WP-004-0 Mud &amp;amp; Cement Program Contract No.: MTN-94-854

August 2016 Page 121 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

 API Fluid Loss

This hole section will be drilled using SHALE-DRILL FLUID SYSTEM. It is recommended to maintain the fluid loss below 3 cc/30 min using FL control polymers to minimize the filter cake thickness.

 Reduced Dilution Rates

GLYCO-DRILL GP improves the inhibition and stability of clays and shales and field data has shown that much lower dilution rates are required to maintain optimum mud properties. In some cases, the fluid can even be recycled to give further cost and environmental savings.

GLYCO-DRILL GP improves filter cake quality and reduces fluid loss as the cloud point threshold is exceeded, the micro-emulsion formed by the now insoluble Glyco-Drill will help to reduce the HPHT fluid loss. This improvement in filter cake quality and the lower fluid loss will significantly reduce the chances of differential sticking.

F.1.5.4 Lesson Learned and Recommendation

These recommendation were prepared based on lesson learned of previous drilled wells, they can be useful to drill this well if used.

 Due to the importance of drilling this section, after drilling each stand in shale and clay

intervals the same stand should be Wash and Ream completely before connection and

continuing drilling.

 Adequate shale and clay inhibition is necessary during drilling this section.

F.1.5. Completion Fluids Design and Program

F. 1.5.1. Clean up and Completion Program

This program describes the procedure to clean up and displace the cased hole from water based mud brine as safely and effectively as possible prior to running the completion equipment.

Clean working practices and good housekeeping as always are important.

All rig pits, ditches, and lines (including gun lines) should be cleaned using solvents and detergents. If it is practical, lines should be opened to check for any mud solids that might have settled in them.

All the pits, sand traps, and under the shale shakers should be cleaned out and washed down using high pressure cleaning equipment. In the pit room, all gratings should be cleaned, all the lights and beams should be washed down.

All cleaning should be done well in advance wherever possible. To clean pits and lines, 15 m3 of water containing 1 to 2 drums of CLEAN SURF should be mixed up and circulated through all lines, gun lines, mixing lines etc. This can also be used to clean the tank system initially.

 Pump should be worked at the maximum safe rate.

 The below check list should be filled by the supervisor in the site.

Equipment CompleteBrine Storage TanksTransfer LinesPill and Slug PitsReserve/Mix PitRig PumpsTrip TankPump Charge LinesCement Unit LinesChoke Unit LinesKill Lines

 It should be noted that all dump valves should seal with grease to ensure they are in good

order.

South Azadegan

APP-04 Drilling Program

Doc No.: NDCAZD-EN-WP-004-0 Mud &amp;amp; Cement Program Contract No.: MTN-94-854

August 2016 Page 124 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

 All ditch gates should be sealed with silicon on each side of the gate. This will need to be

replaced if the gate is opened.

 Under no circumstances should barite, bentonite or polymers be used to seal anything.

 All pump packing should be examined before starting the cleaning.

F.1.5.2. Displacement Design

To ensure effective mud displacement and water wetting of the casing, the displacement pill needs to be designed carefully. The use of a weighted push pills with a viscosity greater than that of the mud, will minimize channeling and ensure good cleaning of the low side of the well bore.

The best fluid for thinning the mud is the continuous phase of the mud. In addition, SPERSEEN CFL could be used to reduce the yield point and gel strengths. The yield point should be between 8 to10 Pa and the 10 minute gel to &amp;lt;10 Pa. The actual quantity of material required to do this must be determined by the pilot testing performed by the mud engineer to determine the most cost-effective treatment.

Throughout the drilling fluid conditioning process, the flow rate used should be the maximum practical rate.

 The drill string should be reciprocated and rotated during the operation. The combined

effect of scrapers being run in the hole, the high flow rate and the reciprocation/rotation will

help to remove/disperse large quantities of mud solids and general debris. The reciprocation

stroke should be +/- 10 m. and the rotation speed should be +/- 60 RPM

 During this operation, as much of the surface volume of mud as possible should be

removed from the pits to accommodate the inhibited water and the well clean up pills. Once

the mud has been back-loaded, surface preparation can be done.

 At least 150 m of pill/spacer coverage or 3 min contact time at the highest pump rates

should be considered.

 Pit levels should be monitor throughout the displacement operation to catch and prevent

an influx entering the well contributing to an incident.

K.1. Well Summary and Introduction

Hole Size (in) Drilling Section Interval (m) Mud Weight (pcf)26 151 65-6817 1/2 1105 67-7912 1/4 299 90-1058 1/2 2403 75-845 7/8 342 95-110Total Depth 4300 -

The main purpose of the waste management system is to keep the location as clean as possible from the drilling waste. The system collects the waste materials from the drilling operations and separates the solids from the liquids in order to have a final disposition from the liquid phase as well as the solids produced. For the Waste Management system, all the cuttings coming from the shakers, desander, desilter, solid control centrifuges and dewatering centrifuge/filter press are collected and treated. Also all the waste fluids such as mud and water are collected and sent to dewatering in order to have a good separation of solids from water.

The main part of drilling waste is waste water and drilling fluid waste so the main part of drilling waste management is reducing water consumption and treating drilling fluid waste which is a very serious threat for nature.

K.2.2. Dewatering System

Dewatering system includes a contained flocculation unit with pumps, polymer preparation tank and mixing system, and a Filter Press. Basically the dewatering system is the separation of the solid and liquid phases of the slurry, using mechanical and chemical. The liquid is collected in the coral and sent to the buffer tank #1 (or feed pump). It is then pumped to the dewatering unit and on the way to the filter press, a coagulant (Poly Aluminum Chloride (PAC)) and a flocculent polymer (Poly Electrolyte) are injected to the slurry. The mixture of

South Azadegan

APP-04 Drilling Program

Doc No.: NDCAZD-EN-WP-004-0 Waste Management Program Contract No.: MTN-94-854

August 2016 Page 155 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

the coagulant, flocculent and the fluid goes inside of the filter press where the solid and liquid phases are separated using the filter cartridges of the filter press. As a result, treated water is received from the filter press and collected in buffer tank #2 while dumping the solids to the corral.

The Dewatering suction lines could be connected to middle mud pit and all DWM buffer tanks. In order to use the dewatered water for making new mud and to avoid settling of solids in new mud, using as little flocculent material as possible is considered. Dewatered water is tested by NDCO personnel in order to verify the quality; if water is going to be used to prepare new mud, mud engineer must perform a compatibility pilot test prior using it, if test failed, water must be retreated and then the pilot test must be done again till the water is suitable for the mud.

K.2.3. Filter Press

A filter press is a tool used in separation processes, specifically in solid/liquid separation using the principle of pressure drive, provided by a slurry pump. The filter press is used in fixedvolume and batch operations, which means that the operation must be stopped to discharge the filter cake before the next batch can be started. The major components of a filter press are the skeleton and the filter pack. The skeleton holds the filter pack together while pressure is being developed inside the filtration chamber. The chamber however can only hold a specific volume of solids.

K.2.4. Buffer Tanks

Two rectangle tanks with 400-450 BBL capacities were supplied and installed by NDCO for DWM purposes. Tanks were used as per requirements to store treated water from dewatering system or collected from the pits; water stored in the tanks was pumped back to the rig water tanks to be recycled to be used for cleaning purposes or to prepare new mud.

K.2.5. Pump Transfer Package

Pump transfer package consist of two centrifugal pumps, two diaphragm pumps, two submersible pumps and one vacuum pump. Pumps are available for transferring all fluids from the pits, tanks, cellar, corral and oil trap as per requirements.

The Vertical Cutting Dryer uses centrifugal force to dry drilled solids in oil or synthetic base fluids. It provides G-Force up to 400 and extracts liquid from cuttings.

K.4. Waste Management Procedures

The safe and environmentally sensitive treatment and disposal of waste water and cuttings contaminated with drilling fluid originating from the drilling activity.

The purpose is to provide a standard operating procedure to instruct/guide DWM personnel in the correct methods used in cutting by fixation process.

K.4.1. Waste Water Treatment, Handling and Disposal

Method

Treating waste water and mud by the dewatering unit.

Waste water will be received from:

1. Pump cooling water

2. Dumping of pits

3. Dumping of traps

4. Drain lines

5. Rain

6. Rig wash water

Waste Water Treatment Requirements

RESPONSIBLE PERSONS EQUIPMENT REQUIREDSenior DWM engineerJunior DWM engineerDewatering UnitFilter PressStorage TankPumpsCoagulantFlocculants

Action required:

1- Supervisor/Senior Engineer to hold safety meeting with all involved personnel.

Conduct a toolbox meeting prior to all operations. Identify risk and apply all standard

NDCO safety procedures. Ensure full PPE is worn and the crews are aware of their

roles and responsibilities. Review previous safety bulletin cards to determine specific

risks/hazards associated with this task.

2- Equipment Check. Senior Engineer to inspect all equipment associated with the task

and determines operational suitability and ‘fit for purpose’ status including all above

and chemical inventories of coagulants and flocculants.

South Azadegan

APP-04 Drilling Program

Doc No.: NDCAZD-EN-WP-004-0 Waste Management Program Contract No.: MTN-94-854

August 2016 Page 161 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

3- Fill the suction tank with waste water or fluid from the waste pit and/or mud pits using

the diaphragm or submersible pumps. This tank acts like a buffer to provide steady

volume for the flocculation/coagulation process.

4- Use agitator or centrifugal pump for agitating the fluid in the tank to ensure

homogenous fluid for dewatering process and prevent settling of solids.

5- Test waste water specific gravity, pH and solids content.

6- If necessary adjust pH in the suction tank.

7- Check level of polymer in the mixing funnel, fill up if necessary.

8- Don’t run out of polymer and interrupt the dewatering process.

9- Check level of coagulant in the drum, prepare if necessary according to test results.

10- Check water supply.

11- Start filter press.

12- Start dewatering unit.

13- Start feed pump.

14- Start floc polymer pump and adjust polymer volume.

15- If necessary, start coagulant pumps and add coagulant fluid to improve flocculation.

16- Check floc result from the sample valve (trial and error procedure).

17- If the test results are good (fast settling, large floc’s, clear separation) feed the waste

water to filter press.

18- The effluent discharge should run first back to the waste water pit or return to the

suction tank until all adjustments are made and the effluent is clean.

19- Send clean effluent to the clear water pit/tank by using the T valve.

20- When finished, stop all pumps and filter press.

21- Clean dewatering unit after usage. Take care of polymer mixing parts.

22- For cuttings generated in the dewatering process follow with Standard Operating

Procedures.

23- Threated water send to tanks for using in mud made. Waste water from one of the

following method will be disinfection:

o Liming

o Aerated

o Soda ash

o Biocide

24- Discharged water after dewatering should meet below standards:

 pH = 7-9

 COD &amp;lt; 200 mg/lit, BOD &amp;lt; 300 mg/lit

 Ca2+ &amp;lt; 600 mg/lit

 Hardness &amp;lt; 800 mg/lit

 Turbidity &amp;lt; 1000 ntu

 Color (Color unit, chromaticity) &amp;lt;75

K.4.2. Cutting Fixation Treatment

Method

Solids mixing in the cutting treatment area with cement and Sodium Silicate.

Cutting Fixation Treatment Requirements

RESPONSIBLE PERSONS EQUIPMENT REQUIREDSenior DWM engineerJunior DWM engineerLoader driverLoaderCementSodium SilicateRetort test

Action required:

1- Senior engineer to hold safety meeting with all personnel involved. Conduct a toolbox

meeting prior to all operations. Identify risk and apply all standard NDCO safety

procedures. Ensure full PPE is worn and the crews are aware of their roles and

responsibilities. Review previous safety bulletin cards to determine specific

risks/hazards associated with this task.

2- Weekly inspection of loader. Inspection should include driver skills, breaks, reverse

alarm, lights, wheels, etc. Problems should be reported. The senior engineer is

responsible for the proper use and condition of the equipment!

3- Cuttings are received from the corral discharged on the treatment area into the

compartments made with treated cuttings.

4- Take a sample of the cutting to be treated and perform a retort test, record retort test

results in fixation table.

5- The batch quantity of cement and sodium silicate will be calculated by using the cement

curve and put into the bucket.

South Azadegan

APP-04 Drilling Program

Doc No.: NDCAZD-EN-WP-004-0 Waste Management Program Contract No.: MTN-94-854

August 2016 Page 163 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

6- The bucket will be poured into on the cuttings and mixed until consistent (about 30

min). This mixing time allows the cuttings to activate with the sodium silicate and

cement for sufficient time to achieve initial Fixation.

7- An initial sheen test will be conducted after 4 hours curing.

8- If initial sheen test fail, additional cement and sodium silicate will be added and mixed

for another 15 minutes, the process is continued until the material passes the sheen test

and the batch is deposited for curing.

9- The mixture will be allowed to set for 8 hours more (from the end of the initial sheen

test). This time allows the cuttings to further activate with the sodium silicate and

cement for sufficient time to achieve secondary Fixation. A second step sheen test will

be conducted at 12 hours (from the end of the initial mixing time).

10- If second sheen test fail, the batch will be reprocessed with more cement and sodium

silicate for another 15 minutes, the process is continued until the material passes the

sheen test and the batch is deposited for curing.

11- At this point a Can test will be done on the batch. A Can test is a simple field test that

can provide an indication of free liquid. Results are recorded on the fixation table.

12- If can test pass the batch will be moved to a designated area for permanent residence.

This could be a liner pit or it could be an area where the material could be laid down,

smoothed and allowed to set for future use.

13- If can test fail an absorbent material or additional cement and sodium silicate need to

be used and mixed for another 15 minutes, the process is continued until the material

passes the can test and the batch is deposited for curing.

14- A third and final sheen test will be conducted 48 hours (from the time of the initial

mixing) to ensure that the process results have been achieved.

15- If third and final sheen test pass, the mixture will be continue to cure in the designated

area and time and pass note will be marked on the process sheet.

16- It is unlikely that the batch will fail the 48 hour test, however in the event that the sheen

test fails, the material will be returned to the mixing corral, broken up and will be added

to new batches of cuttings and re-cycled.

L.1. General Quality, Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

Company is committed to conducting operations in a manner which minimizes the risks to the health and safety of those involved in, and affected by, such operations. Company is also committed to conducting its operations in a manner which minimizes the impact on natural and ‘built’ environments in the area of operations.

This section sets out minimum Quality, Health, Safety and Environmental (QHSE) requirements for the Work that Contractor and subcontractors will be required to comply with whilst conducting operations for Company.

Company may perform audits and assessments of Contractor’s and its subcontractors’ performance under the Contract. Company reserves the right without prior notice to conduct quality, health, safety, security and environmental audits of the Operations.

Contractor shall at all times be responsible for performing the WORK in a manner so as to protect against loss of life, injury to people, damage to property and the environment. The detailed manner means and methods of performing the WORK shall be under the control and direction of Contractor.

Prior to the start of Operations, certain QHSE processes must be completed. These QHSE processes include developing the final QHSE plan format and frequency of any QHSE audits, permitting and licensing and Company’s approvals. Contractor shall ensure that sufficient resources are dedicated to this task to ensure completion prior to mobilization.

Company may at any time stop the WORK or any portion of the WORK without penalty to Company if the WORK is not conducted in accordance with the Quality, Health, Safety or Environmental guidelines specified in this Contract. Company reserves the right to require Contractor to remove any person from the Operations in the case of non- compliance with QHSE procedures. Company may also prohibit the use of equipment and plant in cases where that equipment or plant does not meet the required standards or is deemed unsafe.

Contractor shall ensure that activities associated with this Contract are conducted in compliance with applicable national and local HSE laws and regulations, Contractor’s standards and Company’s requirements and IADC documents.

South Azadegan

APP-04 Drilling Program

Doc No.: NDCAZD-EN-WP-004-0 Health, Safety and Environment Contract No.: MTN-94-854

August 2016 Page 172 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

Company’s Representative(s) do not have the authority to relax health, safety or environment standards. If they judge the Operation to be inadequate with regards to any aspect of quality, health, safety, security or the environment, then the operation may be immediately suspended.

Contractor shall be required to develop a project-specific QHSE plan to manage the WORK and associated risks. This plan shall, as a minimum, address topics included in the list detailed in Item 7. Where existing Contractor QHSE publications detail the topics listed, it is sufficient to either include them verbatim, or provide reference to where they may be found in Contractor’s Quality and HSE Manuals. The final project- specific QHSE plan shall satisfy Contractor standards, Company requirements and applicable HSE laws and regulations.

Contractor should establish an effective HSE system and implement it strictly.

Contractor must adhere to the standards and regulations of Health, Safe and Environment constituted by the local government.

Contractor must strictly adhere to the procedures / standards and regulations of Health, Safety and Environment promulgated by NIOC.

Contractor should comply with all applicable local government regulations including guidelines and recommended practices and any other Iranian authorities having jurisdiction.

All personnel should respect the local culture, traditions and social values of the indigenous population of the Iran and South Azadegan region.

Contractor shall hire qualified and experienced worker and familiar his personnel with hazards especially with H2S and Mine and UXO (unexploded ordinance) according to related procedure.

Contractor shall conduct proper training about UXO (unexploded ordinance) and mine awareness to all personnel.

L.2. Health &amp;amp; Safety Management

Contractor shall take all necessary safety measures in relation to the WORK to be provided and shall conduct itself and its work force in such a way as to comply at all times with the provisions of the national and local health and safety regulations pertinent to the contracted Scope of WORK. Contractor shall also comply with all and any of Company’s safety

standards and requirements as particularly applicable to the Operating Area and/or as may be imposed by Company from time to time.

Contractor and its subcontractors shall take all necessary steps to provide a safe and healthy working environment for employees, Company’s personnel and third parties in the performance of the WORK.

Contractor shall operate a management system that ensures:

 Contractor’s and sub contractors’ personnel operate safe systems of work at all

times for the performance of the WORK.

 Hazards associated with the work are identified and appropriate actions are taken

to prevent accidents.

 Risks to safety and health of personnel involved in the WORK are identified and

assessed, and any actions and measurements are implemented to either eliminate

or reduce these risks to a level that is considered as low as reasonably practicable,

given the nature of the WORK.

 Personnel are aware of the identified hazards and risks to their safety and health

and to the safety and health of others.

 The detailed safe working procedures established by Contractor to ensure that

the WORK will be conducted with due regard to the QHSE aspects, shall be

detailed or referenced in the QHSE plan. Copies of the source documents shall

be provided to Company if the procedures are referenced only.

L.2.1. QHSE Representative

Contractor shall provide a dedicated, on-crew QHSE Representative. The primary responsibility of the QHSE Representative shall include, but not be limited to, the maintenance and monitoring of the implementation of HSE guidelines and procedures and where required provide HSE awareness training for the crew. Such activities shall be approved and actively supported by Contractor at corporate management level.

L.2.2. Training and Competence

Contractor shall ensure that its employees and those of its subcontractors are trained and competent to perform the WORK in a safe and environmentally responsible manner. Such training and demonstration of competence will include but not be limited to vocational, safety, emergency, environmental and other training required by regulatory agencies and IADC/OGP guidelines. Contractor’s senior staff shall have received training in safety management.

L.2.3. Accident/Incident Reporting

Contractor shall report all incidents. Any hazardous incident / near miss involving Company, Contractor’s, or any third party personnel, plant or equipment, shall be reported to Company, whether or not injury to personnel or damage/loss to plant or equipment resulted. The following incidents shall be verbally reported immediately to the on-site Company Representative(s): damage to property or equipment belonging to Company, third parties, Contractor or its subcontractors; injury to personnel of Company, third parties, subcontractors or Contractor; near misses which may have had serious potential consequences; environmental damage; media attention. An initial written report, containing factual information only, shall be prepared by Contractor and delivered to the Company Representative within forty- eight (48) hours of the incident. Company reserves the right to participate in the investigation of any incident arising out of performance of the WORK.

Contractor and all subcontractors shall have an accident and incident reporting system, details of which shall be included in the QHSE plan.

Contractor shall maintain and forward to Company, a monthly summary of its safety performance.

All Contractor and subcontractor personnel and Company Representative shall attend safety meetings on a regular basis. Company Representative shall be given a copy of the minutes of the meetings.

L.2.4. Safety Equipment &amp;amp; Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements

Contractor shall ensure that appropriate PPE compliant to national standards is supplied to Contractor’s personnel involved in the WORK. Company intends to use water-based mud and

Contractor shall be solely liable for all costs in equipping its own and all other personnel on contract to, or under the control of, Contractor with the required safety equipment. Contractor will provide to all Contractor’s Personnel appropriate PPE throughout the WORK. Any defective PPE will be replaced without delay. Personnel without the correct PPE will not be allowed to continue work, until replacement PPE has been issued.

Contractor shall detail in the QHSE plan the PPE proposed for issue to the crew. This proposal should include the arrangements for replacement (due to wear and tear and damage) of this equipment.

L.2.5. Health

This well is committed to develop for oil in a responsible manner that promotes employees' and local inhabitants' health.

A trained Paramedic and proper MEDIVAC equipment and ambulance shall be stationed on the drilling rig during the drilling campaign.

Contractor shall, as a minimum, conduct the WORK and provide personnel, equipment, facilities and services consistent with good oil field practices and OGP Guidelines. An assessment of the Contract Area with regard to “Environmental and Occupational Health Risks” and “Local Medical Support” shall be provided by Contractor in the QHSE plan. This assessment and the resulting “Health Risk Assessment Score” will be discussed with Company, and a final assessment will be agreed.

To ensure the fitness of those personnel engaged to undertake the WORK, Contractor shall conduct periodic medical examinations of its staff and ensure that its subcontractors’ personnel are also subject to periodic medical examination. As a minimum this shall include pre-hire medical examinations of temporary local personnel and bi-annual medical examinations of its permanent and expatriate staff. Evidence should be made available to Company to verify an appropriate program of immunizations consistent with the recommendations of the World Health Organization for the area of operations.

L.2.6. Drug Abuse and Control

Contractor warrants that it shall obtain valid written consent of all Personnel to a search of property of such Personnel when Company suspects that such Personnel have in their possession drugs and/or other prohibited substances or any other item likely to prejudice safety or security. Company will provide a representative to attend the search.

Contractor warrants that it shall obtain valid written consent of all Personnel to medical testing for the presence of drugs or other prohibited substances.

Contractor further agrees that it shall immediately notify Company in the event that Contractor becomes aware that any of its Personnel has been found in possession of drugs and/or any other prohibited substance.

Contractor is required to notify Company in the event that any Personnel provided for the WORK have previously been found in possession, or have abused drugs and/or other substances prohibited at Location. The acceptance of such Personnel for the WORK shall be at the sole discretion of Company.

L.2.7. Camp Standards

Contractor shall abide by all statutory Iranian governmental health and safety regulations, and maintain acceptable standards for cleanliness and hygiene for quarters, camps and the Operating Area(s) in general.

Contractor shall detail the standards and facilities proposed for its camp in the QHSE plan.

L.2.8. Emergency Preparedness

Contractor and its subcontractors shall have emergency preparedness and response plans plus procedures available at all times throughout the duration of the Contract.

Contractor shall take all necessary measures to ensure that:

 Potential emergency situations have been identified and assessed;
