L.3. Environmental Management

Contractor shall comply with any and all laws, rules and regulations of governmental agencies having jurisdiction, which now exist or may be promulgated during the term of the Contract, relating to the control and prevention of damage to the environment.

Without prejudice to Item 3.1 above, Contractor shall ensure that all personnel use the highest prevailing standards of care and diligence to prevent unlawful disposal of all waste oil, water and other waste materials or fluids which may accumulate or be caused by Contractor’s performance of the Contract. Contractor shall not dispose of any objects, scrap, waste, rubbish, equipment, fluids or fuel into the surrounding area or allow anything to be stored loose where it can be driven into surrounding areas by wind. Contractor shall take all reasonable precautions to prevent pollution of any nature or kind from its performance of the WORK. Contractor shall have contingency plans and procedures in place for such events.

In the event of any disposal prohibited by Item 3.2 above, whether by dumping, spilling, emission or otherwise arising from Contractor’s performance or non-performance of the Contract, Contractor shall be fully liable for and bear the costs of removal of any such item(s) dumped, spilled, emitted or otherwise disposed regardless of the sole, concurrent or contributory negligence or breach of duty (statutory or otherwise) of Company. In the event of any such disposal, Contractor shall immediately undertake all reasonable remedial and protective measures required in such circumstances.

Contractor shall notify Company immediately with respect to any pollution, loss, damage, claim or demand (or occurrence which may give rise to same) resulting from the Contract. Contractor shall report to Company any incidents of non-compliance with legislative and regulatory environmental requirements that occur during the performance of the WORK.

Without relieving Contractor of any of its obligations under Item 3.2, if Contractor does not promptly proceed to perform its obligations under this Item 3, Company may take part to any degree it deems necessary in the control and removal of any pollution, dumping, spillage or contamination which is the responsibility of Contractor under this Item 3.2, or which is due to any act or omission of Contractor. Contractor shall reimburse Company for costs arising from such actions of Company upon receipt of invoice from Company. Company shall have

L.3.1. Requirement on location

 The access road and well location construction shall be accorded with construction

program of well location. It minimizes any impacts on the local residents, prevent all

soil contamination, prevent all ground water contamination, and prevent all surface

water contamination. Cutting and waste water pit shall be lining and drainage system

shall be good and to avoid farm and season canal contamination.

 Management regulation for transportation truck, drilling operation machine and tools

shall be carried out strictly to avoid damage farm and trees, etc.

 Well site shall be flat and clean. All the equipment, materials, drilling tools shall be

put in order.

 Control the rig noise to decrease the influence to surroundings while drilling at the

inhabitation area.

 Contractor shall perform on site segregation of wastes prior to transfer to the transfer

area and/or delivery to the transportation Contractor in accordance with the following

waste hazard classification.

L.3.2. Non-Hazardous Wastes (Re-usable, Recyclable and Recoverable Wastes)

 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals, plastics, and wood wastes, PETs and potentially paper

and glass.

 Materials shall be separately segregated and provision may be made for size reduction

and containerization equipment.

 BOP stack is equipped according to drilling design

L.3.6. Management of environment protection on location

 In drilling operation， keep mud and sewage from overflowing. If it happens, clean up

timely.

 Mud chemicals shall be stored according to the standard and shall not be scattered

around well site. If mud chemicals scatter while loading or unloading, clean it up at

once. The sack of mud chemicals shall be recovered. Do not dispose it on site.

 Enhance water management at well location and do not wash equipment with fresh

water. Stop water flowing for long time. Overhead tanks shall be utilized.

 Oil management shall be carefully at the well site. No oil dirt on site, no dripping and

leaking at oil tank and manifold system area.

 After the well is completed, reinforce the sewage pit ， solidify the disposed mud and

have environment procedure fulfilled.

 Install fuel supply lines and keep them in good condition.

 All the drilling fluid materials shall be recovered and shall not be left at the well site

after completion.

 The environmental protection personnel from contractor and operator side shall check

and accept the well site environment according to the regulation after completion. Only

well site environment is qualified, the well can be delivered.

 Transition Area for Hazardous Waste shall also be provided by each Contractor in his

allocated area,

 Company shall approve each area before use as well. The transition area of hazardous

waste shall be:

 Paved, fenced, marked and illuminated

 Equipped with appropriate Fire Extinguisher and other emergency response

equipment (e.g. Eye-Wash and Emergency Shower, appropriate First Aid kits,

neutralizer substances etc.).

 In compliance with the requirements of handling, transportation and storage of

generated during the work.

L.8. Well Control

Recording Reference

All BOP tests, drills, function tests, any malfunctions, repair or maintenance to the mud system and well control equipment shall be recorded in the IADC daily reports and shall be signed by both the Drilling Contractor's Tool Pusher and Drilling Supervisor on the well site. They shall also be recorded in the Daily Drilling Report.

Flow Check Procedure

To avoid a kick situation, it is recommended that a flow check be conducted at specific times during the drilling operation.

 While drilling(any warning sign)

 Prior to tripping the drill string

 While tripping(any warning sign)

 While out of hole(continuously)

 Trip out:

o After pulling 5% of the drill pipe

o At the midpoint depth of the wellbore

o Prior to pulling the first stand of drill collars

South Azadegan

APP-04 Drilling Program

Doc No.: NDCAZD-EN-WP-004-0 Health, Safety and Environment Contract No.: MTN-94-854

August 2016 Page 191 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

o After all the drill string is out of hole.

 Trip in:

o Upon reaching surface casing shoe

o At midpoint of the wellbore

Primary Control Reference

It is the responsibility of the Drilling Contractor to keep the hole full at all times by using all the available equipment. The Drilling Supervisor shall monitor that the correct preventive practices are being implemented and/or conducted at all times.

Extreme care shall be taken to monitor mud volume, drilling breaks and gas cut mud. The MACP (Maximum allowable casing pressure) shall be confirmed by the Drilling Supervisor, either after setting each new casing string or, whenever the density of the drilling mud changes.

The MACP shall be clearly written on a kick control sheet that will be posted near the choke control panel.

The predetermined distance at which the Tool Joint is to be pulled above the rotary should be posted on rig floor near the BOP control panel.

The Driller is responsible for carefully measuring and recording the slow pump pressure.

Awareness of these values is an important element in killing operations, in order to avoid formation breakdown.

Take a measure and record the slow pump pressure at three different flow rates with all pumps at the following times:

 Once per tour.

 Whenever changes occur in the mud density/rheology.

 Whenever changes occur in the dimension and characteristics of the string, BHA, jet

size, jet plugged or jet lost, etc.

Secondary Control Reference

Any time a drilling break is noticed, drilling shall stop and a static monitoring of the well shall be carried out. Space-out for all Pipe Rams and Annular Preventer must be known to the Driller at all times to keep tool joints clear of annular preventer and rams.

Kick Detection Procedure While Drilling

If there is an indication of a possible kick occurring, the Driller shall follow the kick detection procedures outlined below:

Stop drilling with the pump on, Pick up top drive to a predetermined space-out position, Shut off the pumps and check for well flow by visual examination on the bell nipple or flow line.

If the well is not flowing:

 Immediately notify the rig manager, Drilling Supervisor and Toolpusher.

 The Drilling Supervisor will decide whether to circulate bottoms up or resume drilling.

The penetration rate will be limited as long as the cause of the abnormal situation is

undetermined. Always be aware that some hydrocarbons (gas or oil cut mud) may rise

to the surface. Ensure that the proper monitoring and safety systems all in place.

If the well is flowing:

 Close the well as per the Shut-in Procedure.

 Immediately notify the Well site Drilling Supervisor, rig manager and Toolpusher.

M.1. Introduction

This document has been developed in line with concerns regarding Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) operations customized for operations being on the APP-04.

In General Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is an extremely hazardous, toxic compound. It is a colorless, flammable gas that can be identified in relatively low concentrations, by a characteristic rotten egg odor. The gas occurs naturally in coal pits, sulfur springs, gas wells, and as a product of decaying sulfur-containing organic matter, particularly under low oxygen conditions. Industrial sources of hydrogen sulfide include petroleum and natural gas extraction and refining, pulp and paper manufacturing, rayon textile production, leather tanning, chemical manufacturing and waste disposal.

Formation gas from Asmari, Sarvak, and Dariyan containing harmful hydrogen sulfide (H2S) has the risks to harm site personnel during the operation. From analysis the H2S content in Sarvak formation is 2436 ppm. All site personnel should pay more attention on H2S hazards and all H2S equipment should be in good condition.

M.2. Scope &amp;amp; Purpose

Identifying, classifying, and responding to different levels of H2S hazard, H2S safety training, drills in South Azadegan Project Well No. APP-04.

M.3. General Characteristics of Hydrogen Sulfide

Chemical Symbol H2SSpecific Gravity 1.192 (Heavier Than Air)Explosive Limits Lower Limit: 4% - Upper Limit: 44% , Volume in airIgnition Temperature 260o CSolubility in Water 2.9 Volumes of gas per volume of water at 20o C

August 2016 Page 196 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

Hydrogen sulfide has a very low odor threshold, with its smell being easily perceptible at concentrations well below 1 part per million (ppm) in air. The odor increases as the gas becomes more concentrated, with the strong rotten egg smell recognizable up to 30 ppm. Above this level, the gas is reported to have a sickeningly sweet odor up to around 100 ppm. However, at concentrations above 100 ppm, a person's ability to detect the gas is affected by rapid temporary paralysis of the olfactory nerves in the nose, leading to a loss of the sense of smell. This means that the gas can be present at dangerously high concentrations, with no perceivable odor. Prolonged exposure to lower concentrations can also result in similar effects of olfactory fatigue. This unusual property of hydrogen sulfide makes it extremely dangerous to rely totally on the sense of smell to warn of the presence of the gas.

Altered respiration, pain in the eyes and drowsiness after 15-30 minutes followed by throat irritation after 1 hour. Several hours’ exposure results in gradual increase in severity of these symptoms and death may occur within the next 48 hours.200-300 ppm Marked conjunctivitis and respiratory tract irritation after 1 hour of exposure500-700 ppm Loss of consciousness and possibly death in 30 minutes to 1 hour.700-1000 ppm Rapid unconsciousness, cessation of respiration and death.1000-2000 ppmUnconsciousness at once, with early cessation of respiration and death in a few minutes. Death may occur even if individual is removed to fresh air at once.

Hydrogen Sulfide is a naturally occurring gas mixed with natural gas or dissolved in the oil or brine and released upon exposure to atmospheric conditions.

M.7. HSE and H2S

This information sheet provides guidance for duty-holders on detecting and managing hydrogen sulfide (H2S) hazards in hydrocarbon processing systems. As reservoirs begin to water out, hydrogen sulfide can become an issue when processing returning fluids. The gas is toxic in relatively low concentrations and the risks to the workforce need to be addressed as soon as its‟ presence becomes known. It is not intended to provide detailed advice on workplace exposure limits.

Hydrogen sulfide is considered a broad-spectrum poison, meaning that it can poison several different systems in the body, although the nervous system and respiratory systems are most affected. Besides being highly toxic H2S is a flammable gas. It is heavier than air and hence tends to accumulate in low-lying areas. It is pungent but rapidly destroys the sense of smell.

H2S is toxic at breathable concentrations between 500-1000ppm, but death is not instantaneous. However, at concentrations of greater than 1000ppm, H2S is rapidly lethal. Industry practice is to recognize that fatality from H2S exposure can occur over a wide concentration band but at around 500–1000ppm exposure for a short period, the fatal exposure levels would be significant.

800 ppm is the generally accepted lethal concentration for 50% of an exposed human population for 5 minutes exposure (LC50).

Some further details on concentrations and effects are given below:

 0.0047 ppm is the recognition threshold of human smell, the concentration at which

50% of humans can detect the characteristic odor of hydrogen sulfide.

South Azadegan

APP-04 Drilling Program

Doc No.: NDCAZD-EN-WP-004-0 H2S Monitoring &amp;amp; Control Contract No.: MTN-94-854

August 2016 Page 201 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

 10-20 ppm is the borderline concentration for eye irritation.

 50-100 ppm leads to eye damage.

 At 150-250 ppm the olfactory nerve is paralyzed after a few inhalations, and the sense

of smell disappears, often together with awareness of danger.

 320-530 ppm leads to pulmonary edema with the possibility of death.

 530-1000 ppm causes strong stimulation of the central nervous system and rapid

breathing, leading to loss of breathing.

 Concentrations over 1000 ppm cause immediate collapse with loss of breathing, even

after inhalation of a single breath.

HSE sets limits for the control of hazardous substances in air. They are known as workplace exposure limits (WELs) and are set to help protect the health of workers who may be exposed to such substances. These limits are concentrations of hazardous substances in the air, averaged over a specific period referred to as a time-weighted average (TWA). Two time periods are used: long-term (8 hours) and short-term (15 minutes). Short-term exposure limits (STEL) are set to help prevent acute effects such as eye irritation, which may occur following exposure for a few minutes. HSE does not set limits or publish information on concentrations of gasses that are immediately dangerous to life or health (IDLH). However, the National Institute of Safety and Health (NIOSH) in the USA has set IDLH figures for a number of substances, which may be used by duty-holders.

M.8. Standards and guidance

ISO 10418 covers industry practice for handling H2S and is based on the accepted criterion that significant fatalities would occur from exposure to H2S in gas at concentrations of 500-1000ppm. Detection guidance is based on the argument that the hydrocarbon gas detection system will provide adequate detection if the H2S is below 500ppm in the hydrocarbon (HC) process streams. This is an acceptable argument only if it can be demonstrated that the HC detection system is ~100% effective. Above 500ppm specific H2S detection is required.

Hydrogen sulfide has a WEL of 5 ppm 8-hour TWA based on data indicating a shift towards anaerobic respiration at exposures to 10 ppm.

August 2016 Page 202 of 221 Drilling Engineering Department

NIOSH has set a concentration of 100 ppm as IDLH.

Use of hydrocarbon detection systems for H2S monitoring need to take account of this “detection effectiveness”.

M.9. Hazard identification and management

Production of liquid and gaseous hydrocarbons containing hydrogen sulfide in significant amounts can be hazardous to people. H2S in hydrocarbon fluids has the potential to form sulfur dioxide (SO2) via combustion. Flaring hydrocarbon gas containing measurable quantities of H2S needs to be managed to ensure the SO2 produced does not present a toxic hazard. Combinations of H2S, SO2 and hydrocarbon gaseous mixtures also need to be considered in terms of their accumulated toxic load.

H2S presence in reservoir streams tends to increase with time and it is important therefore that duty-holders ensure that if the concentration levels in modules begin to increase the toxicity status of the areas are revised accordingly. The recommended strategy for fixed and portable detection is based on accepted management practice for confined space entry, and normally accessible process modules.

M.10. Training Program

All personnel working in an area where concentrations of Hydrogen Sulfide may exceed the 10 Parts per Million (PPM) should be provided with training before beginning work assignments.

All operators and contract personnel must complete site specific H2S Induction Training Program conducted by qualified H2S Engineer.
